Treibe eine UNENDLICHE Coroutine (eine o: Never drive an ENDLESS coroutine (one with no natural end) with FOR EACH — that runs for ever. Steer it by hand with CORO_RESUME instead and break off yourself once you have enough values. Tip: in a manual RESUME loop the very last (finishing) call delivers the RETURN value or NIL — so for plain collecting, FOR EACH is the safer choice.
YIELD ist keine Einbahnstraße. YIELD ist: YIELD is not a one-way street. YIELD is itself an expression: you can assign its result to a variable. With CORO_SEND you not only carry the coroutine on but push a value into it as you do — and that value becomes the result of the YIELD at which it is currently paused. A genuine dialogue between your code and the coroutine arises that way.
Setzt die Coroutine fort wie CORO_RESUME: Carries the coroutine on like CORO_RESUME, but the YIELD expression at which it is paused delivers the value passed in. (At the very first start there is no waiting YIELD yet — use CORO_RESUME there.)
x bekommt den hineingegebenen Wert: x receives the value passed in
Coroutinen sind ein Spezialwerkzeug – fü: Coroutines are a specialist tool — for many programs you will never need them. Where they do fit, though, they simplify the code enormously, because the coroutine keeps track of its own progress instead of your having to carry it laboriously in variables:
Zwischensequenzen / Dialoge: ein Schritt: Cutscenes and dialogue: one step per YIELD, the rest waits.
Gegner- oder Boss-Muster: „fahre links,: Enemy or boss patterns: “move left, wait, fire three times, from the top.”
Generatoren: erzeuge eine (auch endlose): Generators: produce a sequence of values on demand — an endless one, if you like.
Eine pausierte Coroutine, die du nicht z: A paused coroutine that you do not let run to the end can be shut down cleanly with CORO_CLOSE(c). In short programs that is rarely necessary; with many long-lived coroutines it is good form.
Je größer ein Programm wird, desto unhan: The bigger a program grows, the more unwieldy a single enormous file becomes. With IMPORT you pull in code from outside — either one of Drachenhauch's many built-in libraries or a file of your own into which you have moved reusable code. That keeps your programs tidy and saves typing, because you do not keep rewriting what already works.
Eine IMPORT-Zeile schreibst du an den An: You write an IMPORT line at the start of your program. There are two sorts of module, and they differ in one small detail — remember that difference well.
Drachenhauch bringt eine große Sammlung: Drachenhauch ships a large collection of ready-made modules — for 2D vectors, JSON, databases, physics, pathfinding and much more (you will meet them all in Part V). You fetch such a module with IMPORT and the module name in quotation marks, WITHOUT a file extension. Afterwards the module's functions and types are at your disposal.
Macht ein eingebautes Modul nutzbar. Der: Makes a built-in module usable. The name goes in quotation marks with no extension. Afterwards you can use the module's functions and external types.
Du kannst deinen eigenen Code in eine se: You can move your own code into a separate .dh file and import it. That divides a large program into manageable pieces — all the maths helpers in mathe.dh, for instance. When importing a file of your own you give the file name WITH the .dh extension. Drachenhauch inserts the file's contents at that point, so you can use its functions and constants directly.
Angenommen, du hast neben deinem Program: Suppose you have a file mathe.dh next to your program with these contents:
Dann holst du sie so in dein Hauptprogra: Then you pull it into your main program like this and use its contents as though they stood there directly:
Fügt den Inhalt einer eigenen .dh-Datei: Inserts the contents of one of your own .dh files — given with its extension, relative to your program's directory. Afterwards its functions, SUBs, classes and constants are available.
Hier der feine, aber wichtige Unterschie: Here is the fine but important difference: you write a built-in module WITHOUT an extension (IMPORT "vec2") and a file of your own WITH one (IMPORT "mathe.dh"). The .dh extension tells Drachenhauch: “this is a file of mine, not a built-in module.”
Manche Module haben lange Funktionsnamen: Some modules have long function names. With the addition AS you give a module a shorter name prefix on import. The JSON functions, which normally begin with JSON_, then become J_ functions, say — which saves typing when you use the module often.
Importiert ein Modul und ersetzt sein Na: Imports a module and replaces its name prefix with the abbreviation given. JSON_PARSE thus becomes J_PARSE, for example.
Der Alias ersetzt das Präfix für alle Fu: The alias replaces the prefix for all the module's functions and types (J_PARSE, J_HANDLE …). It works for modules whose functions begin with the module name — that is, for the great majority.
Lagere zusammengehörige Bausteine in eig: Move related building blocks into files of their own: one for maths helpers, one for your player class, one for the enemies. Your main program then begins with a few IMPORT lines and stays readable. That way you find your bearings even in large projects — and can simply reuse a file that has proved itself in your next game.
Damit endet Teil II: Du beherrschst jetz: That brings Part II to a close: you now have the whole Drachenhauch language at your command — from variables through loops and functions to classes, coroutines and modules. The following parts cover the built-in commands in detail (Part III), graphics, sound and games (Part IV), and the modules that ship with it (Part V).
Mit Teil III beginnt der Nachschlage-Tei: Part III begins the reference half of the book. The chapters that follow present Drachenhauch's built-in commands arranged by topic — each with its signature, a short explanation and a small example. You need not read them at a stretch; use them as a lexicon when you are after a particular command.
Dieses erste Referenzkapitel sammelt die: This first reference chapter gathers the commands for the text console: printing with PRINT, reading with INPUT, formatting with FORMAT$. The console is plain text-based input and output — with no graphics window at all. (Keyboard and mouse in the game window are covered in Part IV.)
Gibt die Werte aus und beginnt eine neue: Outputs the values and starts a new line. Separate several values with a comma (space between) or a semicolon (no gap). A semicolon right at the end suppresses the line break, so that the next PRINT carries straight on. PRINT with no argument outputs a blank line.
Ausführlich erklärt im Kapitel „Ein- und: Explained at length in the chapter “Input and output” (Part II).
Liest eine Zeile von der Tastatur in die: Reads a line from the keyboard into the variable. The input is converted to the variable's type (number, text, truth value). A prompt text may stand in front. The variable must have been declared with DIM beforehand.
Formatiert einen Wert nach einer Format-: Formats a value according to a C-style format specification and returns a string. The placeholder begins with %. The most important: %d (whole number), %.Nf (decimal with N places), %0Nd (number padded with zeros to N digits), %x (hexadecimal), %s (string). Text around the placeholder is kept.
Innerhalb eines f-Strings kannst du dies: Inside an f-string you can use the same format specifications directly in the placeholder: f"FPS {wert:.1f}". That is usually the most convenient way to format — see the chapter “Input and output”.
Hinweis zur Konsole und zum Spielfenster: A note on the console and the game window
PRINT und INPUT arbeiten mit der Textkon: PRINT and INPUT work with the text console. As soon as you open a graphics window (with SCREEN, see Part IV), you draw text with TEXT at a position on screen instead, and you poll key presses with commands such as KEYPRESSED or the input module — not with INPUT. For console programs (pure logic, small helpers, learning examples) this chapter remains your toolkit.
WAITKEY hält das Programm an, bis eine T: WAITKEY halts the program until a key is pressed — the classic ending (“press any key to continue”). INKEY$ gives the character last typed OR an empty text if nothing is pending; so it does NOT wait.
Zahl- und Textumwandlung für die Ausgabe: Number and text conversion for output (STR$, VAL, CHR$ …) is in the chapter “Type conversion and checking” and under “String functions”. Graphical text, keyboard and mouse come in Part IV (“Graphics, sound and games”).
Drachenhauch bringt eine vollständige Ma: Drachenhauch ships a complete mathematics library — from simple functions such as absolute value and square root through to trigonometry and practical game helpers. Every function presented here is available directly, with no IMPORT. Angles are given in radians, as is usual in mathematics — DEG and RAD convert to and from degrees.
ABS liefert den Betrag (das Vorzeichen f: ABS gives the absolute value (the sign falls away), SQR the square root (x ≥ 0), POW the power (b to the e), HYPOT the length of the hypotenuse — the square root of x²+y², without overflow. (SQRT is an accepted second name for SQR.)
EXP ist e hoch x, LOG der Logarithmus (o: EXP is e to the x, LOG the logarithm (with no base: the natural logarithm to base e; with a second argument, to any base). LOG10 exists as a short form for the base-ten logarithm.
FLOOR rundet ab (zur nächstkleineren gan: FLOOR rounds down (to the next lower whole number), CEIL up, ROUND to the nearest whole number in the commercial manner. With a second argument, ROUND rounds to that many decimal places.
Liefern den kleinsten bzw. größten der ü: Give the smallest and the largest of the values passed in. You may supply as many as you like.
CLAMP zwängt einen Wert in den Bereich v: CLAMP forces a value into the range lo to hi (anything smaller becomes lo, anything larger hi). SIGN gives the sign: -1 for negative numbers, 0 for zero, +1 for positive. (CLAMP01(v) is short for CLAMP(v, 0, 1).)
Diese Funktionen sind das Rückgrat viele: These functions are the backbone of many animations and movements — letting a value travel smoothly from A to B, say, or carrying a measurement across into a different range.
LERP („lineare Interpolation“) liefert d: LERP (“linear interpolation”) gives the value lying at fraction t between a and b: t=0 gives a, t=1 gives b, t=0.5 the middle. REMAP carries a value from one range linearly into another.
Die Winkelfunktionen erwarten den Winkel: The trigonometric functions expect the angle in radians. ATAN2(y, x) does the reverse, giving the angle (in radians) to the point (x, y) — ideal for working out the direction from one point to another. (Also present: ASIN, ACOS, ATAN.)
Rechnen zwischen den Winkeleinheiten um:: Convert between the angle units: DEG turns radians into degrees, RAD degrees into radians. Handy, because one often thinks of angles in degrees while the functions want radians.
WRAP faltet einen Wert zyklisch in den B: WRAP folds a value cyclically into the range [lo, hi) — good for angles or indices that come round again (370° becomes 10°). PINGPONG swings back and forth in the range [0, länge] (a triangle wave, good for to-and-fro movement). MOVETOWARD nudges the current value at most maxd towards the target, without overshooting.
Zwei Kreiszahl-Konstanten stehen bereit:: Two circle constants are available: PI (3.14159…) and TAU (= 2·PI, the full circle in radians). There is deliberately NO constant E, because e is a popular name for the error variable in CATCH — use EXP(1) instead.
SGN liefert das Vorzeichen als -1, 0 ode: SGN gives the sign as -1, 0 or +1 — handy for extracting a direction from a velocity. FRAC returns the fractional part (FRAC(3.75) = 0.75).
Prüft, ob zwei Kommazahlen NAHEZU gleich: Checks whether two decimal numbers are NEARLY equal. With decimals that is almost always the right question: 0.1 + 0.2 does not internally come out as exactly 0.3, so a comparison with = fails. Without epsilon, a small default tolerance is used.
Dreidimensionales, geschichtetes Rausche: Three-dimensional, layered noise (fractal Brownian motion): several noise layers on top of one another give more natural-looking structures than a single one. Using the third axis as time gives you noise that changes slowly — drifting clouds, for instance.
Für Zufallszahlen gibt es ein eigenes Ka: Random numbers have a chapter of their own (“Randomness”). For smooth, coherent “noise” — for generating terrain or clouds, say — NOISE, NOISE2, NOISE3 and FBM are available; more on those under the game helpers in Part IV.
Zufall macht Spiele lebendig: Würfel, zu: Randomness brings games to life: dice, random enemy positions, shuffled cards, varied loot. Drachenhauch offers several functions for it — from the simple random number to weighted drawing from a list. Because the values naturally differ on every call, most examples here show no fixed output but describe the possible range instead.
Ohne Argument liefert RND eine Kommazahl: With no argument, RND gives a decimal number in the range 0 (included) to 1 (excluded). With one argument n, RND gives a whole number from 0 to n-1 — an ideal building block, for a die for instance.
RANDINT liefert eine ganze Zufallszahl v: RANDINT gives a random whole number from lo to hi — both bounds included (unlike RND(n)). RANDF gives a decimal from lo (included) to hi (excluded). RANDINT(1, 6) usually reads more pleasantly than RND(6) + 1.
Liefert ein zufällig gewähltes Element e: Gives a randomly chosen element of a one-dimensional array — each with equal probability.
Zieht ein Element aus werte, aber nicht: Draws an element from werte, but not with equal probability: the higher the corresponding weight, the likelier it is. werte and gewichte are two one-dimensional arrays of the same length. The classic tool for loot tables (“rare, occasional, common”).
Mischt ein 1D-Array zufällig durch – dir: Shuffles a one-dimensional array at random — on the spot (the array itself is changed, no copy is made). Perfect for shuffling a deck of cards.
Hinter den Zufallszahlen steckt ein bere: Behind the random numbers is a computed stream of values that depends on a starting value — the seed. Set a fixed seed with RANDOMIZE and the SAME sequence comes out every time afterwards. That sounds unrandom, but it is very useful: for testing (every run is the same) or for reproducible levels (“world no. 42” looks identical for every player).
Setzt den Startwert des Zufalls. Mit ein: Sets the starting value of the randomness. With a fixed number the random sequence becomes reproducible; with no argument Drachenhauch takes an unpredictable system seed (the normal case for genuine randomness).
Mit RANDOMIZE(42) erhältst du genau dies: With RANDOMIZE(42) you get exactly this sequence (2, then 5) — the same for you as here. Leave the RANDOMIZE out, or call it with no argument, and the sequence differs on every run.
Für echten Zufall im fertigen Spiel brau: For genuine randomness in a finished game you usually do not need RANDOMIZE at all — with no seed, every round differs. Reach for a fixed seed deliberately: when testing, for random levels that can be rebuilt, or when a bug appears only with certain random values and you want to reproduce it reliably.

NUMFMT$ abbreviates large numbers readably (K, M, T …) — exactly what building and idle games need constantly. The number of decimal places is selectable, two by default; small numbers get no abbreviation but the same number of decimal places.
Zum Umwandeln zwischen Text und Zahl (ST: For converting between text and number (STR$, VAL, CHR$, ASC), see the chapter “Type conversion and checking”. To assemble text from values comfortably, use f-strings (chapter “Input and output”).
Werte haben Typen – Zahl, Text, Wahrheit: Values have types — number, text, truth value. Often you have to convert between them: a number into text for printing, typed text back into a number for calculating. This chapter gathers the conversion functions, together with the commands for checking a value's type at run time.
STR$ macht aus einem beliebigen Wert sei: STR$ turns any value into its text (3.14 becomes "3.14", TRUE becomes "TRUE"). VAL does the reverse, reading a number out of a string — with a point you get a decimal, otherwise a whole number; unreadable text quietly becomes 0. TRYVAL does the same but gives your fallback value instead of 0 on invalid input.
Wandelt eine Kommazahl in eine ganze Zah: Turns a decimal into a whole number by rounding down (towards minus infinity): INT(3.7) is 3, INT(-1.5) is -2.
Wandelt eine ganze Zahl (oder Kommazahl): Turns a whole number (or a decimal) into a decimal (FLOAT) — the counterpart to INT. Handy when an INTEGER variable is needed as a FLOAT for a calculation, to force an uneven division for instance.
CHR$ macht aus einer Zeichen-Nummer (Uni: CHR$ turns a character number (Unicode code point) into the character, ASC turns the first character into its number. A is 65, B is 66 …
Stellen eine ganze Zahl als Text im Hexa: Represent a whole number as text in hexadecimal (base 16) or binary (base 2) — useful for colours (HEX$) or bit masks (BIN$).
Liefert den Typnamen eines Werts als Tex: Gives a value's type name as text at run time — "INTEGER", "FLOAT", "STRING", "BOOLEAN", say, or the name of a class or module type.
Fragt zur Laufzeit, ob ein Wert von eine: Asks at run time whether a value is of a given type, and returns TRUE or FALSE. What stands on the right is a TYPE NAME, not a variable: a class, a value type such as INTEGER, a module type such as VEC2, or NIL, ARRAY, MAP. For classes the whole inheritance chain counts: a Hund IS a Tier as well. An unknown name is an error at check time - otherwise a typo would quietly stay FALSE forever.
Prüfen den Typ und liefern TRUE oder FAL: Check the type and give TRUE or FALSE. Important: a truth value does NOT count as a number — ISNUM(TRUE) is FALSE. And ISINT(3.0) is FALSE, because 3.0 is a decimal.
Eine Objekt-Variable, die zwar mit DIM a: An object variable that has been declared with DIM but not yet filled with NEW holds “nothing” — a special empty value called NIL. With IS_NIL you check whether a variable is in that state, before you reach into it by accident.
Liefert TRUE, wenn der Wert NIL ist (als: Gives TRUE when the value is NIL (“nothing yet”), otherwise FALSE. Typically used to check, before using an object, whether it has been created at all.
NIL kannst du auch direkt hinschreiben u: You can also write NIL out and compare against it: IF boss = NIL THEN … and IF boss <> NIL THEN … mean the same as IS_NIL. And with boss = NIL you empty an object variable again (to release a defeated enemy object, for instance).
Für Speicherstände und Datenaustausch gi: For saved games and exchanging data there are a few more helpers. Base64 packs arbitrary text into a compact, transportable form; checksums tell you whether data is unchanged.
Kodiert Text nach Base64 und wieder zurü: Encodes text to Base64 and back again. Handy for storing or sending arbitrary data as plain text.
Liefern eine Prüfsumme (CRC32) bzw. eine: Give a checksum (CRC32) or a stable 64-bit hash (HASH) of a string — useful for checking that saved games are intact, or for sorting values into buckets.
Das Zusammenbauen von Text aus Werten ge: Assembling text from values is most comfortable with f-strings (chapter “Input and output”); fixed decimal places or leading zeros come from FORMAT$ (chapter “Console and input/output”).

This chapter presents them one by one with an example. Note: functions such as SORT or SHUFFLE change the array on the spot (“in place”); they do not give back a new array.
Anzahl der Elemente. Bei mehrdimensional: The number of elements. For multi-dimensional arrays, the size of the first dimension.
DIMCOUNT liefert die Anzahl der Dimensio: DIMCOUNT gives the number of dimensions, DIMSIZE the size of the nth dimension (counted from 0).

Kehrt die Reihenfolge der Elemente um –: Reverses the order of the elements — in the array itself.
Liefert den ersten Index, an dem wert st: Gives the first index at which wert appears, or -1 if it does not occur.
Summe bzw. Durchschnitt eines Zahlen-Arr: The sum or the average of a numeric array. ARRAY_AVG always comes out as a decimal and needs a non-empty array.
Kleinstes bzw. größtes Element eines Zah: The smallest or largest element of a numeric array.
Setzt alle Fächer auf denselben Wert – g: Sets every locker to the same value — good for resetting.
Liefert eine unabhängige Kopie. Nötig, w: Gives an independent copy. Necessary because a plain b = a does not copy but leaves both names pointing at the same array (see the chapter “Arrays”).
Erzeugt eine fertige Zahlenreihe als TUP: Produces a ready-made sequence of numbers as a TUPLE — like the FOR of other languages, but as a value. The end is NOT included. Very handy together with FOR EACH or a comprehension.
ARRAY_PUSH hängt einen Wert hinten an un: ARRAY_PUSH appends a value at the end and gives the new length. ARRAY_POP removes the last element and returns it (the array must not be empty). Together they make a stack.
ARRAY_INSERT schiebt einen Wert an Posit: ARRAY_INSERT pushes a value in at position idx (the rest moves back; idx from 0 to the length). ARRAY_REMOVE_AT removes the element at idx and returns it (the rest moves forward).
Ändert die Größe nachträglich: wächst (n: Changes the size after the fact: grows (new lockers = the default value) or shrinks (surplus ones fall away). Existing values are kept.
Ein zufälliges Element ziehen (CHOICE) o: Drawing a random element (CHOICE) or shuffling the array (SHUFFLE) is in the chapter “Randomness”. Sorting by a rule of your own (a FUNCREF comparator) is possible — use a comparison function as described in the chapter “Functions and SUBs”.
Eine Map verbindet Schlüssel (immer Stri: A map connects keys (always strings) with values — explained at length in the chapter “Maps” (Part II). Here you will find every map function on its own with an example, for looking up. Many also exist in dot notation (m.get(...), m.put(...) …); that comes at the end of the chapter.

Liefert den Wert zum Schlüssel. Achtung:: Gives the value for the key. Careful: if the key is missing, the program stops — check first with MAPHAS or use MAPGETOR.
Liefert den Wert zum Schlüssel oder den: Gives the value for the key, or the fallback value if the key is missing. Never stops with an error.
TRUE when the key is present. The same as schlüssel$ IN m.
Entfernt ein Paar und liefert TRUE, wenn: Removes a pair and gives TRUE if the key was there (otherwise FALSE).
Empties the whole map at once.
Die Paare erscheinen stets in der Reihen: The pairs always appear in the order in which they were inserted.
Liefert alle Schlüssel als ARRAY OF STRI: Gives all the keys as an ARRAY OF STRING (good for sorting or walking through).
Liefert alle Werte als Array (in Einfüge: Gives all the values as an array (in insertion order).
Liefert alle Paare als Array von (Schlüs: Gives all the pairs as an array of (key, value) tuples — ideal with FOR EACH. paar[0] holds the key, paar[1] the value.
Auch direkt über die Map läuft FOR EACH: FOR EACH also runs over the map directly — the loop variable then receives each KEY, and you fetch the value with MAPGET. See the chapter “Maps”.

Diese Befehle liefern die aktuelle Uhrze: These commands give the current time, the date, and the time elapsed since the program started — useful for measuring durations, for cooldowns, or for a timestamp in a saved game. Because the values depend on when the program runs, the examples show a representative value as a comment rather than a fixed output.
Liefert die Anzahl der Millisekunden sei: Gives the number of milliseconds since the program started (1000 ms = 1 second). The absolute figure is rarely of interest — what is valuable is the difference between two MILLIS values, to measure a duration.
MILLIS eignet sich gut für eigene Zeitsc: MILLIS is well suited to time limits of your own (“do something every 500 ms”). For deliberate actions once a time has elapsed there is also the timer module with COOLDOWN (Part V).
Hält das Programm für die angegebene Zei: Halts the program for the time given. In a graphical game with a running picture you should avoid SLEEP (it freezes the window) — there you control the pace through the frame rate. For console programs, though, it is handy.
Liefert die aktuelle Uhrzeit als String: Gives the current time of day as a string in the format "HH:MM:SS" (hours:minutes:seconds).
Liefert das aktuelle Datum als String im: Gives the current date as a string in the format "YYYY-MM-DD" (year-month-day).
Beide eignen sich gut für einen Zeitstem: Both are well suited to a timestamp — for recording when a game was saved, for instance:
Für framerate-unabhängige Bewegung im Sp: For frame-rate-independent movement in the game window you use not MILLIS but DELTA() — the seconds since the last frame. That belongs to the game loop and is covered in Part IV (“The window”).
Mit Datei-Befehlen speicherst du Daten d: With the file commands you store data permanently on disk — saved games, high scores, settings, levels. Drachenhauch offers two routes: the classic one with a FILE handle (open the file, read/write line by line, close it) and the convenient path-based one (read or write a whole file in a single call). Paths are relative to your program's directory.
Jedes Beispiel hier schreibt und liest e: Every example here writes and reads real files. When trying them out, mind which folder your program is in — that is where the files appear.
OPENFILE öffnet eine Datei und liefert e: OPENFILE opens a file and gives a FILE handle. The mode is "r" (read), "w" (write anew, overwriting) or "a" (append). CLOSEFILE closes it again — important, so that what was written safely reaches the disk.
WRITELINE schreibt den Text und einen Ze: WRITELINE writes the text and a line break. WRITE writes with no break, so that several pieces end up on one line.
READLINE liefert die nächste Zeile (ohne: READLINE gives the next line (without the break). ENDOFFILE becomes TRUE once the end of the file is reached — the typical loop reads while NOT ENDOFFILE.
Liest den gesamten verbleibenden Inhalt: Reads all the remaining contents of the file at once, as one string.
Bequem: ganze Datei auf einmal: Convenient: the whole file at once
Für viele Fälle brauchst du gar kein Han: For many cases you need no handle at all. These path-based commands do the opening, reading/writing and closing in one step.
Schreibt den Text komplett in die Datei: Writes the text into the file in full (creating it anew, or overwriting it).
Liest die ganze Datei und liefert ihre Z: Reads the whole file and gives its lines as an ARRAY OF STRING.
Hängt Text ans Ende einer Datei an (legt: Appends text to the end of a file (creating it if it does not yet exist).
Gives the size of the file in bytes.
TRUE, wenn die Datei existiert. Praktisc: TRUE when the file exists. Handy for checking before reading whether a saved game, for instance, is there at all.
COPYFILE kopiert eine Datei, RENAME bene: COPYFILE copies a file, RENAME renames or moves it, DELETEFILE deletes it.
MKDIR legt ein Verzeichnis an (samt fehl: MKDIR creates a directory (along with any missing parent directories). DIREXISTS checks whether a directory is there.

Verbindet Pfadteile sauber mit Schrägstr: Joins path parts cleanly with slashes — better than stringing them together by hand with "/".
BASENAME liefert den letzten Bestandteil: BASENAME gives the last part of a path (the file or folder name), DIRNAME the directory part in front of it.
Statt einen Pfad im Code fest zu verdrah: Rather than wiring a path into the code, you can let the user choose with the familiar operating-system dialogue — “Open”, “Save as” or “Choose folder”. All three commands block the program until the user makes a choice or cancels (cancelled = the empty string "") — so do not use them in a running game loop, but at program start or from a menu item, say.
Diese drei Befehle öffnen ein echtes Sys: These three commands open a real system window and wait for the user. The following examples therefore show how they are used, without printing an output.
Öffnet den „Datei öffnen“-Dialog. endung: Opens the “Open file” dialogue. endungen$ filters what is shown, comma-separated and without dots ("png,jpg", for instance). Gives the chosen path, or "" if cancelled.
Öffnet den „Speichern unter“-Dialog mit: Opens the “Save as” dialogue, with an optional suggested file name. Gives the chosen path, or "" if cancelled.

Für echte Spielstände musst du Dateien n: For real saved games you do not have to manage files line by line yourself: the save module (Part V) offers comfortable save slots with named values, and the json module stores whole data structures. The raw file commands here are the foundation underneath.

Das Fenster & der Game-Loop: The window and the game loop
Jetzt wird es bunt: In Teil IV verlässt: Now things turn colourful: in Part IV you leave the text console and open a real graphics window. Here you draw shapes and images, play sounds, poll keyboard and mouse — in short, here is where games come about. The dhrt runtime handles all of it; a graphics program therefore always runs in the dhrt window, not in the console.
Bevor irgendetwas gezeichnet werden kann: Before anything can be drawn, a window has to be open. And because a game is in constant motion, almost every graphics program runs in a loop that draws a new picture many times a second. This chapter explains both: the window, and that game loop.
Öffnet das Grafikfenster mit der angegeb: Opens the graphics window at the logical size given, in pixels. Optionally a window title and a scale: skala > 1 enlarges every logical pixel (for a retro look). SCREEN must come before all other graphics commands.
Weitere Wege, ein Fenster zu öffnen: Other ways of opening a window
Öffnet ein randloses Fenster, das genau: Opens a borderless window covering exactly the current monitor (borderless fullscreen) — the logical resolution matches the monitor's native one. An alternative to SCREEN when you want not a fixed pixel grid but the full screen area.
Wie SCREEN, aber das Fenster selbst ist: Like SCREEN, but the window itself is transparent — only what you draw is visible, and the rest of the window lets the desktop show through. breite/höhe <= 0 covers the whole current monitor as a transparent overlay. MUST be the very first graphics instruction (transparency cannot be switched on after the fact).
SCREEN_NATIVE und SCREEN_TRANSPARENT ers: SCREEN_NATIVE and SCREEN_TRANSPARENT replace SCREEN — call only one of the three window openers per program, as the very first graphics instruction.
Ein paar Befehle stellen native Fenster-: A few commands set native operating-system window properties that go beyond mere size — for tool windows, overlays or kiosk modes, say.
WINDOW_TOPMOST hält das Fenster über all: WINDOW_TOPMOST keeps the window above all others (always in front) — useful for an overlay HUD. WINDOW_UNDECORATED removes the title bar and frame.
Lässt Maus-Klicks durch das Fenster hind: Lets mouse clicks pass through the window to whatever lies beneath — together with SCREEN_TRANSPARENT and WINDOW_TOPMOST that makes a pure display overlay which does not interact with the mouse.
Schaltet ein/aus, ob die ESC-Taste autom: Switches on or off whether the ESC key automatically raises QUITREQUESTED() (raylib's default behaviour). Turn it off when your game wants ESC for itself (a pause menu, say) rather than closing the window.
ESC schliesst das Fenster NICHT mehr aut: ESC no longer closes the window automatically
WINDOW_X/WINDOW_Y liefern die aktuelle B: WINDOW_X and WINDOW_Y give the current screen position of the window's top-left corner. SET_WINDOW_POS moves the window there.
Auf einem Mehrschirm-Setup willst du vie: On a multi-screen setup you may want to know how many monitors there are and what resolution they have — to place your window deliberately on a particular screen, for instance.
MONITOR_COUNT liefert die Anzahl angesch: MONITOR_COUNT gives the number of monitors attached. CURRENT_MONITOR gives the index (0-based) of the monitor the window is currently on.
Liefern Breite/Höhe in Pixeln, den Anzei: Give the width and height in pixels, the display name and the refresh rate (Hz) of the monitor with index i (0-based, 0 = main monitor).
MONITOR_X/MONITOR_Y liefern die Position: MONITOR_X and MONITOR_Y give a monitor's position within the virtual desktop area. SET_WINDOW_MONITOR moves the window to the monitor with index i.
Ein Spiel zeigt nicht ein einziges Stand: A game shows not a single still picture but many pictures per second — that is how motion comes about. The game loop is a loop that does the same thing over and over: clear the old picture, draw the scene afresh, show the finished picture. Three commands make its skeleton:
löscht das Bild (füllt es mit einer Farb: clears the picture (fills it with a colour, black by default).
alle Formen, Bilder und Texte dieses Bil: all the shapes, images and text of this frame.

Die einzelnen Zeichenbefehle (TEXT, BOX,: You will meet the individual drawing commands (TEXT, BOX, CIRCLE …) in detail in the next chapter. What matters here is the pattern: CLS at the start, FLIP at the end, drawing in between — frame after frame.

Zeigt das fertig gezeichnete Bild im Fen: Shows the finished picture in the window and waits for the next frame (60 per second by default). Without FLIP, what you drew stays invisible.
erst jetzt wird es sichtbar: only now does it become visible

Nicht jeder Computer schafft gleich viel: Not every computer manages the same number of frames per second. If you moved a figure by a fixed 5 pixels every frame, it would run faster on a fast machine than on a slow one. The remedy: DELTA() gives the time (in seconds) since the last frame. Multiply your speed by it and the movement is equally fast on every machine.

Liefern die aktuelle Breite und Höhe des: Give the current width and height of the window in pixels — handy for centring something without using fixed numbers.
Den Fenstertitel kannst du jederzeit änd: You can change the window title at any time (to show the file name or the score, for instance). SET_FULLSCREEN switches to fullscreen and back, WINDOW_IS_FULLSCREEN asks the state.

Setzt das Fenstersymbol aus einem per LO: Sets the window icon from an image loaded with LOADIMAGE. Without it an exported game carries the runtime's default icon — a detail that makes the difference between “tinkering” and “finished program”.

Normalerweise hat ein SCREEN-Fenster ein: Normally a SCREEN window has a fixed size. You can release it, though — SCREENWIDTH and SCREENHEIGHT then give the current size, and your program has to arrange its layout accordingly.
Gibt das Fenster zum Ziehen frei und beg: Releases the window for dragging and limits how small or large it may become.
TRUE in dem Frame, in dem der Nutzer die: TRUE in the frame in which the user changed the size — the right moment to recompute a layout, rather than doing so every frame.

Fragen denselben Zustand ab. WINDOW_MINI: Ask that same state. WINDOW_MINIMIZED is useful for saving processing time while the window is minimised.
WINDOW_FOCUSED sagt, ob dein Fenster ger: WINDOW_FOCUSED tells you whether your window is currently in front — the usual way of pausing a game automatically when the player clicks away. WINDOW_FOCUS brings the window forward.
Macht das ganze Fenster durchscheinend (: Makes the whole window translucent (1.0 = opaque, 0.0 = invisible) — for overlays, fade-ins, or a gentle appearance at startup.
Die Skalierung des Bildschirms: 1.0 ist: The screen's scaling: 1.0 is normal, 2.0 a HiDPI/Retina display. Without these values a program cannot tell whether its pixel sizes will come out tiny on the target device — for enlarging text and controls, for instance.
Sekunden seit Programmstart als Kommazah: Seconds since the program started, as a decimal, rising monotonically. Unlike TIMER it runs on independently of the time of day — good for animations, timings and sequences.
Lesen und Schreiben der System-Zwischena: Reading and writing the system clipboard. That lets a saved game be passed on as text, or a level code pasted in.
Zieht der Nutzer Dateien auf das Fenster: If the user drags files onto the window, FILES_DROPPED gives their number in that frame and FILE_DROPPED(i) each path — the most convenient way of opening a level or an image.
Öffnet eine Adresse im Standardbrowser –: Opens an address in the default browser — the manual or the game's page, for instance.
OPENURL nimmt bewusst keine anderen Sche: OPENURL deliberately accepts no other schemes. The address is passed on to the system shell; a file: scheme would therefore be a way of starting arbitrary programs from within a Drachenhauch program.
PRINT und INPUT (Teil III) gehören zur T: PRINT and INPUT (Part III) belong to the text console. Once SCREEN is running, you put text into the window with TEXT and poll input with the keyboard and mouse commands (chapter “Input”). Do not mix the two in the same part of a program.
Mit dem Fenster aus dem letzten Kapitel: With the window from the last chapter you can now draw. Drachenhauch offers all the basic shapes: pixels, lines, rectangles, circles, triangles, polygons, ellipses, arcs and text. Every command is called between CLS and FLIP (see the game loop). The last argument is almost always a colour — as RGB(r, g, b) or one of the colour constants (chapter “Colours”).

Die 2D-Grundformen: Linie, gefülltes und: The 2D basic shapes: line, filled and outlined rectangle, circle, triangle, ellipse, polygon, arc and text.
Koordinaten zählen ab der linken oberen: Coordinates count from the top left corner: x to the right, y DOWNWARDS. So (0, 0) is top left. With BOX and RECT you give two corner points (x1, y1, x2, y2) — both included.
Zieht eine Linie von (x1, y1) nach (x2,: Draws a line from (x1, y1) to (x2, y2).
Zeichnet ein GEFÜLLTES Rechteck zwischen: Draws a FILLED rectangle between the two corner points.
Zeichnet nur den RAHMEN eines Rechtecks: Draws only the OUTLINE of a rectangle (1 pixel wide).
Zeichnet einen gefüllten Kreis mit Mitte: Draws a filled circle with centre (x, y) and the radius given.
Wie CIRCLE, zeichnet aber nur die Kontur: Like CIRCLE, but draws only the outline (1 pixel wide) rather than a filled area.
Zeichnet eine Ellipse, eingepasst in das: Draws an ellipse fitted into the rectangle (x1, y1)–(x2, y2). ELLIPSE fills, ELLIPSEOUTLINE draws only the outline (with an optional width).
Zeichnet ein Dreieck aus drei Eckpunkten: Draws a triangle from three corner points — TRIANGLE filled, TRIANGLEOUTLINE as an outline only.
Zeichnet ein Vieleck. punkte ist ein ARR: Draws a polygon. punkte is an ARRAY OF INTEGER with alternating x and y values ([x1, y1, x2, y2, …], at least 3 points). POLYGON fills, POLYGONOUTLINE draws only the edges.
Die Reihenfolge der Eckpunkte spielt bei: The order of the corner points makes no difference for filled triangles and polygons — clockwise or anticlockwise, the area is always filled.
Zeichnet ein Bogensegment, eingepasst in: Draws an arc segment fitted into the rectangle (x1, y1)–(x2, y2). The angles start and ende are in radians (0 to 2·PI), anticlockwise.
Schreibt Text an die Position (x, y) (li: Writes text at position (x, y) (the top left corner of the text). In the console you use PRINT, in the window TEXT.
Schreibt Text ZENTRIERT auf (x, y), um d: Writes text CENTRED on (x, y), rotated about that point (angle in degrees) and optionally scaled — good for slanted labels or score pop-ups.
Standardmäßig zeichnet TEXT in einer ein: By default TEXT draws in a built-in font. For headings, a menu or a style of your own, you load a TrueType file — or a pixel font from a PNG.
LOADFONT lädt eine .ttf-Datei in einer b: LOADFONT loads a .ttf file at a particular size and gives a handle; SETFONT makes it the active font (-1 switches back to the built-in one). TEXT_SIZE changes the character size for the TEXT calls that follow.
Backe die Schrift in der Größe, in der d: Bake the font at the size you need: LOADFONT rasterises it once, and text scaled up beyond that goes blurry. So for two sizes, two LOADFONT calls.
Lädt eine Pixelschrift aus einem PNG, in: Loads a pixel font from a PNG in which the characters are set apart by a separator colour. erstes_zeichen is the code of the first character in the image (usually 32, for the space). Unlike TrueType fonts, this one stays unfiltered — so pixel type stays pixelly.
Wie breit wird dieser Text, und wie hoch: How wide this text will be, and how tall a line is — in the current font and size. With those you centre text properly, or draw a box of the right size behind it.
TEXT_SPACING ändert den Abstand zwischen: TEXT_SPACING changes the gap between characters (letter spacing), TEXT_LINE_SPACING the line spacing in multi-line text.
Schalten Fett und Kursiv für die folgend: Switch bold and italic on or off for the TEXT calls that follow. Both are produced artificially (by offsetting several times, or shearing) — a proper bold font loaded separately looks better, but for emphasis in a game this will do.
Über die Grundformen hinaus bietet Drach: Beyond the basic shapes, Drachenhauch offers some pleasant extras: thick lines, rounded rectangles, gradients, smooth curves, blend modes for glow effects, ready-generated textures and intermediate drawing surfaces. All of them — like the whole chapter — are used in the graphics window between CLS and FLIP.
Farbverläufe, ein rundes Rechteck, dicke: Gradients, a rounded rectangle, thick lines and a smooth spline curve.
Wie LINE, aber mit einstellbarer Strichb: Like LINE, but with an adjustable stroke width in pixels.
Zeichnen ein Rechteck mit abgerundeten E: Draw a rectangle with rounded corners (corner radius in pixels). BOXROUND fills, RECTROUND draws only the outline.
Füllen ein Rechteck mit einem weichen Fa: Fill a rectangle with a smooth gradient from farbe1 to farbe2 — GRADIENTV vertically (top to bottom), GRADIENTH horizontally (left to right). Good for skies, backgrounds or buttons.
Zeichnet eine weiche Kurve, die durch al: Draws a smooth curve running through all the control points given. xs and ys are two arrays of the same length holding the points' x and y coordinates.
Normalerweise überdeckt eine neue Form d: Normally a new shape covers whatever lies beneath it. With a different blend mode you can add colours instead — overlapping areas then become brighter and glow. Ideal for fire, magic or cones of light.
Oben drei erzeugte Texturen; unten überl: Above, three generated textures; below, overlapping circles in additive mode (brighter = glow).
Stellt den Mischmodus für die folgenden: Sets the blend mode for the drawing commands that follow: "alpha" (normal), "add" (additive — glows), "mult" (multiplying — darkens) or "subtract". Switch back with BLEND_MODE("alpha") after the effect.
Diese Befehle berechnen ein fertiges Bil: These commands compute a finished image (an IMAGE), which you then draw with DRAWIMAGE like a loaded picture (see the chapter “Images”). Handy for backgrounds, with no image file to ship.
Erzeugt eine weiche, wolkige Rauschtextu: Generates a soft, cloudy noise texture (Perlin noise). A larger skala gives coarser patterns. Good for clouds, fog, terrain.
Erzeugt eine Verlaufstextur von farbe1 n: Generates a gradient texture from farbe1 to farbe2 (vertikal = TRUE for vertical, FALSE for horizontal).
GENTEX_CHECKED erzeugt ein Schachbrettmu: GENTEX_CHECKED generates a chequerboard (fx × fy squares), GENTEX_COLOR a plain area of one colour, GENTEX_RADIAL a round gradient from the centre outwards — perfect for soft lights and glows.
Ein Render-Target ist eine unsichtbare Z: A render target is an invisible drawing surface in the background. You draw something into it once and then stamp it into the picture as often as you like — which saves work when a composite image (a badge or a minimap, say) appears several times or changes only rarely.
RENDERTARGET_NEW legt eine Fläche an. Zw: RENDERTARGET_NEW creates a surface. Between _BEGIN and _END all drawing commands land in that surface rather than in the window. _DRAW stamps the finished surface into the picture at position (x, y).
ab jetzt in die Flaeche zeichnen: draw into the surface from here on
Flaeche ins Bild stempeln: stamp the surface into the picture
Drei weitere Muster: GENTEX_CELLULAR erz: Three more patterns: GENTEX_CELLULAR generates cellular noise (Voronoi) — stone floors, cracks, scales; a smaller kachel gives finer cells. GENTEX_NOISE is pure white noise, with anteil (0.0–1.0) controlling how many pixels are set — for starfields or film grain. GENTEX_GRADIENT_BOX runs rectangularly from the inside out and is thus the square counterpart to GENTEX_RADIAL — ideal for vignettes.
Shader: eigene Effekte auf der Grafikkar: Shaders: your own effects on the graphics card
Ein Shader ist ein kleines Programm, das: A shader is a small program that the graphics card runs for EVERY pixel. It gives you effects that would be unaffordable with ordinary drawing commands: screen curvature as on a cathode-ray monitor, glow (bloom), colour casts, ripples. Drachenhauch passes the finished frame through a fragment shader written in GLSL.
Lädt einen Fragment-Shader – entweder au: Loads a fragment shader — either from a file or directly as source in the string. Gives a handle, or -1 if compilation fails (the graphics card's error message then appears in the console).
Schickt ab jetzt jeden fertigen Frame du: From here on, sends every finished frame through the shader before it appears in the window. POSTFX(-1) switches the effect off again. Internally the scene is rendered into an invisible surface for this and then brought to the screen with the shader.
Setzen eine Variable („Uniform“) im Shad: Set a variable (a “uniform”) in the shader: a single number, a pair (a screen size, say) or a triple (a colour, say). The name must match the one in the shader exactly; unknown names are not an error (the compiler throws unused variables away).
Für größere Datenmengen: SHADER_SET_ARRA: For larger amounts of data: SHADER_SET_ARRAY fills a uniform float[] from an ARRAY OF FLOAT (several light positions, for instance), SHADER_SET_TEXTURE occupies a SECOND image sampler (masks, colour tables, cross-fades), SHADER_SET_MATRIX passes a MAT4 from the m3d module.
Fertige Beispiel-Shader (CRT, Bloom, Vig: Ready-made example shaders (CRT, bloom, vignette) are under examples/assets/shaders/, and a complete demo is examples/86_postfx_shaders.dh.
Normalerweise wird ein Render-Target zu: Normally a render target is cleared for every frame — you draw into it, stamp it, done. With behalten = TRUE, by contrast, the contents stay put beyond the frame. That creates feedback: what you draw is still there next frame, and whatever you paint over it is added. That is exactly how light trails and streaks come about.
Leert eine behaltene Fläche von Hand. Be: Clears a retained surface by hand. With behalten = TRUE nobody else does it for you any more.
jedes Bild: alles ETWAS abdunkeln, dann: each frame: darken everything SLIGHTLY, then set the point afresh
Das Abdunkeln ist der Trick: Ohne es wür: The darkening is the trick: without it the trail would never fade and the surface would fill up after a few seconds. A full-screen rectangle in multiply mode takes a few per cent of brightness off every frame — so the tail grows darker towards the back by itself.
RENDERTARGET_DRAW innerhalb eines andere: RENDERTARGET_DRAW inside another render target does nothing. If you want feedback, use behalten = TRUE — that is exactly what it is for.
Licht, Nebel, Himmel, Schatten, Kamera,: Lighting, fog, sky, shadows, camera, font and the post effect are GLOBAL. Change them in one scene and you have to change them back by hand when you leave — and forget a single line and you see the mistake two scenes later: fog in the wrong room, the shader over the menu. With a stack that becomes a property of the language instead of a question of discipline.
GFX_PUSH legt den gesamten Zeichenzustan: GFX_PUSH puts the entire drawing state onto a stack, GFX_POP fetches it back. GFX_DEPTH tells you how deep the stack currently is — a POP without a PUSH is an error.
Gesichert wird ausschließlich EINSTELLUN: What is saved is SETTING only, never resource: the 2D camera including shake, the active layer, the background colour, lighting, environment, shadows, the 3D camera, the font and POSTFX. Loaded images, models and shaders naturally stay loaded — a POP only puts their use back.
AUDIO_PUSH und AUDIO_POP tun dasselbe fü: AUDIO_PUSH and AUDIO_POP do the same for all the bus settings — volume, balance, filter, reverb, delay, distortion, compressor, EQ. More on that in the audio chapter.
Alles nur in dhrt: All of it in dhrt only
Diese Extras (besonders Blend-Modes, Gen: These extras (blend modes, GenTex, render targets and shaders in particular) use the graphics card and run only in the dhrt window — as does the whole of Part IV. In a pure console program they do not exist.
Statt alles aus Formen zu zeichnen, läds: Rather than drawing everything from shapes, you usually load finished pictures (sprites, backgrounds, tilesets) from PNG files. In Drachenhauch a picture is an IMAGE value; you load it once before the game loop and then draw it every frame. Often a file holds a whole “spritesheet” — several single frames side by side, from which you cut out the one you want.
Ein Spritesheet als Ganzes, ein einzelne: A spritesheet as a whole, a single frame from it, scaled and rotated, plus mirrored and tinted (imgfx).
Bildpfade sind relativ zum Verzeichnis d: Image paths are relative to your program's directory (an assets/ subfolder is customary). Load images once before the game loop — not afresh every frame.
Lädt eine Bilddatei (PNG, JPG, BMP …) un: Loads an image file (PNG, JPG, BMP …) and gives an IMAGE. The result is cached — a second call with the same path does not load from disk again.
Liefern Breite und Höhe eines Bildes in: Give the width and height of an image in pixels — useful for centring it, or for dividing a sheet into frames.
Liest die Farbe eines einzelnen Pixels e: Reads back the colour of a single pixel of a loaded image (as a 0xRRGGBB number, the same format as RGB()). Gives -1 for invalid coordinates. Combined with RED()/GREEN()/BLUE() (chapter “Colours”) you read the individual channels out — handy for evaluating a heightmap or a colour map pixel by pixel, for instance.
Zeichnet das ganze Bild mit der linken o: Draws the whole image with its top left corner at (x, y).
Zeichnet nur einen Ausschnitt des Bildes: Draws only a section of the image: the rectangle (sx, sy, sw, sh) from the source, drawn at (x, y). That is how you fetch a single frame from a spritesheet — here the first of eight 32×32 frames.
Wie DRAWIMAGEPART, aber mit eigener Ziel: Like DRAWIMAGEPART, but with a target size of your own (w, h) rather than 1:1 — the section is stretched or squeezed to the target size as it is drawn. Handy for showing a small sprite frame enlarged, without making a scaled copy first.
Zeichnet das Bild ZENTRIERT auf (x, y),: Draws the image CENTRED on (x, y), rotated about that point by winkel degrees and optionally scaled and tinted. Ideal for rotating sprites (asteroids, projectiles, turning figures).
Zeichnet das Bild gespiegelt, ohne dafür: Draws the image mirrored, without making a mirrored copy for it. The classic case: a figure that should walk both left AND right — you draw the same image once normally and once with flip_x = TRUE.
Verschiebt den gesamten bisherigen Bildi: Shifts everything drawn so far by dx/dy pixels. With it you build a trailing effect or an endlessly scrolling background without redrawing everything — the edge that is freed up stays empty, though, and has to be filled by you.
Lädt alle in einer JSON-Datei aufgeführt: Loads every image and sound listed in a JSON file in advance and puts them into the cache; gives the number of files loaded. Afterwards every later LOADIMAGE/LOADSOUND is a cache hit — the game no longer stutters the first time an enemy appears.
Alias aus dem Manifest, sofort da: alias from the manifest, there at once
Im Manifest stehen zwei Abschnitte, beid: The manifest has two sections, both optional. Written as an object (alias → path) you can load the image later by the short alias; as a list, only by the path. The paths are relative to the manifest:
Das Modul imgfx erzeugt aus einem Bild e: The imgfx module makes a NEW, altered image out of an image — scaled, rotated, mirrored or tinted. The original stays unchanged. Do such transformations once before the game loop (not every frame), because they cost some time.
Liefert eine in der angegebenen Größe sk: Gives a copy of the image scaled to the size given.
Liefert eine gespiegelte Kopie – flipX s: Gives a mirrored copy — flipX mirrors horizontally (left/right), flipY vertically (top/bottom). The classic use is making a figure that walks right face left as well.
IMAGE_ROTATE liefert eine um grad gedreh: IMAGE_ROTATE gives a copy rotated by grad degrees (the image size may grow with it). IMAGE_TINT multiplies every pixel colour by farbe — good for tinting the same sprite in team colours (red team / blue team).
Willst du ein Bild nur beim Zeichnen dre: If you only want to rotate or scale an image as you draw it, use DRAWIMAGEROT — that is fast and needs no new image. If, on the other hand, you need the altered version repeatedly (a mirrored walk animation, say), make it once with imgfx and then draw it normally.
Neben Skalieren/Spiegeln/Drehen/Tönen br: Besides scaling, mirroring, rotating and tinting, imgfx brings further filters. Like IMAGE_SCALE and company they give a NEW, altered copy of the image — the original stays unchanged.
IMAGE_GRAYSCALE liefert eine Graustufen-: IMAGE_GRAYSCALE gives a greyscale copy (all channels mixed to the same brightness value). IMAGE_INVERT reverses every colour channel (255 minus the value) — red becomes cyan-ish, the classic photographic negative effect.
IMAGE_BRIGHTNESS hellt jeden Kanal um n: IMAGE_BRIGHTNESS lightens every channel by n (negative = darken). IMAGE_CONTRAST stretches or squeezes the contrast by n per cent (negative = flatter, positive = punchier).
Liefert eine weichgezeichnete Kopie – gr: Gives a blurred copy — a larger radius means a stronger blur. Good for glow effects, or a background picture meant to sit out of focus behind the figure.
Ersetzt jedes Pixel der Farbe von durch: Replaces every pixel of colour von with nach — the classic colour-swap technique for sprite recolours (making a green team out of a red sprite, say) or for marking a colour as transparent.
IMAGE_CROP schneidet den Bereich (x, y,: IMAGE_CROP cuts the area (x, y, w, h) out of an image. IMAGE_RESIZE_CANVAS changes the canvas size (without scaling the picture itself) and places the old image at (offx, offy) — the new border is filled with fuellfarbe.
Die folgenden vier Befehle unterscheiden: The following four commands differ from the filters above: they change the image passed in DIRECTLY (in place) rather than giving a copy — like a miniature drawing program on an IMAGE canvas. Handy for assembling a texture atlas at run time, or for painting a heightmap or colour map procedurally.
Zeichnen einen gefüllten Kreis, eine Lin: Draw a filled circle, a line or a filled rectangle directly into the image's pixels — the same basic shapes as when drawing to the window (chapter “2D drawing”), only applied to an IMAGE instead of the screen.
Schreibt Text direkt in die Pixel des Bi: Writes text directly into the image's pixels — to burn a label permanently into a generated icon or a map, for instance.
IMAGE_COPY macht eine echte Kopie (nützl: IMAGE_COPY makes a genuine copy (useful before the mutating drawing commands further down). IMAGE_SCALE_NN scales WITHOUT smoothing — for pixel art that is the right way, because IMAGE_SCALE smears the hard edges into gradients. Use whole-number multiples where you can (2x, 3x, 4x).
Freie Faltung mit einem quadratischen Ke: Free convolution with a square kernel (3×3, 5×5 …) as a flat ARRAY OF FLOAT in row order. With it you build sharpening, edge detection or embossing yourself — IMAGE_BLUR can only blur.
ALPHA_MASK überträgt die Durchsichtigkei: ALPHA_MASK carries over the transparency of a second image (soft edges, cones of light). ALPHA_CROP cuts transparent borders away — handy for trimming a sprite that was exported too large. PREMULTIPLY prevents dark seams when scaling semi-transparent images.
IMAGE_DITHER reduziert die Farbtiefe mit: IMAGE_DITHER reduces the colour depth with dithering — the typical retro look. ONLY the combinations 5,6,5,0 and 5,5,5,1 and 4,4,4,4 are permitted; anything else is refused (raylib would otherwise deliver an unusable image). IMAGE_PALETTE gives an image's most frequent colours as an array — for tinting a matching user interface from it, say.
Die vier DRAW-Befehle mutieren das Bild: The four DRAW commands mutate the image directly — NO copy is made. If you want to keep the original, make a copy yourself beforehand (with IMAGE_SCALE(img, IMAGEWIDTH(img), IMAGEHEIGHT(img)), for instance).
Eine Farbe ist in Drachenhauch eine ganz: In Drachenhauch a colour is a whole number combining the red, green and blue components (the format 0xRRGGBB). You never have to work that number out yourself, though: RGB(r, g, b) builds it from three values between 0 and 255, and there are ready-made constants for the common colours. This chapter shows how to make, mix and take colours apart.
Farbkonstanten, ein HSV-Regenbogen, ein: Colour constants, an HSV rainbow, a COLOR_LERP gradient and a brightness series.
Baut eine Farbe aus den drei Kanälen Rot: Builds a colour from the three channels red, green and blue (each 0 to 255). 0,0,0 is black, 255,255,255 white, 255,0,0 pure red.
Hexadezimale Farb-Literale schreibst du: In Drachenhauch you write hexadecimal colour literals with &H rather than 0x: &HFF8000 is the same as RGB(255, 128, 0). For beginners, though, RGB(...) stays the most readable.
Für die häufigsten Farben gibt es Konsta: For the commonest colours there are constants you can put straight in as a colour — shorter than RGB(...). Available are, among others: BLACK, WHITE, GRAY, LIGHTGRAY, DARKGRAY, RED, GREEN, BLUE, YELLOW, CYAN, MAGENTA, ORANGE, PURPLE, BROWN, PINK, and DARKRED, DARKGREEN, DARKBLUE.
Vordefinierte Farbwerte. Du kannst sie ü: Predefined colour values. You can use them anywhere a colour is expected.
Farben zerlegen: RED, GREEN, BLUE: Taking colours apart: RED, GREEN, BLUE
Holen den einzelnen Kanal (0 bis 255) au: Fetch a single channel (0 to 255) out of a colour. Handy for darkening a colour or comparing two. (With brackets these are functions; without brackets, RED is the red colour constant — Drachenhauch tells the two apart by the brackets.)
Manchmal denkt man Farben lieber als „Fa: Sometimes one would rather think of colours as “hue, saturation, brightness” than as red/green/blue. That is precisely HSV: the hue (0 to 360 degrees) runs once round the rainbow, the saturation (0 to 1) goes from grey to vivid, the value (0 to 1) from dark to light. HSV is ideal for producing rainbow effects, or for making a colour merely lighter or darker.
Erzeugt eine Farbe aus Farbton (0–360 Gr: Makes a colour from hue (0–360 degrees), saturation (0–1) and value/brightness (0–1). HSV(120, 1, 1) is a rich green.
Regenbogen: Farbton mit der Zeit durchla: rainbow: let the hue run round with time
Mischt zwei Farben kanalweise. t = 0 erg: Mixes two colours channel by channel. t = 0 gives farbe1, t = 1 gives farbe2, t = 0.5 the middle. Perfect for smooth colour transitions (day to night, an energy bar from green to red).
RGBA baut eine Farbe MIT Durchsichtigkei: RGBA builds a colour WITH transparency: a = 255 is opaque, 0 invisible, and values in between let the background show through. ALPHA reads a colour's alpha component back out.
Ein hübsches Muster: Färbe einen Lebensb: A pretty pattern: colour a health bar according to how full it is. anteil = hp / max_hp (0..1), then farbe = COLOR_LERP(RED, GREEN, anteil) — full is green, empty is red, and it flows in between.
Ein Spiel wird erst lebendig, wenn der S: A game only comes alive when the player can intervene. In the graphics window you poll keyboard, mouse and gamepad not with INPUT (that is for the console only) but frame by frame in the game loop. This chapter shows the direct queries and the comfortable input module, with which you bind keys to named actions.
Eine kleine Steuerungs-Demo: ein per Tas: A small control demo: a player moved by keyboard, and a legend of the controls.
Liefert TRUE, solange die angegebene Tas: Gives TRUE as long as the key named is held down. You give the key as a KEY_ constant. Polled in the game loop, that gives smooth movement.
Eingebaute Tasten-Konstanten gibt es für: There are built-in key constants for all the important keys: KEY_LEFT, KEY_RIGHT, KEY_UP, KEY_DOWN, KEY_SPACE, KEY_RETURN (= KEY_ENTER), KEY_ESCAPE, KEY_TAB, KEY_BACKSPACE, the letters KEY_A to KEY_Z and the digits KEY_0 to KEY_9.
KEYPRESSED ist „gehalten“ – es ist TRUE,: KEYPRESSED means “held” — it is TRUE as long as the key is down. For “exactly once on the press” (a jump, a menu choice) you use the edge detection of the input module further down (INPUT_PRESSED).
Liefern die aktuelle Mausposition im Fen: Give the current mouse position in the window (in logical pixels). Good for drawing a crosshair or a cursor, or for checking what the mouse is over.
Liefert TRUE, wenn die Maustaste n gedrü: Gives TRUE when mouse button n is down: 0 = left, 1 = middle, 2 = right.
Liefert die Drehung des Mausrads seit de: Gives the turn of the mouse wheel since the last call: positive upwards, negative downwards, 0 if nothing was turned. Good for zooming or paging.
MOUSE_VISIBLE zeigt/versteckt den System: MOUSE_VISIBLE shows or hides the system cursor (hide it when you draw a cursor sprite of your own). MOUSE_LOCK captures the cursor inside the window — for mouse camera control in 3D or first-person view.
Tasten direkt abzufragen funktioniert, h: Polling keys directly works, but has two weaknesses: the controls are wired in (no remapping possible), and “exactly once on the press” is something you have to rig up yourself. The input module solves both: you bind keys to named actions ("springen", "links") and query those actions. Several keys per action are allowed (arrow key AND WASD).
Wichtig: Einmal pro Frame ruft INPUT_UPD: Important: call INPUT_UPDATE() once per frame — that is what makes the edge detection (PRESSED/RELEASED) possible in the first place.
INPUT_BIND verbindet eine Aktion mit ein: INPUT_BIND connects an action with one or more keys (once, at the start). INPUT_UPDATE reads the current key state once per frame — compulsory at the beginning of the game loop.
INPUT_HELD ist TRUE, solange eine gebund: INPUT_HELD is TRUE as long as a bound key is held (for movement). INPUT_PRESSED is TRUE only in the one frame in which the key is newly pressed (for a jump, a menu). INPUT_RELEASED fires on release.
Fasst zwei gegensätzliche Aktionen zu ei: Combines two opposing actions into one axis and gives -1, 0 or +1. Very handy for left/right or up/down movement in a single line.
Das input-Modul unterstützt auch Gamepad: The input module supports gamepads too: bind actions to button codes such as JOY_BUTTON_A or JOY_DPAD_LEFT, or read an analogue stick with INPUT_JOY_AXIS(slot, "left_x"). That way the same game logic works with keyboard AND controller, with no change to the code.
KEYPRESSED und MOUSEBUTTON melden „wird: KEYPRESSED and MOUSEBUTTON report “is being held” — which is almost never what is meant by a click. The commands below give the EDGE, that is the single frame in which something changes. For that you need neither the input module nor bookkeeping of your own.
KEYPRESSED und MOUSEBUTTON heißen so, se: KEYPRESSED and MOUSEBUTTON have borne those names since Drachenhauch began, and still report “held”. The edge variants therefore have names of their own: KEYHIT and MOUSE_HIT.

The game notices nothing: during replay, KEYPRESSED, MOUSEX and company deliver the recorded values. Three things become possible with it: a demo mode that plays itself; bug reports that can be replayed; and automated play tests.

For the same thing to come out, the rest has to match: reset the starting state, pin the randomness with a fixed seed (RANDOMIZE 12345) and calculate per frame rather than per second — the replay counts in frames, and with DELTA()-based movement the same recording gives a slightly different path at a different frame rate.
Aufgezeichnet wird die EINGABE, nicht de: What is recorded is the INPUT, not the course of play

Drachenhauch plays short sound effects and longer pieces of music, and can even generate tones itself, with no audio file to ship. Sound cannot of course be printed in a book — but what you build with it can: this chapter develops a small, playable piano.

Layer, Sprite-Atlas & Bulk-Draws: Layers, sprite atlas and bulk draws
Dieses Kapitel sammelt drei Techniken fü: This chapter gathers three techniques for tidy, fast graphics: layers arrange what you draw into planes (background at the back, HUD at the front), a sprite atlas puts many images into one file and makes them addressable by name, and the bulk commands draw hundreds of similar shapes in a single call.
Eine geschichtete Szene: Sternenfeld (PL: A layered scene: starfield (PLOTS) and planets (CIRCLES) as bulk draws, with the HUD bar on the topmost layer.
Normalerweise überdeckt später Gezeichne: Normally what is drawn later covers what came earlier. Layers free you from that strict order: you draw onto named planes with a z value, and at the FLIP all the layers are stacked from back (small z) to front (large z). Your HUD thus always stays in front, no matter when you draw it.
LAYER_DEFINE registriert eine Ebene mit: LAYER_DEFINE registers a layer with its depth z (small = at the back). LAYER switches the drawing target to that layer — every drawing command that follows lands there until you switch to another.
legt bg und hud in z-Reihenfolge überein: stacks bg and hud in z order
LAYER_END schaltet zurück auf das Haupt-: LAYER_END switches back to the main picture (FLIP does that automatically anyway). LAYER_CLEAR empties a single layer by hand — rarely necessary, since FLIP clears every layer after stacking them.
Viele Sprites aus einer Textur: der Spri: Many sprites from one texture: the sprite atlas
Ein Sprite-Atlas ist ein großes Bild, in: A sprite atlas is one large image holding many small sprites, plus a list saying which name belongs to which section. That saves memory and makes drawing many sprites fast. You describe the atlas in a JSON file:
ATLAS_LOAD lädt das Manifest und liefert: ATLAS_LOAD loads the manifest and gives a SPRITE_ATLAS. ATLAS_DRAW draws the named sub-sprite at (x, y).
Zeichnet ein Sub-Sprite gespiegelt: flip: Draws a sub-sprite mirrored: flipX horizontally, flipY vertically (TRUE/FALSE each). Classic for walk animations — only the right-facing variant is in the atlas, and the left-facing one is derived with flipX.
Zwei Befehle aus alten Tagen. BATCH_DRAW: Two commands from the old days. BATCH_DRAW is nowadays merely a second name for ATLAS_DRAW, and BATCH_FLUSH does nothing at all. You need neither — they are kept only so that older code keeps working.
Der Name führt in die Irre: Es wird nich: The name misleads: nothing is gathered and nothing is batched. Drachenhauch records every drawing command in the active layer at once and plays all the layers back in order at the FLIP — gathering would not even be possible there. If you want to draw many similar things, use the bulk commands in the next section; those genuinely save work.
Hunderte Formen auf einmal: Bulk-Draws: Hundreds of shapes at once: bulk draws
Willst du sehr viele gleichartige Formen: If you want to draw a great many similar shapes — a starfield, a point cloud, a rain of particles — a loop of individual PLOT calls is slow. The bulk commands instead take whole arrays of coordinates and draw everything in a single call. The colour is either one number (all the same) or an array (one colour per shape).
Zeichnet viele Pixel auf einmal. xs und: Draws many pixels at once. xs and ys are arrays of the same length holding the coordinates. Ideal for starfields and point clouds. anzahl draws only the first n entries.
Die Bulk-Varianten von CIRCLE, BOX und L: The bulk variants of CIRCLE, BOX and LINE: every parameter is an array, and all the shapes are drawn in one call. CIRCLES additionally needs an array of radii. Here too anzahl limits how many entries are drawn.
Das ist die häufigste Falle bei den Bulk: This is the commonest trap with the bulk commands. A buffer of fixed size — DIM xs[1000], but only 200 stars on screen — drags its 800 unused slots along: they all stand at 0 and appear as a clump in the top left corner. Pass the actual count and the rest is left alone.
Ohne anzahl wird IMMER das ganze Array g: Without anzahl the WHOLE array is always drawn
Für eine Handvoll Formen sind die normal: For a handful of shapes the ordinary commands (CIRCLE, BOX …) are perfectly fine and more readable. The bulk variants only pay off at many hundreds or thousands of similar shapes per frame — then they save noticeable time.
Drachenhauch kann nicht nur flache 2D-Bi: Drachenhauch can draw not only flat 2D pictures but real 3D worlds — with the g3d module. A third coordinate joins in for that: z (depth). A virtual camera looks from a point in space towards a target, and you place bodies such as cubes, spheres and cylinders wherever you like. This chapter shows the basic building blocks; 3D is a large subject, and here you take only a first look at it.
Eine einfache 3D-Szene: Boden-Raster, Wü: A simple 3D scene: ground grid, cube (with wireframe), sphere, cylinder and cone.
3D läuft – wie der ganze Teil IV – nur i: 3D runs — like the whole of Part IV — only in the dhrt window. The structure is as in 2D: CLS in the game loop, then draw, then FLIP. Only the camera joins in at the start of each frame, and all the commands come from the g3d module (IMPORT "g3d").
Setzt die Kamera für diesen Frame: Sie s: Sets the camera for this frame: it stands at the point (px, py, pz) and looks towards the target (tx, ty, tz). fov is the field of view in degrees (45, say). Make this call first in the 3D part of every frame — before the bodies.
Eine kreisende Kamera baust du, indem du: You build a circling camera by working out its position over time with SIN and COS: cx = COS(t) * radius, cz = SIN(t) * radius, increasing t every frame. The view then orbits the action.
Orientierung: das Boden-Raster: Getting your bearings: the ground grid
Zeichnet ein Gitter in der Bodenebene –: Draws a grid on the ground plane — very helpful for finding your bearings in space. linien is the number of lines per direction, abstand their spacing.
Die Grundkörper bekommen ihre Position a: The basic bodies take their position as (x, y, z) and their dimensions, then a colour. For each filled body there is usually a wireframe variant (…_WIRES) that draws only the edges — nice for emphasising outlines.
Zeichnet einen Quader am Mittelpunkt (x,: Draws a box centred on (x, y, z) with the three edge lengths. CUBE fills, CUBE_WIRES draws only the wireframe (they combine well: CUBE first, then CUBE_WIRES in a darker colour).
Zeichnet eine Kugel mit Mittelpunkt (x,: Draws a sphere centred on (x, y, z) with the radius given.
Zeichnet einen Zylinder. Mit unterschied: Draws a cylinder. With different radii it becomes a truncated cone; set radius_oben to 0 and you get a pointed cone.
PLANE zeichnet eine flache Fläche in der: PLANE draws a flat surface on the ground plane, LINE3D a line between two points in space, POINT3D a single point. Good for floors, axes and markers.
Liefern, wo die Kamera steht und worauf: Give where the camera stands and what it is looking at. You need that constantly: for the origin of a ray of your own, for distance calculations (what is close enough to pick up?), or for following the camera smoothly.
Schaltet eine fertige Kamerasteuerung ei: Switches on a ready-made camera control: 1 = free, 2 = orbital (circles the target), 3 = first person, 4 = third person. The call belongs in the loop once per frame and handles mouse and keys itself.
Eigene Formen: Meshes und Modelle: Shapes of your own: meshes and models
Ein MODEL ist eine wiederverwendbare For: A MODEL is a reusable shape, created once and then drawn as often as you like — unlike CUBE or SPHERE, which are rebuilt on every call. You either load a file or have a shape computed.
LOADMODEL lädt eine OBJ- oder GLTF-Datei: LOADMODEL loads an OBJ or GLTF file. MODEL draws it at a position; MODEL_EX additionally rotates it about a freely chosen axis (ax, ay, az) by winkel degrees — scale and colour are compulsory there. MODEL_WIRES draws only the wireframe (good for fault-finding).
Erzeugen Standardformen ohne Datei. Mehr: Generate standard shapes with no file. More rings or segments mean a rounder shape, but also more computation.
TORUS ist ein Ring, KNOT ein verschlunge: TORUS is a ring, KNOT a twisted trefoil knot (a handsome demo object). MESH_HEIGHTMAP builds terrain out of a greyscale image: brightness becomes height — combined with GENTEX_PERLIN, a landscape comes about in two lines.
MODEL_TEXTURE legt ein Bild als Oberfläc: MODEL_TEXTURE lays an image onto the model as its surface. MODEL_TEXTURE_NORMAL adds a normal map — an extra map that fakes unevenness for the light (joints, rivets, bark) without the shape gaining any more triangles. It only takes effect with lighting switched on.
Geriggte Modelle (GLTF oder IQM) bringen: Rigged models (GLTF or IQM) bring animations with them — walking, running, waving. Drachenhauch loads them as a set and sets the pose you want each frame.
MODEL_LOAD_ANIMS lädt alle Animationen e: MODEL_LOAD_ANIMS loads all of a file's animations and gives a set. The three queries tell you how many there are, what they are called, and how many frames each has.
MODEL_ANIMATE setzt die Pose auf ein bes: MODEL_ANIMATE sets the pose to a particular frame (the counter wraps round by itself). MODEL_ANIMATE_BLEND mixes two animations: anteil 0.0 shows all of A, 1.0 all of B — so walking turns smoothly into running instead of switching abruptly.
oder weich zwischen Gehen (0) und Rennen: or smoothly between walking (0) and running (1):
Ohne Licht sind 3D-Objekte flache Farbfl: Without light, 3D objects are flat areas of colour. Drachenhauch brings physically based lighting (PBR) for up to four light sources. Important: a model has to be registered with MODEL_LIT, otherwise it stays unlit.
LIGHT_ENABLE schaltet die Beleuchtung ei: LIGHT_ENABLE switches lighting on (once, at the start). LIGHT_AMBIENT sets the ambient light that falls everywhere — without it, shaded sides are pitch black; the strength scales the colour (0.0 = off). MODEL_LIT registers a model for lighting.
Ein gerichtetes Licht scheint aus einer: A directional light shines onto the whole scene from one direction (the sun); a point light radiates in all directions from a position (a torch, a lamp). Both give a light number for changing them later.
Ändern ein bestehendes Licht zur Laufzei: Change an existing light at run time — the torch travels with the player, the sun turns to evening red, the light goes out.
MODEL_PBR bestimmt das Material: metalli: MODEL_PBR determines the material: metallic from 0.0 (plastic, wood) to 1.0 (chrome), roughness from 0.0 (mirror-smooth) to 1.0 (matt). MODEL_EMISSIVE makes a model glow of its own accord — together with a bloom shader that gives genuine neon.
Nebel, der mit der Entfernung zunimmt. E: Fog that thickens with distance. It hides the hard edge of the view distance and gives a scene depth at once. A density of 0.0 switches it off.
Umgebungslicht: LIGHT_ENV nimmt vereinfa: Environment light: LIGHT_ENV takes, in simplified form, two colours (sky above, ground below) — metals then reflect them. LIGHT_ENV_HDR instead loads a real HDR panorama and computes the reflections from it. SKYBOX additionally draws that environment as a visible background.
SHADOW_ENABLE schaltet Schlagschatten ei: SHADOW_ENABLE switches cast shadows on (a higher resolution means sharper edges and more computation). Shadows are cast by the first directional light; only models registered with MODEL_LIT cast and receive them. SHADOW_AREA sets how large the shadowed area is — too large makes the shadows coarse. SHADOW_TARGET moves that area, customarily onto the player.
Zeichnet ein Bild im Raum, das sich IMME: Draws an image in space that ALWAYS turns to face the camera. The classic trick for trees, sparks, smoke or health bars above enemies — an image instead of a model, and presentable from every direction.
Ein Mausklick zeigt auf einen Pixel – im: A mouse click points at a pixel — in space that corresponds to a ray. The PICK commands send that mouse ray out, the RAY_HIT commands one of your own choosing. All give the distance to the hit, or -1 if nothing was hit; the point of impact is therefore origin + direction · distance.
Prüfen gegen einen Hüllkörper (Quader, K: Test against a bounding volume (box, sphere) or against a model's actual triangles. For “which object did the player click?” you take the smallest non-negative result.
Prüfen gegen eine einzelne Fläche statt: Test against a single surface rather than a bounding volume — for floor tiles, wall panels or control surfaces floating freely in space. The four points of a quad must go ROUND in order (in a circle, not crosswise). It is hit from behind as well.
Dieselben Tests mit selbst gewähltem Str: The same tests with a ray of your own — for lines of sight (“can the guard see the player?”), shots, or ground contact. The direction need not be brought to length 1; the distance still comes back in world units.
Die Flächen-Tests mit eigenem Strahl – e: The surface tests with your own ray — for checking whether a projectile goes through a wall panel, say.
Wohin zeigt die Maus auf dem Boden? Dies: Where is the mouse pointing on the ground? These three project the mouse ray onto a horizontal plane — the foundation of any building or strategy game's controls. MOUSE_GROUND_HIT is FALSE when the ray does not meet the plane at all (looking at the sky).
Der Weg in beide Richtungen: WORLD_TO_SC: The route in both directions: WORLD_TO_SCREEN converts a 3D position into screen pixels — that is how you put a name plate or a health bar above a figure (for which you draw in ordinary 2D after the 3D part). SCREEN_TO_WORLD_DIR does the reverse, giving the viewing direction through a point on screen; the origin of that ray is the camera position.
3D ist mächtig, aber der Einstieg ist an: 3D is powerful, but getting started is more demanding than in 2D. Begin with a fixed camera and a few basic bodies on a grid (as in the picture above), then bring movement into the camera, and only afterwards feel your way towards models and lighting. For most 2D games, by the way, you do not need 3D at all.
