Mit Teil V tauchst du in die mitgeliefer: With Part V you dive into the modules that ship with Drachenhauch — ready-made toolkits for recurring game tasks. You pull each in with IMPORT (chapter “Importing modules”). First comes sprite: it turns a spritesheet into an animated figure with position, velocity, named animations, mirroring and collision — all things you would otherwise have to build by hand.
Dasselbe animierte Sprite zweimal: links: The same animated sprite twice: on the left normal, on the right mirrored horizontally — both scaled threefold.
Ein Spritesheet ist ein Bild mit mehrere: A spritesheet is one image holding several frames of equal size side by side. The hero picture here is 256×32 pixels and contains 8 frames of 32×32 — a whole walk animation.
Erzeugt ein SPRITE aus einem Spritesheet: Creates a SPRITE from a spritesheet. image is the whole sheet (loaded with LOADIMAGE), frame_breite × frame_höhe the size of a single frame. Drachenhauch divides the sheet into frames itself.
SPRITE_SET_POS setzt die Position. SPRIT: SPRITE_SET_POS sets the position. SPRITE_SET_VELOCITY prescribes a velocity in pixels per second — the sprite then carries on moving by itself at every SPRITE_UPDATE (independently of frame rate).
Eine Animation ist ein benannter Bereich: An animation is a named range of frames with a playback speed. You register it once and then start it by name.
SPRITE_ADD_ANIM registriert eine Animati: SPRITE_ADD_ANIM registers an animation from frame erster to letzter at fps frames per second. SPRITE_PLAY starts it as a loop. SPRITE_PLAY is safe to call every frame — if the animation is already running, nothing happens.
Spielt eine Animation genau einmal ab un: Plays an animation exactly once and stops on the last frame (for actions such as striking or jumping, which should not repeat endlessly).
Spiegelt das Sprite waagerecht (flipX) u: Mirrors the sprite horizontally (flipX) and/or vertically (flipY). Classic: the same walk animation for both directions, leftwards via flipX.
Skaliert die Darstellung. Wichtig: rein: Scales how it is drawn. Important: purely visual — the collision box stays at its original size (deliberately, for a pop effect when picking something up, say).
SPRITE_UPDATE schreibt Position und Anim: SPRITE_UPDATE advances position and animation — dt_ms is the time elapsed in milliseconds (a whole number), that is INT(DELTA() * 1000). SPRITE_DRAW draws the sprite at its position (camera-aware).
Liefert TRUE, wenn sich die Boxen zweier: Gives TRUE when the boxes of two sprites overlap (AABB collision). With it you test hits between player and enemy, projectile and target, and so on.

Lesen zurück, wo das Sprite steht und wi: Read back where the sprite stands and how large a single frame is — for letting the camera follow, say, or drawing a health bar above it.
Der Animationszustand: aktuelles Einzelb: The animation state: read or set the current frame, the name of the running animation, and whether an animation started with SPRITE_PLAY_ONCE has finished — the usual trigger for “back to idle after the strike”.
Überlappen sich zwei Sprites, trifft ein: Do two sprites overlap, does a sprite meet a rectangle (a platform, a zone), or does a point lie on it (a mouse click)? All three work with the sprite's bounding rectangle.
Färbt das Sprite ein – der klassische ku: Tints the sprite — the classic brief flash of red on a hit, or a green cast for poisoned enemies. SPRITE_TINT_CLEAR takes the tint off again.
Spritesheets musst du nicht von Hand mal: You do not have to paint spritesheets by hand: the pixel editor dhsprites that comes with Drachenhauch draws frames and animations and exports finished sheets (and even atlas manifests). That closes the circle from the artwork to the game.
Im sprite-Kapitel hast du Animationen vo: In the sprite chapter you switched animations by hand (IF vx <> 0 THEN "walk" ELSE "idle"). With many states — standing, walking, jumping, falling, attacking — that if-then quickly becomes unmanageable. The animfsm module takes it off your hands: you describe the states and transitions once in a file, set only a few parameters in the game (“speed”, say), and the state machine picks the right animation itself.
Die Zustandsmaschine wählt den Zustand:: The state machine picks the state: because the speed is high, “run” is playing — ANIM_FSM_STATE shows the current state.
Die Zustandsmaschine wird datengetrieben: The state machine is loaded, data-driven, from a .dhanim file (most conveniently drawn in the dhanim editor). It describes three things: states (each bound to a range of frames), parameters (values you set in the game) and transitions (conditions for when one state changes to another). A simple version with two states:
Übergänge prüfen Parameter mit Operatore: Transitions test parameters with operators such as gt (greater), lt (less), eq (equal). A from of "*" applies from EVERY state (“jumping is always possible”, say). With wait_finished a one-shot state only changes once its animation has finished.
ANIM_FSM_LOAD lädt und prüft die .dhanim: ANIM_FSM_LOAD loads and checks the .dhanim file and gives an ANIM_FSM (in its default state). ANIM_FSM_SETUP registers the frame ranges of all the states as animations of the sprite and starts the default state. You create the sprite with the sprite module as usual.
Setzt einen Parameter der Zustandsmaschi: Sets a parameter of the state machine. At the next ANIM_FSM_UPDATE the transitions decide the state on the basis of these values.
Feuert einen Trigger-Parameter (ein einm: Fires a trigger parameter (a one-off signal, “jump” for instance). It is evaluated once at the next UPDATE and then reset automatically.
Das Herzstück: schreibt die laufende Ani: The heart of it: advances the running animation, tests the transitions and changes the state where needed (along with its animation). dt_ms is the time elapsed in milliseconds. Gives TRUE when a change of state happened in this frame.
ANIM_FSM_STATE liefert den Namen des akt: ANIM_FSM_STATE gives the name of the current state (good for display, or for logic of your own). ANIM_FSM_FORCE forces a state with no conditions — handy for a reset or a respawn.
Im Spiel meldest du nur noch die Paramet: In the game you only report the parameters and call UPDATE — the constant switching of animations by hand falls away:
Neben Kommazahlen und Auslösern kennt di: Besides decimals and triggers, the state machine knows whole numbers and truth values as parameters — the number of jumps in a combination, say, or “is on the ground”.
Lesen einen Parameter zurück – nützlich: Read a parameter back — useful when fault-finding, if a transition does not fire: simply display the value the state machine actually sees.
Für eine Figur mit nur zwei Animationen: For a figure with only two animations, the simple IF from the sprite chapter is enough. As soon as there are many states with conditions (walk, jump, fall, land, strike …), animfsm keeps the code clean — and the visual editor dhanim makes designing the states child's play.
Ein Tween (von engl. „in-between“) ist e: A tween (from “in-between”) is a value that travels of its own accord from a starting value to an end value over a given time — smoothly rather than in jumps. With it you effortlessly animate a pop-up that flies in, a number that counts up, or a figure that springs elastically into view. You create the tween once and then ask it for its current value every frame; the module looks after the timing itself.
Sechs Tweens mit verschiedenen Easing-Ku: Six tweens with different easing curves, queried at the same moment — each has got a different distance (out_elastic even overshoots the target).
Erstellt einen einmaligen Tween, der in: Creates a one-off tween that runs from start to ende in dauer_ms milliseconds and then stops at the end value. easing determines the shape of the movement (see below; linear by default).
Endlos laufende Tweens. LOOP springt am: Tweens that run endlessly. LOOP jumps back to the start at the end (start→end, start→end …) — good for spinners. PINGPONG swings to and fro (start→end→start …) — good for an up-and-down bob. Neither is ever “finished”.
TWEEN_VALUE liefert den aktuellen Wert (: TWEEN_VALUE gives the current value (query it every frame). TWEEN_DONE is TRUE once a one-off tween has reached its end (always FALSE for LOOP and PINGPONG).
Hält einen Tween an, setzt ihn fort oder: Halts a tween, carries it on, or reverses its direction (a menu sliding back out, for instance).
Das Easing bestimmt, WIE sich der Wert z: The easing determines HOW the value travels between start and end. linear is even; the out_ variants start fast and slow down (good for things flying in); in_ is the reverse; inout_ combines both. Special curves give character: out_bounce bounces to a stop like a ball, out_elastic springs past the target and swings back. A selection:
– sanft an und ab (ideal für Wippen/Atme: — gently up and down (ideal for bobbing or breathing)
– hüpft am Ende aus wie ein Ball: — bounces to a stop like a ball
– federt über das Ziel hinaus und schwin: — springs past the target and swings back
Ein typisches Beispiel: ein Banner, das: A typical example: a banner that flies in from above and brakes gently at its destination:
TWEEN_PROGRESS liefert den Fortschritt v: TWEEN_PROGRESS gives the progress from 0.0 to 1.0 — unlike TWEEN_VALUE, which gives the actual value; with it you fill a loading bar, say. TWEEN_RESTART puts the run back to the beginning. TWEEN_EASINGS lists all the available easing kinds as text.
tween ist zeitbasiert: „bewege diesen We: tween is time-based: “move this value in 700 ms”. If instead you need a curve that you steer yourself through a parameter (a flight path along control points, say), look at the curves module — it supplies the pure curve functions with no timing of its own.
Oft soll etwas nach einer Weile passiere: Often something should happen after a while (“explode in 2 seconds”) or at intervals (“spawn an enemy every half second”). You could solve that with MILLIS and bookkeeping of your own — the timer module takes it off your hands. You give it a function and a time, and it calls the function at the right moment. COOLDOWN joins in as a one-line rate limiter. The module is purely logical — it needs no graphics window.
Die Funktionen, die ein Timer aufruft, ü: You pass the functions a timer calls as a FUNCREF (chapter “Functions and SUBs”) — that is, simply as the function name without brackets. Such callback functions take no parameters.
TIMER_AFTER ruft die Funktion fn einmali: TIMER_AFTER calls the function fn once after ms milliseconds. TIMER_EVERY calls it again and again every ms. Both give back a timer ID, with which you can query or cancel the timer later.
Muss einmal pro Frame (im Game-Loop) auf: Must be called once per frame (in the game loop) — only then are due callbacks actually run. The same pattern as INPUT_UPDATE() or GUI_UPDATE(). Without TIMER_UPDATE no timer fires.
Ein TIMER_EVERY feuert pro TIMER_UPDATE: A TIMER_EVERY fires at most once per TIMER_UPDATE — so there is no “catch-up pile-up” if the game stutters briefly. Outside a graphics loop you can also call TIMER_UPDATE in a loop of your own (with SLEEP).
TIMER_CANCEL bricht einen Timer über sei: TIMER_CANCEL cancels a timer by its ID (an ID that has already fired, or an unknown one, does no harm). TIMER_ACTIVE checks whether a timer is still running.
TIMER_COUNT liefert die Anzahl gerade la: TIMER_COUNT gives the number of timers currently running. TIMER_CLEAR discards all timers (and cooldowns) at once — handy on a scene change, so that no timers from the old scene fire afterwards.
COOLDOWN ist ein eigenständiges Mini-Wer: COOLDOWN is a self-contained little tool for “no more often than every X milliseconds”. It gives TRUE when the action is currently allowed (and then starts the block), otherwise FALSE. Each block is identified by a text ID of your choosing. Unlike the timers, COOLDOWN needs no TIMER_UPDATE — the check happens on the call.
Liefert TRUE, wenn seit dem letzten erla: Gives TRUE when at least ms have passed since the last permitted call with this id (and then notes the new moment), otherwise FALSE. Ideal for rate of fire, guarding against hit-sound spam, and the like.
höchstens alle 250 ms ein Schuss: one shot every 250 ms at most
Im Schnelltest unten zeigt sich die Wirk: The quick test below shows the effect: six rapid attempts, but with a 1000 ms block only the first gets through.
Nimm TIMER_AFTER/EVERY, wenn etwas zu ei: Use TIMER_AFTER/EVERY when something should happen of its own accord at a given moment (a callback). Use COOLDOWN when you want to allow an action you are already testing for less often (a limit). COOLDOWN is the shorter solution where it fits.
Funken, Feuer, Rauch, Explosionen, Regen: Sparks, fire, smoke, explosions, rain — all of these are many little dots that move by simple rules and then pass away. The particles module takes on that bookkeeping: a particle system (the emitter) produces many particles on demand, with randomly scattered velocities and lifetimes, moves them and fades them out. You only set the rules and say “emit N particles”.
Eine Funken-Fontäne im Glow-Modus mit Fa: A fountain of sparks in glow mode with a colour ramp from yellow to red — from an emitter with gravity.
Erzeugt einen Emitter an der Position (x: Creates an emitter at position (x, y) with sensible defaults. PARTICLE_SYSTEM_NEW plus PARTICLE_EMIT is already enough for visible sparks; all further settings are optional.
Mit den SET-Befehlen formst du den Effek: With the SET commands you shape the effect. Velocity and lifetime are given as ranges (min/max) — from which the system rolls a random value per particle, which makes the effect look natural.
VELOCITY legt die Streuung der Start-Ges: VELOCITY sets the spread of the starting velocities (pixels per second; a negative vy means upwards). GRAVITY is a constant acceleration — a positive gy pulls the particles downwards, so that a fountain forms.
LIFETIME bestimmt, wie lange (in ms) ein: LIFETIME determines how long (in ms) a particle lives, SIZE its size in pixels — both as a range.
COLOR ist die Startfarbe. Setzt du zusät: COLOR is the starting colour. If you also set COLOR_END, every particle moves from the starting colour to the end colour over its lifetime — fire from yellow to red, for instance.
MODE wählt die Darstellung: \"circle\",: MODE chooses how they are drawn: "circle", "pixel", "square", "streak" or "glow" (currently rendered identically to "circle" — a genuine additive blend mode for particles is not yet implemented with the present draw-recording model; for real additive glow, put BLEND_MODE("add") around the PARTICLE_DRAW calls). FADE = TRUE lets particles fade out with age.
Stößt sofort anzahl neue Teilchen aus. E: Emits anzahl new particles at once. Called a single time that gives an explosion; a few every frame gives a continuous stream (a fountain, a fire).
PARTICLE_UPDATE schreibt die Physik um d: PARTICLE_UPDATE advances the physics by dt_ms (milliseconds) and removes dead particles, PARTICLE_DRAW draws all the living ones (camera-aware), PARTICLE_COUNT gives their number.
Eine Fontäne im Game-Loop: A fountain in the game loop
So entsteht der Dauer-Effekt aus dem Bil: This is how the continuous effect in the picture above comes about — emit a few new particles every frame, then update and draw:
PARTICLE_SET_POS verschiebt die Quelle –: PARTICLE_SET_POS moves the source — that is how a plume of smoke hangs off a moving car, or a torch off the player. PARTICLE_CLEAR removes all existing particles at once (on a scene change, so that no sparks blow across from the last level).
Explosion: einmalig viele Teilchen mit R: Explosion: many particles at once, scattered in all directions. Smoke: slow, large, long-lived particles with no gravity and FADE on. Rain: a narrow x range, a strong positive gy, streak mode. There is also a particle editor of its own for trying the values out.
Drachenhauch bringt drei Physik-Module m: Drachenhauch brings three physics modules — choose as you need: physics is pure collision mathematics with no state of its own (you keep full control), while physics2d and physics3d are full physics engines that compute gravity, impacts and friction themselves. This chapter presents all three.
physics2d in Aktion: zehn Bälle fallen u: physics2d in action: ten balls fall under gravity, bounce and gather — all computed by the engine.
Das Modul physics besteht nur aus reinen: The physics module consists of pure functions only: they work something out and give a result back, without remembering anything. With them you test overlaps, measure distances or bounce a ball off a wall — you program the movement yourself. Ideal when you want lean, predictable control.
Liefern TRUE, wenn sich zwei Rechtecke b: Give TRUE when two rectangles, or two circles, overlap. PHYSICS_BOX_BOX is the fastest collision test there is — ideal as a player-hits-enemy test.
PHYSICS_DISTANCE misst den Abstand zweie: PHYSICS_DISTANCE measures the distance between two points, PHYSICS_LENGTH the length of a vector. (For plain “closer than” comparisons there is PHYSICS_DISTANCE2 without the square root — faster.)
NORM liefert die Anteile des auf Länge 1: NORM gives the components of the vector brought to length 1 (direction without speed). REFLECT mirrors a velocity vector off a surface with normal (nx, ny) — the classic “ball bounces off the wall”.
Es gibt außerdem PHYSICS_BOX_CIRCLE, PHY: There are also PHYSICS_BOX_CIRCLE, PHYSICS_POINT_BOX/CIRCLE and the ray tests PHYSICS_RAY_BOX/RAY_CIRCLE (for shots and lines of sight). All are pure functions — no state, no surprises.
Während physics nur rechnet, simuliert p: Where physics merely calculates, physics2d simulates a whole world: you create bodies, prescribe a gravity and call one simulation step per frame — the engine looks after falling, colliding, stacking and bouncing. Handy for sandboxes, stacking puzzles, or anything that should move believably. (It uses the well-proven Rapier physics engine.)
Bildschirm-Konvention: y zeigt nach UNTE: Screen convention: y points DOWNWARDS, and the default gravity is (0, 980) — so bodies fall downwards of their own accord. Box dimensions are half-extents (half the width and height).
PHYS2D_NEW erstellt eine Physik-Welt (mi: PHYS2D_NEW creates a physics world (with the default gravity pointing down). PHYS2D_SET_GRAVITY changes the gravity (gy = 0 for weightless, negative for upwards).
Fügen einen Körper hinzu und liefern sei: Add a body and give its ID. dynamisch = TRUE moves (falls, collides); FALSE is an immovable body (floor, wall). bounce (0..1) is the springiness. For the box, hw and hh are HALF the width and height.
Simuliert einen Zeitschritt von dt Sekun: Simulates a time step of dt seconds — call it once per frame with DELTA(). Only that makes anything move at all.
Lesen Position und Drehwinkel (Radiant): Read a body's position and angle of rotation (in radians) — with them you draw your sprite at the place the engine has computed (rotated via DRAWIMAGEROT with DEG(...)).
Im Game-Loop ist das Muster immer gleich: In the game loop the pattern is always the same: simulate a step, then draw every body at its current position. That is exactly how the picture above came about:
In die Simulation eingreifen: SET_VEL se: Intervening in the simulation: SET_VEL sets the velocity hard (a jump, a catapult), APPLY_IMPULSE adds a single push (an explosion, a blow), and the two getters read the current velocity — for playing an impact sound at high speed, say.
SET_POS versetzt einen Körper (Wiederein: SET_POS moves a body (respawning after death, a teleport). LOCK_ROTATION prevents it from turning — exactly what a player figure needs, which would otherwise topple at every touch.
Removes a body from the world, or counts those present. The numbers stay stable after a REMOVE — so a body number you have noted never points at a different body by accident.
Schaltet einen Körper zwischen statisch: Switches a body between static (immovable, like a wall) and dynamic (falls, collides, rolls). With it a structure stands still at first and collapses precisely when you want it to.
Turm steht statisch, bis der Ball ihn tr: the tower stands static until the ball hits it
Erst stellen, dann fallen lassen: Set it up first, then let it fall
Ein Stapel aus dynamischen Körpern begin: A stack of dynamic bodies starts to wobble and shuffle itself into place the moment the world runs — by the first throw it is standing crooked. So build it statically and switch the pieces to dynamic only on the hit: then it stands until it should not.
physics3d ist das Gegenstück in drei Dim: physics3d is the counterpart in three dimensions: the same idea, only with a z axis and 3D bodies. The bodies additionally have a spatial rotation (as a quaternion), which you use when drawing your 3D model. Together with the g3d module you can thus build 3D objects that fall, roll and stack physically.
Wie bei physics2d, nur mit drei Koordina: As with physics2d, only with three coordinates. PHYS3D_NEW creates the 3D world, ADD_BOX and ADD_SPHERE add bodies (dynamisch TRUE/FALSE), PHYS3D_STEP simulates a step.
Lesen die 3D-Position und die Drehung (a: Read a body's 3D position and its rotation (as a quaternion QX/QY/QZ/QW). You put position and rotation into a model matrix (the m3d module) and draw your 3D model at the simulated place with it.
Dieselben Eingriffe wie in 2D, nur mit d: The same interventions as in 2D, only with three axes. The gravity can be changed at any time — for a moon landing, underwater sections, or a gravity-reversal switch.
Mond statt Erde: the moon instead of the earth
Versetzen, entfernen, zählen – wie in 2D: Moving, removing, counting — as in 2D, and likewise with stable body numbers.
Der einfachste Treffer-Test überhaupt un: The simplest hit test there is, and available with no IMPORT: do two rectangles overlap? You give the top left corner plus the width and height of each. For most 2D games — shot hits enemy, player touches coin — that is exactly enough.
Schneiden sich zwei STRECKEN? Der klassi: Do two LINE SEGMENTS cross? The classic case for laser against wall, or line of sight against obstacle. The other two give the point of intersection — but only if there is one: otherwise NAN comes back, so ask PHYSICS_LINES_HIT first.
Liegt ein Punkt auf einer Strecke (mit e: Does a point lie on a segment (with a tolerance for click accuracy)? And does a circle meet a segment — ball against bat, projectile against wall?
Punkt in einem Dreieck, in einem beliebi: A point in a triangle, in any polygon, or in a circle. PHYSICS_POINT_POLY takes the corners as two arrays of the same length and works for inward-curving (concave) shapes as well — which makes irregular click areas and zone maps possible.
PHYSICS_RAY_CIRCLE schickt einen Strahl: PHYSICS_RAY_CIRCLE sends a ray against a circle (distance, or -1). The other two are the 3D counterparts of CIRCLE_CIRCLE and DISTANCE — sphere against sphere, and distance in space, without your having to set up a whole physics world.
Viele Objekte prüfen: die Broadphase: Testing many objects: the broad phase
Prüfst du jedes Objekt gegen jedes ander: If you test every object against every other, the work grows quadratically — with 500 projectiles that is already 125,000 comparisons per frame. The broad phase sorts the objects into a grid beforehand and gives only those pairs that come near each other at all.
Eine Broadphase anlegen und pro Frame ne: Create a broad phase and refill it each frame: clear it, then enter every circle (centre and radius). PHYSICS_BROAD_ADD gives the number under which the object appears in the pairs — enter them in the same order as your own object list and the mapping fits.
QUERY berechnet die möglichen Paare, dan: QUERY computes the possible pairs, and then you fetch them one at a time. The result is a PRE-SELECTION: the pairs are close together, and you still test the exact hit yourself (with PHYSICS_CIRCLE_CIRCLE, say) — only now for a few dozen instead of every combination.
Für simple Treffer-Abfragen und selbst g: For simple hit tests and movement you steer yourself, physics is enough (fast, predictable). If something should feel “real” — falling, stacking, bouncing — take physics2d or physics3d. You can mix the two: the engine for the world, physics mathematics for special cases of your own.
Spielwelten sind oft größer als der Bild: Game worlds are often larger than the screen. So that you show only a section — and let it scroll along when the figure walks — there is the camera module. It shifts and zooms the whole drawing: once a camera is set, your coordinates count as world coordinates, and the camera converts them to the screen. So you go on drawing “at world positions”, and the visible section follows the camera.
Eine 800×600-Welt, von der Kamera auf de: An 800×600 world, centred by the camera on the player (world position 400, 300) — the HUD bar at the top stays put (drawn with no camera).
Legt fest, welcher Welt-Punkt (x, y) obe: Determines which world point (x, y) lands at the top left of the screen, and optionally a zoom (1.0 = normal, 2.0 = twice the size and closer, 0.5 = more world visible). From here on all drawing coordinates are world coordinates.
Welt-Punkt (100,50) -> Bild oben links: world point (100,50) -> top left of the picture
Setzt die Kamera so, dass das Ziel (ziel: Sets the camera so that the target (ziel_x, ziel_y) lands at the centre of the screen — ideal for following the player figure. You usually give the picture width and height as SCREENWIDTH() and SCREENHEIGHT().
Schaltet die Kamera wieder aus (zurück z: Switches the camera off again (back to 0,0 and zoom 1). Important before drawing the HUD: score, lives and menus should stick fast to the screen and not scroll along.
Bildschirm zurück in die Welt rechnen: Converting the screen back into the world
Rechnen einen Bildschirm-Pixel zurück in: Convert a screen pixel back into a world coordinate — indispensable for finding out WHERE in the world the mouse pointer is (for clicking an object, say).
Lässt die Kamera kurz wackeln – ein klas: Makes the camera wobble briefly — the classic thump effect on hits or explosions. The strength is in world pixels, and the shake dies away by itself over dauer_ms (300 by default). You call it once; no per-frame code needed.
Das übliche Muster: am Frame-Anfang der: The usual pattern: follow the figure at the start of the frame, draw the world in world coordinates, then reset the camera for the HUD:
ab hier fester Bildschirm: fixed to the screen from here on
Die Kamera wirkt auf alle Welt-Zeichenbe: The camera acts on every world drawing command — BOX, CIRCLE, LINE, TEXT, DRAWIMAGE, DRAWTILEMAP, SPRITE_DRAW and PARTICLE_DRAW. So draw the text HUD deliberately AFTER CAMERA_RESET(), to stop it travelling along.
Lesen die aktuelle Kamera-Position und d: Read the current camera position and zoom back — after CAMERA_FOLLOW has drawn them along smoothly, say, or to save the state in a saved game.
Dreht die Weltansicht um die Bildschirmm: Rotates the view of the world about the centre of the screen — for an earthquake, a fall, or a game in which the world turns instead of the figure.
CAMERA_SET_ROTATION verschiebt, wohin ei: CAMERA_SET_ROTATION moves where an object is drawn — the objects themselves stay upright. A sprite that should turn with it needs the angle itself as well: DRAWIMAGEROT(bild, x, y, eigener_winkel + CAMERA_ROTATION()).
Die Drehung dreht Positionen, nicht Form: The rotation turns positions, not shapes
Setzt die 3D-Kamera über Kugelkoordinate: Sets the 3D camera by spherical coordinates: it looks at the target (zx, zy, zz) and stands at distance radius, turned by gier (yaw, horizontal) and nick (pitch, vertical, in degrees). It spares you the trigonometry when the camera should orbit an object.
Statt die Kamera hart auf den Spieler zu: Rather than setting the camera hard onto the player, you can let it follow smoothly: move the camera position a little way towards the target each frame (with MOVETOWARD or LERP, for instance). That gives a pleasant, slightly trailing feel instead of a rigid stickiness.
Das Modul input hast du bereits kennenge: You have already met the input module — in the chapter “Input” (Part IV), which dealt with keyboard, mouse and gamepad. It binds keys to named actions, so that your game logic stays independent of particular keys and can easily be remapped. What follows here is only a compact overview for looking up; the full introduction with examples is in that chapter.

– einmal pro Frame; liest den Tastenzust: — once per frame; reads the key state in (compulsory for PRESSED/RELEASED).
– TRUE, solange eine gebundene Taste geh: — TRUE as long as a bound key is held (movement).
– nur im Frame des Drückens TRUE (Sprung: — TRUE only in the frame of the press (a jump, a menu choice).
— TRUE in the frame of the release.
– Analogstick-Wert eines Gamepads (mit D: — the analogue stick value of a gamepad (with a dead zone).
Aktionen einmal binden, dann pro Frame I: Bind the actions once, then INPUT_UPDATE and query each frame:
INPUT_BOUND liefert die Tasten, die auf: INPUT_BOUND gives the keys bound to an action (for display in a key-binding menu). INPUT_UNBIND releases a single action, INPUT_RESET all of them — before loading a saved key mapping, for instance.
Wie viele Gamepads sind angeschlossen un: How many gamepads are attached and what they are called — for a “controller 1 connected” display, or for assigning them in multiplayer.
Die ausführliche Erklärung von INPUT_BIN: The full explanation of INPUT_BIND/UPDATE/HELD/PRESSED/RELEASED/AXIS, together with the direct keyboard and mouse commands (KEYPRESSED, MOUSEX/Y, MOUSEBUTTON …), is in the chapter “Input” (Part IV).
Menüs, Knöpfe, Schalter und Schieberegle: Menus, buttons, switches and sliders are needed by almost every game. The ui module offers them in what is called immediate mode: you do not create the controls in advance but simply call them every frame in the game loop. A button call draws the button AND returns straight away whether it has just been clicked. The module remembers the state (is the checkbox on? where is the slider?) by a text ID that you give each element.
Ein Einstellungs-Panel aus Immediate-Mod: A settings panel of immediate-mode widgets: a panel with a title, a label, a button, a checkbox and a slider.
Pflicht: Rufe am Ende jedes Frames UI_EN: Compulsory: call UI_END_FRAME() at the end of every frame — before FLIP(). Only that lets the module handle clicks and focus correctly. Forget it and the widgets do not respond.
UI_LABEL zeichnet einen Text. UI_PANEL z: UI_LABEL draws a text. UI_PANEL draws a rectangular background container with an optional title — nice for framing controls that belong together.
Zeichnet einen Knopf und liefert TRUE ge: Draws a button and gives TRUE in precisely the frame in which it is clicked. That is why it usually sits directly in an IF. Every button needs a unique id$.
Zeichnet ein Häkchen-Kästchen mit Beschr: Draws a tick box with a label and gives back its current state (TRUE/FALSE). The first time round it starts at default. Clicks toggle it — so you do not have to store the state yourself.
Zeichnet einen Schieberegler von min bis: Draws a slider from min to max and gives its current value (FLOAT). Ideal for volume, difficulty or other stepless settings.
Weitere Widgets nach demselben Muster: U: Further widgets on the same pattern: UI_PROGRESS (a progress bar), UI_TEXTFIELD (text entry with keyboard focus), UI_RADIO (option groups) and UI_TABLE (a table). All of them likewise use a text ID for their state.
Ein Einstellungs-Menü im Game-Loop: A settings menu in the game loop
Alle Widgets werden jeden Frame neu aufg: All the widgets are called afresh every frame — that is how the panel in the picture comes about. Do not forget UI_END_FRAME():
Fasst die dazwischen erzeugten Bedienele: Gathers the controls created in between into a frame with a title. Unlike in the gui module, no lasting window arises from this — it is purely a grouping for this frame.
Zu einer mit UI_TABLE gezeichneten Tabel: For a table drawn with UI_TABLE: which row is selected, set the selection, and was a column heading clicked (-1 = no)? The last of these is the basis for sorting by click.
Setzt den Inhalt eines Eingabefeldes von: Sets the contents of an entry field from the program's side — to pre-fill it, say, or to empty it after submitting.
Aussehen des ui-Moduls: The look of the ui module
Dieselben Farbschemata wie beim gui-Modu: The same colour schemes as in the gui module ("dark", "light", "retro", "contrast", "modern_dark", "modern_light"), plus individual colour roles for fine adjustment.
Maße statt Farben (Innenabstand, Eckenru: Dimensions rather than colours (padding, corner radius, row height). UI_RESET discards the remembered state of every control — necessary when you reuse the same element IDs in a different scene.
Das ui-Modul (Immediate-Mode) ist perfek: The ui module (immediate mode) is perfect for quick game menus and debug overlays: little code, nothing to set up in advance. If, on the other hand, you need persistent windows that can be moved and overlapped (as on a desktop), take the gui module from the next chapter.
Das gui-Modul ist das Gegenstück zum ui-: The gui module is the counterpart to ui: instead of controls rebuilt every frame it manages persistent windows with widgets — movable by the title bar, overlapping, with a z order and a close button, almost like a desktop. You build windows and widgets ONCE before the game loop; after that you only call GUI_UPDATE (handle mouse and keys) and GUI_DRAW (draw) per frame, and poll for events.
Ein verschiebbares gui-Fenster mit Titel: A movable gui window with a title bar, label, checkbox, slider and button (cyan theme).
Ein Fenster erstellst du mit GUI_WINDOW;: You create a window with GUI_WINDOW; the widgets take it as their first parameter and their coordinates are RELATIVE to the window's contents. Every constructor gives a handle (GUI_WINDOW or GUI_WIDGET) that you keep, in order to query it later.
Legt ein Fenster mit Titelleiste an (per: Creates a window with a title bar (movable with the mouse by that bar). Gives a GUI_WINDOW handle.
Fügen dem Fenster ein Text-Label bzw. ei: Add a text label or a button to the window (coordinates relative to the window). Both give a GUI_WIDGET handle.
Fügen eine Checkbox bzw. einen Schiebere: Add a checkbox or a slider. You poll their state later (see below).
GUI_UPDATE verarbeitet Maus und Tastatur: GUI_UPDATE handles mouse and keyboard (hover, click, window dragging, focus, z order) and must come BEFORE GUI_DRAW and the polling queries. GUI_DRAW draws every window from back to front.
GUI_CLICKED liefert TRUE im Frame, in de: GUI_CLICKED gives TRUE in the frame in which a button was clicked. GUI_CHECKED gives a checkbox's state, GUI_VALUE a slider's value. These queries come after GUI_UPDATE.
Eine Baumansicht zeigt hierarchische Dat: A tree view shows hierarchical data with expandable nodes — ideal for a level browser, a file and folder structure, or a scene-graph inspector.
GUI_TREE creates an empty tree view. GUI_TREE_ADD appends a node — parent = -1 for a root node, otherwise the id of an existing node. Gives the new node id (stable until GUI_TREE_CLEAR).
GUI_TREE_EXPAND klappt einen Knoten auf: GUI_TREE_EXPAND opens or closes a node (only expanded nodes show their children). GUI_TREE_LABEL reads a node's label text.
GUI_TREE_SELECTED liefert die id des vom: GUI_TREE_SELECTED gives the id of the node the user clicked (-1 = no selection). GUI_TREE_SET_SELECTED sets the selection programmatically, to pre-mark the level last opened, for instance.
Entfernt alle Knoten (z. B. um die Bauma: Removes every node (to refill the tree view with a newly loaded folder structure, say). It also resets the selection.
GUI_MENU baut die klassische Menüleiste: GUI_MENU builds the classic menu bar at the top of the window (“File”, “Edit”, …), GUI_CONTEXT a context menu that appears on a right click in the window. Both get their items through GUI_MENU_ITEM — and every item then behaves like a button: query it with GUI_CLICKED.
GUI_MENU fügt der Menüleiste des Fenster: GUI_MENU adds an entry with a dropdown to the window's menu bar (“File”, say). GUI_MENU_ITEM appends a clickable item to it, GUI_MENU_SEPARATOR a dividing line for grouping.
Legt ein Kontextmenü für das Fenster an: Creates a context menu for the window (it opens on a right click, with no title of its own in the menu bar). Items are added in the same way through GUI_MENU_ITEM and GUI_MENU_SEPARATOR.
Tabs teilen ein Fenster in mehrere Seite: Tabs divide a window into several pages, between which the user clicks at the top — handy for fitting many settings in without an enormous window. The tabs belong to the WINDOW (GUI_TABS), and individual widgets are then assigned to a page with GUI_SET_TAB.
GUI_TABS legt die Reiter des Fensters fe: GUI_TABS lays down the window's tabs (numbered from 0 in the order passed). GUI_SET_TAB assigns a widget to a page (-1 = visible on every page, the default).
GUI_ACTIVE_TAB liefert den Index der ger: GUI_ACTIVE_TAB gives the index of the page currently visible (it changes when the user clicks a tab). GUI_SET_ACTIVE_TAB changes the page programmatically.
Weitere Widgets: Spinner, Splitter, Text: Further widgets: spinner, splitter, text area, tooltip
Ein Zahlenfeld mit Auf/Ab-Pfeilen (und M: A number field with up and down arrows (and mouse-wheel support) — like GUI_SLIDER, but more compact and with exact entry rather than dragging. Read the value with GUI_VALUE.
Eine ziehbare Trennlinie zum Aufteilen e: A draggable divider for splitting a window into two areas (a tree view on the left, content on the right, say). orientierung$ = "v" (a vertical bar, draggable horizontally) or "h" (a horizontal bar, draggable vertically). You read the position with GUI_VALUE (relative to the window) and lay the two areas out yourself with it (via GUI_SET_BOUNDS, for instance).
Ein mehrzeiliges Eingabefeld (das einzei: A multi-line entry field (the single-line counterpart is GUI_TEXTINPUT). Reading and setting the text goes through the general GUI_TEXT and GUI_SET_TEXT commands.
Legt einen Hilfetext fest, der erscheint: Sets a help text that appears when the mouse lingers over the widget — it explains icons or terse labels without needing the space for a long label.
Eine Toolbar ist ein flacher, dekorative: A toolbar is a flat, decorative strip serving as a background for a row of icon buttons — the buttons themselves lie over it as widgets of their own.
GUI_TOOLBAR zeichnet nur den Streifen (s: GUI_TOOLBAR draws only the strip (it is not clickable itself). GUI_ICON_BUTTON is an ordinary button with an image (an IMAGE handle, from LOADIMAGE or GENTEX_COLOR for instance) instead of, or in addition to, text — query it with GUI_CLICKED as usual.
Tauscht das Icon eines bestehenden Butto: Swaps an existing button's icon (-1 removes it again) — for toggling a play/pause button between two icons, say.
Beide öffnen einen echten System-Dialog: Both open a real system dialogue and block until the user responds — so the following examples show how they are used, without an output box.
GUI_MESSAGE zeigt einen einfachen Hinwei: GUI_MESSAGE shows a simple notice dialogue with an OK button. GUI_CONFIRM asks OK/Cancel and gives TRUE/FALSE — for a “really quit?” safety question, say.
Macht den Fensterinhalt scrollbar (Mausr: Makes the window contents scrollable (mouse wheel plus scroll bar) when there are more widgets in it than fit the visible height — handy for long lists of options in a small window.
Auswahl-Widgets: Dropdown, Listbox, Radi: Selection widgets: dropdown, list box, radio
Für „eines aus vielen“ gibt es drei Bauf: For “one out of many” there are three shapes: the dropdown opens out and needs little room, the list box shows several entries permanently, and radio buttons are the classic variant when every possibility should stay visible. You pass the entries as a TUPLE or an ARRAY OF STRING in each case.
GUI_DROPDOWN legt eine aufklappbare Ausw: GUI_DROPDOWN creates an expandable selection. GUI_DROPDOWN_SELECTED gives the chosen index (from 0; -1 = nothing chosen), GUI_DROPDOWN_TEXT the text of the chosen entry. The opened popup draws over every other widget.
Sets the selection from the program's side (when loading a saved game, say), or replaces the entries entirely (a list of resolutions after a monitor change, for instance). After GUI_SET_DROPDOWN nothing is selected any more.
Wie das Dropdown, nur dauerhaft ausgekla: Like the dropdown, but permanently open: the list is always visible and scrolls when there are too many entries. Querying and pre-setting work identically (GUI_LISTBOX_SET_SELECTED, GUI_SET_LISTBOX).
Radioknöpfe derselben gruppe$ schließen: Radio buttons of the same gruppe$ exclude one another — click one and the others in the group go off. GUI_RADIO_SELECTED gives TRUE for the button currently chosen.
Eine Tabelle zeigt Zeilen und Spalten mi: A table shows rows and columns with a fixed header row — for high scores, an inventory, a server list. It can show far more than text: every cell carries colours of its own, an alignment and a KIND (text, image, tick, bar, button). Sorting, filtering, editing and multiple selection it brings with it.
GUI_TABLE legt eine leere Tabelle an. GU: GUI_TABLE creates an empty table. GUI_TABLE_HEADERS sets the column headings (ARRAY OF STRING), GUI_TABLE_COL_WIDTHS the column widths in pixels (ARRAY OF INTEGER). With no widths the table divides them evenly.
Beide Befehle wollen ein ARRAY, kein TUP: Both commands want an ARRAY, not a TUPLE. `GUI_TABLE_HEADERS(tab, ("a", "b"))` is refused with “ARRAY OF STRING expected”.
GUI_TABLE_ADD_ROW hängt EINE Zeile an (A: GUI_TABLE_ADD_ROW appends ONE row (ARRAY OF STRING) and gives its number. That is the usual route: tables are almost always filled in a loop — from a file, a database, the saved game.
GUI_TABLE_ROWS setzt alle Zeilen auf ein: GUI_TABLE_ROWS sets every row at once — the cells come as a TWO-DIMENSIONAL ARRAY OF STRING (row, column). GUI_TABLE_REMOVE_ROW removes a row (the selection moves with it), GUI_TABLE_CLEAR empties the table.
Die Spaltenzahl ist frei: Sie ergibt sic: The number of columns is free: it follows from the widest entry given. Rows shorter than the header are simply empty, longer ones widen the table — there is no order you have to keep to.
Jede Zelle hat einen Inhalt, zwei Farben: Every cell has a content, two colours, an alignment and a kind. The kinds are: text (the default), bild (an IMAGE, fitted into the cell), haken (a tick box — a click toggles it by itself), balken (progress, 0..1) and knopf (a button).
Inhalt einer einzelnen Zelle schreiben b: Write or read the contents of a single cell.
Farben je Zelle bzw. für eine ganze Zeil: Colours per cell, or for a whole row. -1 means “not set” and passes on to the next level: cell → row → zebra. That way ONE call colours a row and individual cells can still break ranks.
Art einer Zelle setzen (text/bild/haken/: Set a cell's kind (text/bild/haken/balken/knopf) and write or read its value: 0 or 1 for a tick, 0.0 to 1.0 for a bar.
Text liegt auf dem Balken: the text lies on the bar
Legt ein Bild in die Zelle – es wird ein: Puts an image into the cell — it is fitted in and the aspect ratio is kept. It sets the kind at the same time, so a second call is unnecessary.
Ausrichtung („links“, „mitte“, „rechts“): Alignment (“links”, “mitte”, “rechts”) for a cell or a whole column. Numbers belong right-aligned — otherwise they cannot be compared.
Auswahl und Hover liegen halbdurchsichti: Selection and hover lie semi-transparently OVER the cell areas. So a cell colour of your own no longer hides which row is currently chosen.
GUI_TABLE_SELECTED liefert die markierte: GUI_TABLE_SELECTED gives the selected row (-1 = none). GUI_TABLE_CLICKED gives the row hit ONLY in the frame of the click, otherwise -1; GUI_TABLE_CLICKED_COL gives the column with it — that is how you tell a click on the button in column 5 from one on the tick in column 4.
Markiert eine Zeile vom Programm aus; -1: Selects a row from the program's side; -1 clears the selection. A row number outside the table becomes -1 rather than throwing an error.
Auf `>= 0` prüfen, nicht bloß `IF GUI_TA: Test for `>= 0`, not merely `IF GUI_TABLE_CLICKED(tab) THEN`! With no click, -1 comes back — and -1 counts as true. The condition would be met in EVERY frame.
Ein Klick auf die Kopfzelle sortiert von: A click on the header cell sorts by itself, and a second reverses the direction. These commands do the same from the program's side, or read the state. A column < 0 lifts the sorting.
Sortiert wird ZAHLENWEISE, wenn beide Ze: Sorting is NUMERIC when both cells can be read as numbers, otherwise by text. Without that, a score column would put 100 before 9.
Filtert eine Spalte nach Teiltext, Groß-: Filters a column by substring, regardless of case; several columns act together. With GUI_TABLE_SET(tab, "filterzeile", 1) the header gains a row of entry fields for the user to type into.
Wie viele Zeilen sind gerade sichtbar, u: How many rows are visible at the moment, and which DATA row stands at view position i? With those you walk the table in the order it is displayed.
Alle Zeilennummern nach außen sind DATEN: Every row number given to the outside is a DATA row. Sorting and filtering do not rearrange the data — they only build a view over it. So a row number your program has noted still points at the same entry.
Mit GUI_TABLE_SET(tab, \"mehrfachauswahl: With GUI_TABLE_SET(tab, "mehrfachauswahl", 1), Ctrl+click adds or removes a row and Shift+click takes the whole range. Existing code that knows only GUI_TABLE_SELECTED runs unchanged — that remains the row last clicked.
Gibst du eine Spalte frei, öffnet ein Do: If you release a column for editing, a double click on a text cell opens an entry field in precisely that cell: Enter accepts, ESC withdraws, and a click elsewhere accepts as well. On opening, the whole content is selected, so the first keystroke replaces it. The two getters tell you which cell is currently being edited (-1 = none).
Benutzt dein Programm ESC zum Beenden, f: If your program uses ESC to quit, test `GUI_TABLE_EDITING_ROW(tab) < 0` first — otherwise the very key meant to withdraw an entry quits the program.
Ein Setter für alle Schalter der Tabelle: One setter for all the table's switches: zeilenhoehe, kopfhoehe, zebra, gitter, filterzeile, sortierbar, spalten_ziehbar, spalten_verschiebbar, feste_spalten, mehrfachauswahl. GUI_TABLE_GET reads them and additionally knows “spalten” (the number of columns). An unknown key is an error that lists the valid ones.
Ist „spalten_verschiebbar“ gesetzt, läss: If “spalten_verschiebbar” is set, a header cell can be dragged sideways. Here too the DATA stay untouched: COL_AT tells which data column stands at a display position, COL_POS the reverse.
Klick und Zug am Kopf sind dieselbe Gest: A click and a drag on the header are the same gesture. Only on release is it settled which was meant: without movement it sorts, with movement it moves the column.
Zwei Bedienelemente, die aussehen wie an: Two controls that look like those on a piece of equipment: the toggle switch instead of a tick, the knob instead of a slider. Both are most at home in the sculpted glass themes.
Ein Kippschalter – dieselbe Aufgabe wie: A toggle switch — the same job as a checkbox, only drawn as a switch. Its state through GUI_CHECKED and GUI_SET_CHECKED.
Ein Drehregler: senkrecht ziehen dreht i: A knob: dragging vertically turns it. Its value through GUI_VALUE and GUI_SET_VALUE — as with the slider, only more compact and more fitting on a mixing desk.
Macht aus einem rechteckigen Knopf einen: Turns a rectangular button into a round one — for transport keys (play/stop/record) and anything meant to look like equipment.
Legt eine eigene Grafik unter eine ganze: Puts artwork of your own under a whole kind of widget (“button”, “panel” …). The image is stretched as a nine-slice: the corners stay, the edges stretch — so one graphic fits every size.
Anzeige-Widgets: Fortschritt, Bild, Tren: Display widgets: progress, image, divider, group, panel
Ein Fortschrittsbalken. Seinen Füllstand: A progress bar. You set how full it is with GUI_SET_VALUE, as a fraction between 0.0 and 1.0 — while loading, say, or for a health bar.
Zeigt ein per LOADIMAGE geladenes Bild i: Shows an image loaded with LOADIMAGE in the window (scaled to w×h) — a preview or a logo, say. GUI_SET_IMAGE swaps the image later.
Drei Ordnungshelfer ohne eigene Funktion: Three tidying aids with no function of their own: GUI_SEPARATOR draws a dividing line, GUI_GROUPBOX frames related widgets with an inset title, GUI_PANEL is a plain background area. All three are purely decorative — the widgets inside them stay independent.
Reserviert eine Fläche im Fenster, in di: Reserves an area in the window into which YOU draw — for a preview, a chart or a minimap. The four getters give the area in SCREEN coordinates (the window is movable, after all); draw after GUI_DRAW and clip to the area yourself.
Statt jeden Frame GUI_CLICKED abzufragen: Rather than querying GUI_CLICKED every frame, you can assign a function to a widget — GUI_UPDATE then calls it itself. That is the pattern the form designer dhform uses as well.
GUI_ON_CLICK feuert bei Knopfdruck, GUI_: GUI_ON_CLICK fires on a button press, GUI_ON_CHANGE on a change of value (slider, checkbox, dropdown). You pass the function as a FUNCREF — that is, without brackets — and it takes no parameters.
Vier weitere Callbacks: Maus betritt bzw: Four further callbacks: the mouse enters or leaves a widget, an entry field gains or loses the keyboard. They fire on the EDGE — once at the transition, not in every frame while the mouse stays put. GUI_ON_BLUR is where one validates an entry.
Fokus bekommen nur Widgets, die Tastatur: Only widgets that accept the keyboard receive focus (text field, text area, number field). Hover and leave work for any clickable widget.
Alles, was du beim Aufbau festgelegt has: Everything you settled while building can be changed later: position, visibility, colour, font — or the widget removed entirely. That is the basis for interfaces that react to the state of play.
Verschiebt und/oder skaliert ein Widget: Moves and/or resizes a widget within its window; the getters give the current placement (relative to the window's contents).
Unsichtbare Widgets werden weder gezeich: Invisible widgets are neither drawn nor clicked. Greyed-out ones (not enabled) stay visible but do not respond — the right way to do “only selectable once …”.
GUI_DESTROY entfernt ein Widget endgülti: GUI_DESTROY removes a widget for good (its handle stays valid but points at nothing — further accesses report as much). GUI_KIND gives the kind as text ("button", "slider", …), GUI_HOVERED whether the mouse is currently over it.
Setzen den Zustand von Programmseite: GU: Set the state from the program's side: GUI_SET_VALUE the slider or progress value, GUI_SET_CHECKED a checkbox's tick — when loading settings from a saved game, for instance.
Übersteuert Farbe und Schrift für EIN Wi: Overrides colour and font for ONE widget. Permitted as rolle$ are "bg", "fg", "border" and "accent"; the font is a handle from LOADFONT.
Bindet ein Widget an Fensterkanten, dami: Anchors a widget to the window's edges, so that it travels or grows when the window is enlarged. kanten$ is a combination of "l", "r", "t", "b" — two opposite edges ("lr") stretch the widget, a single one ("r") sticks it to that edge.
Knopf bleibt unten rechts: the button stays at the bottom right
GUI_FOCUS setzt den Tastatur-Fokus (z. B: GUI_FOCUS sets the keyboard focus (onto an entry field when opening, say). GUI_HIT_TEST gives the topmost visible widget at a point on screen, or -1 — that is how one builds a selection of one's own by mouse click.
Setzt bzw. liest Position und Größe eine: Set or read a window's position and size on screen — to save its placement in a saved game and restore it next time, for instance.
Schalten Verschieben an der Titelleiste,: Switch dragging by the title bar, the close button and the resize grip at the bottom right off or on. A pinned window (movable = FALSE) suits a status display that should always stay in the same place.
Grenzen für das Ziehen am Größengriff –: Limits for dragging the resize grip — so that a window cannot become so small that its widgets no longer fit.
Schaltet Titelleiste und Rahmen ab. Das: Switches off the title bar and frame. The window is then borderless and its contents begin at the top left — so a form fills the whole program window without looking like a gui window at all.
GUI_WINDOW_VISIBLE blendet ein Fenster a: GUI_WINDOW_VISIBLE hides a window and shows it again (an inventory on a key press, say). GUI_WINDOW_CLOSED is TRUE as soon as the user has clicked the X. GUI_WINDOW_DESTROY removes the window along with its widgets.
Zählt die Widgets eines Fensters und lie: Counts a window's widgets and gives them one at a time — with which an interface can be walked through without having kept every handle separately (to grey everything out, for instance).
Schaltet auf ein fertiges Farbschema um:: Switches to a ready-made colour scheme: "dark" (the default), "light", "retro" (green on black), "contrast" (high contrast), "modern_dark" and "modern_light". The two modern presets additionally bring rounded corners, window shadows and a taller title bar.
Einzelne Farbrollen ändern – etwa \"acce: Change individual colour roles — "accent" (highlight), "win_bg", "title_bg", "text_fg", "widget_bg", "widget_border", for instance. GUI_THEME is the older name for GUI_THEME_SET.
Maße statt Farben: \"title_h\" (Titellei: Dimensions rather than colours: "title_h" (title bar height), "pad" (padding), "corner_radius" (corner rounding, 0 = square), "shadow" (window shadow), "slider_h", "check_size".
Ein benannter Style bündelt Eigenschafte: A named style bundles properties ("bg", "fg", "border", "accent", "font", "font_size") and can be applied to any number of widgets — like a stylesheet. GUI_STYLE_SET can be called repeatedly and adds to the style.
Ein ganzes Fenster samt Widgets lässt si: A whole window along with its widgets can be saved as JSON and restored later. That is precisely the format the form designer dhform writes into its .dhform files — so you can load an interface built there directly.
GUI_SAVE schreibt ein Fenster in eine Da: GUI_SAVE writes a window to a file, GUI_LOAD rebuilds it from that and gives the new window handle. If event-handler names are stored (dhform), GUI_UPDATE calls the matching functions automatically.
Dasselbe ohne Datei: als String. Praktis: The same without a file: as a string. Handy for saving an interface along with a saved game, or for sending it over the network.
Räumt alles ab: alle Fenster, Widgets un: Clears everything away: all windows, widgets and styles. The clean start on a scene change, so that no windows of the old scene are left standing.
Aufbau einmal, Verarbeitung im Loop – so: Build once, handle it in the loop — that is how the movable window in the picture comes about:
Das gui-Modul kann noch viel mehr: weite: The gui module can do a good deal more: further widgets (dropdown, table, radio, progress bar, entry field), manipulation at run time (moving, showing and hiding, destroying), saving and loading whole interfaces, and even callback functions instead of polling. There is a form designer of its own for it (dhform).
ui (voriges Kapitel): schnelle, jeden Fr: ui (the previous chapter): quick menus redrawn every frame — ideal for a main menu or a debug overlay. gui (this chapter): real, movable windows that persist — ideal for tools, editors, or more elaborate interfaces within a game.

The chart module draws finished charts: pies and rings for proportions, bars for comparisons, lines and areas for trends, plus analogue dials, bars and LED strings for a single reading. You create a chart once, feed it data and call CHART_DRAW each frame — the module looks after the axes, labels, legend, colours and the mouse.
Vier der sechs Diagrammarten nebeneinand: Four of the six kinds of chart side by side: pie, bar, line, and a dial with colour zones.
Welche Art du bekommst, entscheidet der: Which kind you get is decided by the first parameter of CHART_NEW. Three of them show a whole data series, three a single value:
kuchen / donut – Anteile an einem Ganzen: kuchen / donut — proportions of a whole. “donut” is the same pie with a hole in the middle.
balken – Vergleich von Kategorien; wahlw: balken — comparing categories; vertical or horizontal, grouped or stacked, as you choose.
linie / flaeche – Verläufe über die Zeit: linie / flaeche — trends over time. With a sliding window, for live values such as the frame rate too.
tacho – Rundskala mit Zeiger und Farbzon: tacho — a round scale with a needle and colour zones, like a rev counter.
leiste – liegende oder stehende Leiste m: leiste — a horizontal or vertical bar with a travelling marker (fill level, loading bar).
led – eine Kette diskreter Zellen, die b: led — a string of discrete cells that light up as far as the value (a level meter).
Die einwertigen Arten (tacho, leiste, le: The single-value kinds (tacho, leiste, led) set their orientation to “waagerecht” themselves — the default “senkrecht” is right only for bar charts.
Legt ein Diagramm an und liefert ein CHA: Creates a chart and gives a CHART handle. The rectangle given is in screen coordinates — the chart later draws itself exactly there.
Zeichnet das Diagramm – in den Game-Loop: Draws the chart — into the game loop, after CLS and before FLIP. The module's only command that needs a window; everything else computes without SCREEN as well.
Lässt die Werte weich nachziehen, wenn „: Lets the values follow along smoothly when “animation” is set. Without animation you do not need the call — CHART_DRAW then draws the real values directly.
Verschiebt bzw. skaliert das Diagramm na: Moves or resizes the chart after the fact — handy when the window size changes.
Für ein Diagramm mit EINER Datenreihe –: For a chart with ONE data series — the normal case with pies and bars — CHART_ADD is enough. Every call appends a category.
Fügt eine Kategorie mit Namen und Wert h: Adds a category with a name and a value and gives its index. With no colour given, the chart takes the next colour from its palette.
Farbe 0 ist SCHWARZ, nicht „nimm die Pal: Colour 0 is BLACK, not “take the palette”. If you want the palette, leave the argument out or pass -1.
Setzt den EINEN Wert eines Tachos, einer: Sets the ONE value of a dial, a bar or an LED string. For those kinds this is the right command — CHART_ADD creates categories and leaves the needle at 0.
Sobald du zwei Kurven vergleichen oder B: As soon as you want to compare two curves or group bars, you need named series. CHART_SERIES creates one and gives its index; every further command addresses the series by that index.
Legt eine Datenreihe an und liefert ihre: Creates a data series and gives its index (0, 1, 2 …). The name goes into the legend.
Setzt alle Werte einer Reihe auf einmal: Sets all a series' values at once (ARRAY OF FLOAT or TUPLE) — the quickest way when the numbers are already to hand.

Ein Spiel besteht aus mehreren Abschnitt: A game consists of several sections: the main menu, the game itself, a pause screen, game over. The scene module helps you switch cleanly between such states. It manages a stack of scenes (each with a name) and gives every scene a little data store of its own — for score and lives, say. Your game loop thus stays readable: you only look at which scene is on top at the moment, and draw accordingly.
Es gibt zwei Arten zu wechseln. SCENE_SW: There are two ways of switching. SCENE_SWITCH replaces the whole stack — a final change with no way back (menu → game). SCENE_PUSH puts a scene ON TOP without losing the one beneath (a pause over the running game); SCENE_POP takes it away again and makes the one below active once more.
SCENE_SWITCH wirft den Stapel weg und st: SCENE_SWITCH throws the stack away and starts at name$. SCENE_PUSH puts name$ on top (the old scene is kept). SCENE_POP removes the topmost one and makes the previous one active.
Pause schließen -> zurück ins Spiel: close pause -> back into the game
SCENE_CURRENT liefert den Namen der ober: SCENE_CURRENT gives the name of the topmost (active) scene (or "" for an empty stack), SCENE_DEPTH the number of scenes on the stack. Your game loop branches on SCENE_CURRENT.
Jede Szene hat ihren eigenen Datenspeich: Every scene has a data store of its own (by text key). There you put values that concern only that scene — the score in the “playing” state, say. Important: a scene freshly created by PUSH or SWITCH starts with an EMPTY store; the store of a scene underneath survives a PUSH and POP.

Lesen den Wert zurück. Fehlt der Schlüss: Read the value back. If the key is missing, the type's default comes back (0.0, the empty text, FALSE).

SWITCH for a genuine change with no way back (menu → game → game over). On a scene change you should also clear away any running timers (TIMER_CLEAR, chapter “timer”).
Highscores, Fortschritt, Einstellungen –: High scores, progress, settings — much should survive the game being closed. The save module makes that comfortable: you create a save, set named values in it (numbers, texts, truth values) and write it to a file. Next time you start, you load the file back. Behind the scenes it is all JSON, but you need not concern yourself with that — you work only with key and value (much like the scene data, only permanent).
SAVE_NEW erzeugt einen leeren Save. SAVE: SAVE_NEW creates an empty save. SAVE_LOAD_OR_NEW is the usual route at program start: if the file exists it is loaded, otherwise you get an empty save (no error). SAVE_EXISTS checks whether a file is there. (SAVE_LOAD loads strictly and throws if the file is missing.)

Liefert immer einen Wert: Fehlt der Schl: Always gives a value: if the key is missing (or the type does not fit), default comes back. Just right for optional values, such as a high score that does not yet exist.
Für Versionierung deiner Speicherstände: For versioning your saved games there are SAVE_VERSION(s) and SAVE_SET_VERSION(s, n). With them you recognise an old format on loading and can convert it gently, instead of foundering on the changed structure.
Ein klassisches Beispiel: beim Start den: A classic example: load the high score at the start (or 0), compare at the end of play, and write anew only on a record.
... Spiel läuft, am Ende steht score fes: ... the game runs, and at the end score is fixed ...
Neben ganzen Zahlen und Text speichert e: Besides whole numbers and text, a slot also stores decimals and truth values — play time, volume, whether the tutorial has run.
Mit Ersatzwert lesen bzw. prüfen, ob ein: Read with a fallback, or check whether a value has been stored at all. That is the clean way to deal with older saved games in which a value added later is still missing.
SAVE_KEYS liefert alle gespeicherten Sch: SAVE_KEYS gives all the stored keys as an array (handy for a debugging overview), SAVE_DELETE removes a single value, SAVE_CLEAR empties the whole slot — for “reset progress”, say.
Für Spielstände mit ein paar benannten W: For saved games with a few named values, save is just right — simple, and with a version field. If you need arbitrarily nested data structures (lists, objects within objects), the json module (Part V) is more flexible. save is at bottom a comfortable layer on top of JSON for the commonest case.
Wie findet ein Gegner den Weg zum Spiele: How does an enemy find its way to the player when walls are in between? The astar module answers exactly that: on a tile grid it finds the shortest route from A to B around the obstacles (with the well-known A* algorithm). You create a grid, mark the walls, call the search — and read the path found out step by step.
A* in Aktion: der kürzeste Pfad (gelb) v: A* in action: the shortest path (yellow) from the start (green) to the goal (red) runs diagonally and around the L-shaped wall.
ASTAR_NEW erstellt ein Gitter (anfangs ü: ASTAR_NEW creates a grid (passable everywhere to begin with) and gives an ASTAR_GRID. ASTAR_SET_WALL makes a tile impassable, ASTAR_IS_WALL asks whether a tile is a wall.
Switches diagonal movement on or off. By default the path runs only orthogonally (up/down/left/right); with TRUE it may go diagonally as well, which usually gives shorter, more natural routes.
Sucht den kürzesten Weg von (sx, sy) nac: Finds the shortest route from (sx, sy) to (ex, ey) and stores it internally. Gives TRUE if a route exists, otherwise FALSE (the goal is unreachable).
Nach erfolgreicher Suche liest du den Pf: After a successful search you read the path out: PATH_LEN is the number of waypoints (start AND goal included), PATH_X and PATH_Y the coordinates of waypoint idx. That is how you lead an enemy along tile by tile.
Der Pfad enthält Start- UND Zielpunkt. B: The path contains both the start AND the goal. For a step to an immediate neighbour, ASTAR_PATH_LEN is therefore 2. So you take an enemy's first step from index 1 (index 0 is its current position).
Typisch lässt du die Suche nur ab und zu: Typically you run the search only now and then (not every frame — that costs) and then move the enemy along the waypoints. Sketch:

Gitter einstellen und abfragen: Setting up and querying the grid
Größe abfragen, eine Mauer wieder begehb: Ask the size, make a wall passable again (the counterpart to ASTAR_SET_WALL — when a door opens, say), or remove every wall at once.
Die Schätzfunktion bestimmt, wie der Weg: The heuristic determines how the route is searched: "manhattan" (horizontal and vertical only), "euclid" (as the crow flies) or "chebyshev" (diagonals cost the same). With ASTAR_SET_DIAGONAL_COST you set what a diagonal step costs — 1.4 corresponds roughly to the true length and looks the most natural.
Was hat der gefundene Weg gekostet (Summ: What did the route found cost (the sum of the steps, with diagonals counting more)? With it you compare routes — which of three enemies reaches the player soonest, for instance. ASTAR_CLEAR_PATH discards the result.
Das astar-Gitter denkt in Kacheln (0, 1,: The astar grid thinks in tiles (0, 1, 2 …), your game world in pixels. Convert between the two: kachel = pixel \ kachelgröße, and back pixel = kachel * kachelgröße. Often the grid matches your tile map exactly (next chapter).
Größere Level malt man nicht im Code, so: Larger levels are not painted in code but in a map editor. The tiled module loads maps in the widespread Tiled format (as JSON) — whether you made them in the Tiled program or in the dhtilemap editor that ships with Drachenhauch. A map consists of one or more layers of tiles, plus optional object layers for spawn points and zones. Every tile can carry properties of its own (“solid” or “spike”, say).
Eine geladene Tiled-Karte (30×10 Kacheln: A loaded Tiled map (30×10 tiles): ground, floating platforms and coins — drawn via TILED_TILE_AT.
Karte laden & Maße: Loading a map, and its dimensions
Lädt eine Tiled-Karte (JSON) und liefert: Loads a Tiled map (JSON) and gives a TILED_MAP. The tileset images named in the map file are found relative to the map.
WIDTH/HEIGHT liefern die Kartengröße in: WIDTH and HEIGHT give the map size in tiles, TILE_WIDTH and TILE_HEIGHT the pixel size of a tile. With them you convert between tile and pixel coordinates.
TILED_TILE_AT liefert die GID (Kachelnum: TILED_TILE_AT gives the GID (tile number) at position (tx, ty) of a layer — 0 means “empty”. TILED_TILE_SET writes a tile (gid 0 deletes it) — useful for removing a collected coin from the map, for instance.
Zum Zeichnen läufst du über alle Kacheln: To draw, you walk over all the tiles, fetch the GID and stamp the matching section of the tileset image — which is exactly what produces the picture above:
Lesen eine im Editor gesetzte Eigenschaf: Read a property of a kind of tile set in the editor (by its GID). That is how you mark solid tiles with “solid” = TRUE, or coins with “pickup” = TRUE, and query it in the game.
Neben Kacheln können Karten Objekte enth: Besides tiles, maps can contain objects — points or rectangles with a name, a type and properties of their own: spawn points, triggers or zones, for instance. They live in object layers and are queried by their layer name.
TILED_OBJECT_COUNT liefert die Anzahl de: TILED_OBJECT_COUNT gives the number of objects in an object layer; with the other TILED_OBJECT_ functions you read out each object's position, name, type and properties — for creating enemies at the places set in the editor, say.
... über die n Objekte laufen und Gegner: ... walk over the n objects and place enemies ...
Für Editor- oder Generierungs-Aufgaben g: For editor or generation tasks there are bulk operations: TILED_FILL_RECT (fill a rectangle), TILED_REPLACE (swap one GID for another), TILED_COUNT_GID (count) and TILED_FLOOD_FILL (bucket fill) — they change many tiles in one call.
Eine Tiled-Karte besteht aus mehreren Eb: A Tiled map consists of several layers — ground, decoration, collision, plus object layers. These commands walk through them without your having to write the names into the program.
Zählen, benennen und suchen. TILED_LAYER: Count, name and search. TILED_LAYER_INDEX gives the number for a name (-1 if there is none), TILED_LAYER_TYPE tells "tilelayer" from "objectgroup".
Größe einer Ebene in Kacheln – nicht jed: The size of a layer in tiles — not every layer has to be as large as the map.
Neben den Kacheln kann eine Karte OBJEKT: Besides the tiles, a map can contain OBJECTS — set in the editor as rectangles or points. With them the level designer determines where the player starts, where enemies appear, or which area springs a trap, without your writing coordinates into the program.
Lesen die Eigenschaften eines Objekts ei: Read the properties of an object in an object layer (together with TILED_OBJECT_COUNT and TILED_OBJECT_X). You assign name and type in the editor.
Eigene Eigenschaften eines Objekts, im E: An object's own properties, freely assigned in the editor — how much damage a trap does, say, or which level a door leads to. The game balance thus sits in the map rather than in the source.
Dasselbe für einzelne KACHEL-Arten: Im T: The same for individual KINDS of tile: in the tileset you set properties per tile (solid, damage, friction …), and here you read them out by the tile number (gid).
Eine Karte kann mehrere Tilesets benutze: A map can use several tilesets. Each brings an image file and begins at a particular tile number (firstgid). If you want to draw yourself, then for a given gid you look for the tileset with the largest firstgid that is still less than or equal to that gid.
Du musst Tiled-Karten nicht von Hand als: You do not have to write Tiled maps as JSON by hand: the dhtilemap editor that ships with Drachenhauch paints tiles, manages layers and properties, and saves precisely the format TILED_LOAD reads. For testing ground and walls against it, the tile_collide module (next chapter) is a perfect fit.
Eine Tiled-Karte (voriges Kapitel) zeich: A Tiled map (previous chapter) does not test itself for collisions. The tile_collide module supplies exactly the missing piece: it pushes a rectangular figure against a map's solid tiles and stops it cleanly at floors and walls — the foundation of any platformer movement. So you do not have to write the collision logic yourself.
Der rote Spieler-Block ist über TILE_SWE: The red player block has fallen via TILE_SWEEP_Y and landed exactly on the row of ground tiles.
Bewegen mit Kollision: die Achsen-Sweeps: Moving with collision: the axis sweeps
Der Trick: Man bewegt nicht in beide Ric: The trick: you do not move in both directions at once but separately — horizontally first, then vertically. Each sweep takes the current box and a desired displacement and gives the NEW, corrected position plus the information whether something was hit on the way.
Verschiebt die Box (x, y, w, h) um dx bz: Moves the box (x, y, w, h) by dx or dy and stops it at solid tiles. Each gives a tuple (new position, hit): element 0 is the corrected x or y position, element 1 is TRUE when a wall was in the way.
Prüft, ob die Kachel an (tx, ty) fest is: Checks whether the tile at (tx, ty) is solid (tile coordinates). Handy for queries of your own. Tiles OUTSIDE the map count as solid — so the player cannot fall out of the level without your having to catch it separately.
Das Modul kennt zwei Wege, „fest“ zu bes: The module knows two ways of deciding what is “solid”. If any kind of tile in the tileset has a solid property (set in the editor), then precisely those count as solid — so you can mix solid ground and passable decoration in the same layer. If the tileset has no solid property at all, every occupied tile (GID > 0) counts as solid — and then you customarily make a “collision” layer of your own containing only walls.
Faustregel: Für gemischte Ebenen (Boden: Rule of thumb: for mixed layers (solid ground, passable grass decoration) set the solid flag on the solid tiles in the editor. For a pure wall layer the convention “GID > 0 = solid” suffices, with no properties at all.
Plattformer-Bewegung im Game-Loop: Platformer movement in the game loop
Das volle Muster: horizontale Eingabe sw: The full pattern: sweep the horizontal input, then add gravity to the vertical velocity and sweep vertically. If the y sweep meets ground, the figure has landed (allow jumping again).
... draw the map and the player ...
Welche Kachel liegt an dieser PIXEL-Posi: Which tile lies at this PIXEL position? Gives the tile number (gid) — handy for questions such as “is the figure standing on ice?” or “is there water beneath it?”, without your dividing by the tile size yourself.
