tiled lädt das Level, tile_collide lässt: tiled loads the level, tile_collide lets the player walk on it, and the controller module (next chapter) wraps jumping comforts such as coyote time and a jump buffer around the top. Together they make a complete foundation for a jump-and-run.
Mit tile_collide kannst du eine Figur üb: With tile_collide you can move a figure over a map. The controller module puts a ready-made, good-feeling platformer control on top of it: running, jumping, gravity — and above all the little comforts that make a jump-and-run pleasant (coyote time, jump buffer, variable jump height). Each frame you only feed in the input and call an update; the module looks after the physics and the collision.
Der Character-Controller ist auf die Kar: The character controller has fallen onto the map and is standing — CHAR_ON_GROUND is TRUE.
Anlegen & der Drei-Schritt-Loop: Creating it, and the three-step loop
Erzeugt einen Character-Controller mit S: Creates a character controller with a starting position and a collision size. Gives a CHAR_CONTROLLER handle.
CHAR_SET_INPUT übergibt die Eingabe dies: CHAR_SET_INPUT passes this frame's input: achse_x is -1/0/+1 (left/right), sprung_gedrückt the single press, sprung_gehalten the holding (for variable jump height). CHAR_UPDATE then works out the velocity, collides with the map and sets the position. Nothing more is needed per frame.
Liefern Position und Geschwindigkeit der: Give the figure's position and velocity — with them you draw your sprite in the right place.
Sagen, ob die Figur gerade auf dem Boden: Tell you whether the figure is currently standing on the ground or up against a wall — useful for choosing the animation (stand/walk/fall) or for wall jumps.
Die Voreinstellungen fühlen sich schon g: The defaults already feel good, but you can adjust everything. Three of them make the difference between “awkward” and “fluid”:
– kurz nach dem Verlassen einer Kante da: — shortly after leaving a ledge you may still jump (it forgives a press that comes too late).
– drückt man kurz VOR der Landung Sprung: — if you press jump shortly BEFORE landing, the jump is remembered and released on touchdown.
– kurz getippt = kleiner Hüpfer, gehalte: — a quick tap gives a small hop, holding gives a high jump (as in Mario).
Stellen Lauftempo, Sprungkraft und Schwe: Set the running speed, the jump strength and the gravity. That is how you make the figure nimbler, the jump higher, or the fall steeper.
Schalten die Komfort-Tricks. Die Zeiten: Switch the comforts. The times are in frames (6 each by default, about 100 ms). COYOTE_TIME(c, 0) makes the controls strict (Souls-like); VARIABLE_JUMP(c, FALSE) gives every jump the same height.
Setzen Position bzw. Geschwindigkeit dir: Set the position or velocity directly — CHAR_SET_POS for moving the figure (respawn, a door), CHAR_SET_VX/VY for knockback on a hit, or a wall jump.
Pro Frame sind es nur drei Aufrufe – Ein: It is only three calls per frame — read the input, feed it in, update — and the rest is drawing:
Breite und Höhe der Figur (für eigenes Z: The figure's width and height (for drawing yourself, or for hit tests) plus the facing as -1 (left) or +1 (right) — with which you mirror the sprite to suit.
CHAR_SET_MAX_FALL begrenzt die Fallgesch: CHAR_SET_MAX_FALL limits the falling speed (without a limit, a figure falls through thin floors after a long drop). CHAR_SET_VARIABLE_JUMP_CUT controls the variable jump height: if the player releases the key early, the upward motion is cut by this factor — 0.5 halves it, 1.0 switches the feature off.
tiled (Level) + tile_collide (Kollision): tiled (the level) + tile_collide (collision) + controller (the controls) + sprite/animfsm (the figure) together make a complete jump-and-run. You connect ready-made modules instead of writing everything yourself — which is exactly what Part V is for.
Position, Geschwindigkeit, Richtung – in: Position, velocity, direction — in 2D games you are forever working with pairs of x and y. The vec2 module gathers such a pair into a 2D vector and gives you the mathematics to go with it: adding, scaling, measuring length, normalising, distance and more. A pleasant bonus: the operators +, -, * and / are overloaded for vectors, so you calculate almost as you would with numbers. Vectors are immutable — every calculation gives a new vector.
Vektoren als Pfeile: v + w (gelb) ist di: Vectors as arrows: v + w (yellow) is the sum of v (blue) and w (green) — computed with the + operator.
VEC2_NEW erzeugt einen Vektor aus x und: VEC2_NEW builds a vector from x and y; VEC2_X/VEC2_Y read the two components back out.
Statt jede Komponente einzeln zu addiere: Instead of adding each component separately, you simply write v + w. The same goes for - (difference) and * (scaling by a number). PRINT shows a vector as Vec2(x, y).
Die arithmetischen Operatoren sind für V: The arithmetic operators are overloaded for vectors: addition and subtraction component by component, multiplication by a number scales (lengthens or shortens). = and <> compare two vectors as well.
VEC2_LENGTH liefert die Länge (den Betra: VEC2_LENGTH gives a vector's length (its magnitude). VEC2_NORMALIZE gives a vector of the same direction but of length 1 — the “pure direction”, ideal for multiplying by a speed afterwards.
VEC2_DISTANCE misst den Abstand zwischen: VEC2_DISTANCE measures the distance between two points (vectors). VEC2_DOT is the dot product — useful for judging angle and alignment (positive = a similar direction).
Weitere nützliche Funktionen: VEC2_LERP: Further useful functions: VEC2_LERP (interpolate between two vectors), VEC2_PERP (perpendicular vector), VEC2_REFLECT (mirror off a surface), VEC2_ANGLE / VEC2_FROM_ANGLE (direction ↔ angle), VEC2_CROSS (the z of the cross product).
Typisches Muster: in eine Richtung beweg: A typical pattern: moving in a direction
Ein Klassiker: ein Geschoss soll zum Zie: A classic: a projectile is to fly towards its target. Compute the direction, normalise it, scale by the speed — thanks to the operators, in a few lines:
VEC2_ZERO ist der Nullvektor als Startwe: VEC2_ZERO is the null vector, as a starting value. VEC2_LENGTH_SQ gives the SQUARED length — without the square root, and so quicker. For comparisons (“is the enemy nearer than 100 pixels?”) that is perfectly enough; you then compare against the square of the distance.
Für eine einzelne Position reichen oft z: For a single position two FLOAT variables (px, py) are often enough. But as soon as you calculate in terms of direction — normalising, distances, reflection — vectors make the code shorter and clearer. For 3D there is the sister module m3d (the next chapter), with VEC3 and more.
Was vec2 für die Fläche ist, ist m3d für: What vec2 is for the plane, m3d is for space: 3D mathematics for working with the g3d module. It offers four value types — VEC3 (a 3D vector), VEC4, QUAT (a quaternion for rotations) and MAT4 (a 4×4 transformation matrix). With them you position, rotate and scale 3D objects and hand the result to the renderer as a matrix. Every value is immutable, and +, - and * are overloaded.
Fünf Würfel, jeder mit MAT4_TRS aus Posi: Five cubes, each placed with MAT4_TRS out of a position, a quaternion rotation and a scaling, and drawn with MODEL_MATRIX.
Erzeugt und liest 3D-Vektoren; die Opera: Creates and reads 3D vectors; the operators work as in vec2 (adding and subtracting component by component, scaling by a number).
DOT ist das Skalarprodukt, CROSS das Kre: DOT is the dot product, CROSS the cross product (giving a vector perpendicular to both — important for normals), NORMALIZE brings a vector to length 1.
VEC3_ZERO liefert den Nullvektor (der üb: VEC3_ZERO gives the null vector (the usual starting value), VEC3_NEG turns the direction around, VEC3_SCALE stretches or squeezes — the same as v * s, but as a function more readable in longer expressions.
DISTANCE is the distance between two points. LENGTH_SQ gives the SQUARED length — without the square root, and so quicker; for comparisons (“who is nearer?”, “within range?”) that is perfectly enough, you simply compare against the square of the range. LERP blends linearly between two points (t = 0 … 1).
REFLECT spiegelt einen Vektor an einer F: REFLECT mirrors a vector off a surface with the normal n — a ball's bounce. TRANSFORM applies a matrix to a POINT (the translation takes effect), TRANSFORM_DIR to a DIRECTION (the translation is ignored). This difference is easily muddled: a rotated line of sight must not be moved along too.
VEC4 – der Vektor mit vierter Komponente: VEC4 — the vector with a fourth component
VEC4 brauchst du selten direkt, aber an: You seldom need VEC4 directly, but in two places you do: for colours with alpha, and for the “homogeneous” points that matrices use internally (w = 1 means a point, w = 0 a direction).
Erzeugen und Auslesen. VEC4_FROM_VEC3 hä: Creating and reading out. VEC4_FROM_VEC3 appends the fourth component to a VEC3.
Dieselben Rechenwege wie bei VEC3, nur ü: The same calculations as with VEC3, only over all four components.
Drehungen im Raum stellt man am besten m: Rotations in space are best represented with quaternions — they avoid the notorious “gimbal lock” and blend cleanly into one another. You mostly create a rotation from an axis and an angle.
FROM_AXIS_ANGLE dreht um die Achse (ax,: FROM_AXIS_ANGLE rotates about the axis (ax, ay, az) by the angle (in radians). QUAT_MUL chains two rotations, QUAT_SLERP blends softly from one rotation to another (for gentle camera and object turns). QUAT_FROM_EULER (pitch/yaw/roll) is available too.
QUAT_IDENTITY ist die Drehung um nichts: QUAT_IDENTITY is the rotation by nothing — the starting value for any orientation. You need QUAT_NEW and the getters almost only when you store quaternions or take them over from a physics engine (PHYS3D_BODY_QX/QY/QZ/QW, say).
NORMALIZE bringt eine Quaternion auf Ein: NORMALIZE brings a quaternion to unit length — needed when you chain many rotations one after another, because rounding errors otherwise build up. CONJUGATE gives the REVERSE rotation (identical to the inverse at unit length).
ROTATE_VEC3 dreht einen einzelnen Vektor: ROTATE_VEC3 rotates a single vector — that is how you get a turned character's actual direction out of the line of sight “forwards”. QUAT_TO_MAT4 makes a matrix out of the rotation (to chain it with a translation, say).
Bei gedrehten Vektoren bleiben winzige R: With rotated vectors, tiny rounding remnants stay behind: a 90° rotation of (1, 0, 0) becomes not exactly (0, 0, -1) but (0.00000006, 0, -0.99999994). That is normal for decimal numbers — never compare such values with =, but with APPROX.
Eine 4×4-Matrix fasst Verschiebung, Dreh: A 4×4 matrix gathers translation, rotation and scaling into one value — exactly what the renderer needs. The most convenient constructor is MAT4_TRS: it builds “translation · rotation · scale” in one step out of a position vector, a rotation quaternion and a scaling vector.
MAT4_TRS erzeugt die fertige Transformat: MAT4_TRS creates an object's finished transformation. MAT4_MUL chains two matrices (for hierarchies the rule is: world = MAT4_MUL(eltern, lokal)). MAT4_IDENTITY is the “neutral” matrix (no change at all). Then there are MAT4_TRANSLATE/SCALE/INVERT/LOOKAT/PERSPECTIVE and others.
Die einzelnen Bausteine, wenn MAT4_TRS z: The separate building blocks, when MAT4_TRS is too coarse. Angles in radians (RAD(grad) helps). Chaining is done with MAT4_MUL — the order decides: scale first, then rotate, then translate is the usual reading.
FROM_QUAT baut die Drehmatrix zu einer Q: FROM_QUAT builds the rotation matrix for a quaternion. TRANSPOSE mirrors along the diagonal. INVERT turns a transformation around — with it you calculate back from world into local coordinates (“where does this world point lie in the vehicle's coordinate system?”, say). A matrix that cannot be inverted reports an error.
Die Kamera-Matrizen. LOOKAT ist die Sich: The camera matrices. LOOKAT is the view matrix, PERSPECTIVE the perspective projection, ORTHO the parallel one — the last for plan views, blueprints or a 2D look in a 3D scene.
MAT4_GET liest einen einzelnen Wert (Zei: MAT4_GET reads a single value (row and column 0–3 each) — the translation stands in column 3. The TRANSFORM functions apply the matrix to a vector; they are the counterparts of VEC3_TRANSFORM with the arguments the other way round.
Setzen eigene Kamera-Matrizen statt der: Set camera matrices of your own instead of those CAMERA3D creates — the way to a parallel projection (ortho) or an unusual field of view.
Zeichnet ein g3d-Modell (aus MESH_* oder: Draws a g3d model (from MESH_* or LOADMODEL) with the transformation matrix given — that is how you join m3d to the 3D graphics. That is how the picture above came about: one MAT4_TRS per cube, then MODEL_MATRIX.
Zeichnet EIN Mesh mit hunderten Matrizen: Draws ONE mesh with hundreds of matrices from an ARRAY OF MAT4 — in a single draw call. For forests, asteroid fields or armies that is orders of magnitude quicker than one MODEL_MATRIX per object. tint is either one colour for all, or an ARRAY OF INTEGER with a colour per matrix; anzahl limits how many entries are drawn.
Die Grafikkarte bekommt beim Instancing: With instancing, the graphics card is sent only the matrices, no colours. The runtime therefore groups by colour and makes ONE draw call per DIFFERENT colour — with five shades that is splendid, with 400 different colours you are back to 400 calls. If every instance is to look different, a gradient in the shader is the better way.
Viele verschiedene Farben kosten die Ers: Many different colours cost you the saving again
Mit CAMERA3D_VIEW/PROJECTION lassen sich: With CAMERA3D_VIEW/PROJECTION you can also set camera matrices of your own — for an orthogonal view or a skewed frustum, say.
g3d (voriges Teil-IV-Kapitel) liefert di: g3d (the previous chapter, in Part IV) supplies the building blocks and primitives, m3d the mathematics for placing and turning them precisely. For simple scenes the g3d commands such as CUBE and MODEL are enough; as soon as you need hierarchies (bones, joints), cameras of your own or many instances, m3d comes into play.
JSON ist das Standardformat, um struktur: JSON is the standard format for exchanging structured data as text — saved games, configuration files, the replies of web services. The json module reads such text in and lets you reach single fields conveniently through a path notation, without counting brackets yourself.
Stell dir ein JSON-Dokument wie eine Sch: Picture a JSON document as a box with labelled compartments: an

JSON_PARSE liest einen String, JSON_LOAD: JSON_PARSE reads a string, JSON_LOAD a file. Both give a JSON_HANDLE — the handle by which every further command addresses the document. Inside a Drachenhauch string literal, quotation marks must be doubled ("" stands for one ").
Wandelt JSON-Text bzw. eine JSON-Datei i: Turns JSON text, or a JSON file, into a JSON_HANDLE. Given invalid JSON (a missing bracket, a comma at the end …) the command stops with an error — best guarded with TRY/CATCH.
Ein Pfad beschreibt den Weg zu einem Wer: A path describes the way to a value. You separate an object's fields with a dot, and address an array's entries by their index — with a dot as well. An empty path "" means the root itself.
— the field name in the sub-object user.
– der erste Eintrag (Index 0) des Array: — the first entry (index 0) of the array hobbies.
– Feld titel des dritten Array-Eintrags: — the field titel of the third array entry.
Für jeden Grundtyp gibt es einen eigenen: For each basic type there is a getter of its own. It gives back exactly that type — if the value in the document does not fit it, there is an error. That way a typo in the data structure shows up at once, rather than slipping quietly through.
Liest den Wert am Pfad als String, Ganzz: Reads the value at the path as a string, whole number, decimal number or truth value. JSON_GET_INT accepts round floats too (5.0 → 5), but refuses 3.14.
Bei einer Liste willst du oft jeden Eint: With a list you often want to visit every entry. JSON_LEN tells you the length of the array at the path; you then append the index to the path as text.
Liefert die Anzahl der Einträge eines Ar: Gives the number of entries of an array (or fields of an object) at the path. With a FOR loop you walk through them in order.
Nicht jedes Feld ist immer da, und manch: Not every field is always there, and sometimes you do not know the type in advance. JSON_HAS checks existence, JSON_TYPE names the kind of value.
TRUE, wenn am Pfad ein Wert existiert, s: TRUE when a value exists at the path, otherwise FALSE. Ideal for optional fields.
Liefert den Typ am Pfad als String: \"ob: Gives the type at the path as a string: "object", "array", "string", "number", "boolean", "null" — or "missing" when the path does not exist. Handy in a SELECT CASE.
Zurück zu Text: JSON_STRINGIFY und JSON_: Back to text: JSON_STRINGIFY and JSON_PRETTY
Manchmal willst du ein eingelesenes Doku: Sometimes you want to put a document you have read back out as text — compact for saving, or nicely indented for looking at.
STRINGIFY erzeugt kompakten JSON-Text (e: STRINGIFY produces compact JSON text (one line, no spaces), PRETTY the same content with indentation and line breaks.
Daten von außen sind selten perfekt. Gre: Data from outside is seldom perfect. If you reach for a field with the wrong getter, or the JSON is broken, the command stops. With TRY/CATCH your program stays standing all the same, and can react sensibly.
Ein typisches Muster: Spiel-Einstellunge: A typical pattern: put the game's settings in a settings.json and read them at startup with JSON_LOAD. Check with FILEEXISTS whether the file is there, and otherwise fill in defaults — that way the game runs on the very first start too. For saving games permanently the save module (chapter 61) is more convenient, because it takes care of the writing as well.
Sobald ein Spiel mehr Daten verwalten mu: As soon as a game has to manage more data than a few variables — a high-score table, an inventory, quest progress across many sittings — a real database becomes worthwhile. The db module brings in SQLite: a complete SQL database that keeps its data in a single file (or wholly in memory). You need no installation and no server.
Dieses Kapitel setzt Grundkenntnisse in: This chapter assumes a basic knowledge of SQL (CREATE TABLE, INSERT, SELECT, UPDATE, DELETE). A complete introduction to SQL would burst these covers; the commands shown here are enough for the great majority of game uses, though, and you can take the SQL strings over as they stand and adapt them.
DB_OPEN öffnet (oder erstellt) eine Date: DB_OPEN opens (or creates) a database and gives a DB_CONN connection. As the path you take a file name for a lasting database, or the special value ":memory:" for a fleeting one that lives only in memory and vanishes when the program ends (ideal for trying things out). At the end DB_CLOSE closes the connection.
Öffnet/erstellt die Datenbank, gibt eine: Opens or creates the database and returns a DB_CONN. ":memory:" = a fleeting in-memory database. DB_CLOSE releases the connection when the program ends.
DB_EXEC führt jedes SQL-Statement aus, d: DB_EXEC carries out every SQL statement that returns no rows — that is CREATE, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE. You never put values directly into the SQL string; you write a question mark ? as a placeholder and pass the value as a further argument. That is safer (no “SQL injection”) and takes care of quotation marks and special characters by itself.
Führt ein SQL-Statement aus; jedes ? im: Carries out an SQL statement; each ? in the SQL is replaced in turn by the values that follow. The return value is the number of rows affected. The value types allowed: INTEGER, FLOAT, STRING, BOOLEAN (as 0/1) and NIL (which becomes SQL NULL).
Liefert die rowid (interne Zeilennummer): Gives the rowid (internal row number) of the row inserted last — handy for going on to use an id you have just created.
Lesen: DB_QUERY und die Ergebnis-Schleif: Reading: DB_QUERY and the result loop
Ein SELECT liefert Zeilen – dafür gibt e: A SELECT returns rows — for that there is DB_QUERY. The result is a DB_RESULT, a kind of cursor. You fetch the rows one at a time: DB_NEXT moves on to the next row and returns TRUE for as long as there is one. Inside the loop you read the columns with the typed DB_GET_* commands, by their 0-based index (column 0 = the first column in the SELECT).
DB_QUERY startet die Abfrage, DB_NEXT ge: DB_QUERY starts the query, DB_NEXT goes through row by row (TRUE = there is a row), the DB_GET_* commands read the current row's columns. At the end DB_CLOSE_RESULT releases the cursor.
In SQL bedeutet NULL „kein Wert“. Die DB: In SQL, NULL means “no value”. On a NULL the DB_GET_* commands give a default (0, 0.0, "", FALSE). If you want to recognise real absence, ask first with DB_IS_NULL.
TRUE, wenn die Spalte in der aktuellen Z: TRUE when the column in the current row is NULL. That is how you tell “empty/0” from “not set”.
Anzahl und Namen der Spalten eines Ergeb: The number and the names of a result's columns — useful for generic output or debugging tools.
Normalerweise wird jedes DB_EXEC sofort: Normally every DB_EXEC is stored permanently at once. Sometimes, though, several changes belong together and are only to take effect jointly — deducting gold AND booking in the item, say. DB_BEGIN starts a transaction, DB_COMMIT commits everything in one go, DB_ROLLBACK discards everything should something go wrong. Together with TRY/CATCH the database thus always stays consistent.
Klammern mehrere Statements zu einer Ein: Bracket several statements into one unit. On an error in the TRY block, DB_ROLLBACK undoes every change made since DB_BEGIN.
Die restlichen Spalten-Typen neben DB_GE: The remaining column types beside DB_GET_INT and DB_GET_STRING — decimal numbers (prices, times) and truth values.
Drei Gewohnheiten ersparen viel Ärger: (: Three habits save a great deal of trouble: (1) create the schema with “CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS …”, and starting the program repeatedly is then harmless. (2) Close every DB_RESULT after use with DB_CLOSE_RESULT. (3) Always bind values with ?, never build them into the SQL string. For quite simple saved games (a few numbers and strings), incidentally, the save module from chapter 61 is lighter — db becomes worthwhile as soon as lists, searching and sorting are involved.
Reguläre Ausdrücke (kurz „Regex“) sind e: Regular expressions (“regexes” for short) are a small language for describing patterns in text: “a run of digits”, “a word followed by a number”, “everything between two brackets”. Wherever INSTR and SPLIT grow too weak — taking high-score lines apart, checking input, rewriting text — regex is the right tool.
Ein Muster ist selbst ein String, der So: A pattern is itself a string containing special characters.
thus means “one or more digits”. You combine such building blocks into patterns of any precision you like.
– eine Ziffer · ein Wortzeichen (Buchst: — a digit · a word character (letter/digit/_) · a space or tab. Capitalised (\D \W \S), the opposite in each case.
– eins aus der Menge · ein Bereich · al: — one from the set · a range · anything but x.
– null oder mehr · ein oder mehr · null: — none or more · one or more · none or one.
– genau n bzw. zwischen n und m Wiederh: — exactly n repetitions, or between n and m.
– eine Capture-Gruppe (merkt sich den T: — a capture group (remembers that part of the match).
In Drachenhauch-Strings ist der Backslas: In Drachenhauch strings the backslash is NOT a special character — so you write the pattern directly as "\d+", not "\\d+". That makes regex strings pleasantly readable.
Drei Befehle beantworten unterschiedlich: Three commands answer different questions. REGEX_MATCH requires the pattern to cover the WHOLE text. REGEX_TEST asks only whether the pattern occurs somewhere. REGEX_FIND gives back the first piece of text that matches.
MATCH = does the whole word fit? (BOOLEAN). TEST = does it occur anywhere? (BOOLEAN). FIND = gives the first match as a string (an empty string when nothing fits — no NIL check needed).
REGEX_FIND_ALL liefert ein ARRAY OF STRI: REGEX_FIND_ALL gives an ARRAY OF STRING with every (non-overlapping) match — ideal for pulling all the numbers out of a line, for instance.
Gibt alle Treffer als ARRAY OF STRING zu: Returns every match as an ARRAY OF STRING. If the pattern contains brackets (a capture group), the contents of that group are gathered — not the whole match.
Mit Klammern extrahierst du gezielt eine: With brackets you pull out one particular part of each match. Here only the IP address after “ip ” is extracted, not the “ip ” itself.
REGEX_REPLACE ersetzt alle Treffer durch: REGEX_REPLACE replaces every match with a replacement text, REGEX_REPLACE_ONCE only the first. In the replacement text you refer to the pattern's capture groups with \1, \2 … — that is how you can rearrange pieces of text.
Ersetzt alle bzw. nur den ersten Treffer: Replaces every match, or only the first. \1, \2 … in the replacement stand for the groups found.
REGEX_SPLIT ist wie SPLIT, nur dass die: REGEX_SPLIT is like SPLIT, except that the separator is a pattern. That is how you split at any amount of whitespace, say, or at commas with optional spaces around them.
Teilt den Text an jedem Treffer des Must: Divides the text at every match of the pattern and gives the pieces as an ARRAY OF STRING.
Die native Runtime nutzt die Rust-Regex-: The native runtime uses the Rust regex engine. It covers every building block above, but supports NO lookaheads or lookbehinds ((?=…), (?<=…)) and no back-references (\1) IN the pattern itself. In the REPLACEMENT text of REGEX_REPLACE, by contrast, \1 and \2 are allowed (as shown above). Given an invalid pattern the command stops with an error message.
Rust-Regex: keine Lookarounds/Backrefs I: Rust regex: no lookarounds or back-references IN the pattern
Muster einmal, Nutzung oft: Build the pattern once, use it often
regex merkt sich jedes übersetzte Muster: regex remembers every pattern it has compiled (a pattern cache). So you can use the same pattern in a loop over thousands of lines without a second thought — it is built only once. Practical uses: validating input (a date "\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}", a rough e-mail check), a high-score parser, a chat word filter (REGEX_REPLACE of the rude words with "***").
Kapitel 46 hat die Grundlagen gezeigt: T: Chapter 46 showed the basics: loading and playing tones and sounds. But the audio module can do a great deal more. It is a complete audio engine (built on Kira) that runs on a thread of its own — so your game loop can stutter without the sound stuttering. This chapter shows the advanced tools: steering individual channels, moving the stereo image, playing sounds as samples at different pitches, and laying real-time effects such as reverb, echo or filters over whole groups of buses.
Klang lässt sich im Buch nicht abdrucken: Sound cannot be printed in a book — try the examples out for yourself. Most of the commands here produce no console output; they act on what you hear.
Wenn du einen Sound mit AUDIO_PLAY start: When you start a sound with AUDIO_PLAY you get a channel number (INTEGER) back. By that number you steer precisely that one running playback — halting it, resuming it, louder or quieter, changing the pitch — while other sounds run on untouched.
AUDIO_PLAY startet einen Sound und liefe: AUDIO_PLAY starts a sound and gives its channel number. AUDIO_STOP ends that channel, AUDIO_IS_PLAYING checks whether it is still sounding.
Hält einen Kanal an, ohne ihn zu beenden: Halts a channel without ending it, and resumes it later at the same place. The _ALL variants act on every channel (good for a pause menu).
Lautstärke (0..1) eines Kanals setzen/le: Set or read a channel's volume (0..1) and change the pitch live: faktor 2.0 = an octave higher and twice as fast, 0.5 = an octave lower. (AUDIO_VOLUME is an alias for AUDIO_SET_VOLUME.)
Mit dem Panorama legst du fest, ob ein K: With the stereo image you lay down whether a sound comes rather from the left or the right — so that an enemy is audible from the side he attacks from, say. The position runs from -1 (hard left) through 0 (centre) to +1 (hard right).
PAN_POS setzt die Position sofort, PAN_S: PAN_POS sets the position at once, PAN_SLIDE travels it over a span of time from “von” to “nach” (an object passing by), AUTOPAN lets the sound wander gently to and fro without end.
AUDIO_SFX ist ein kleiner Synthesizer im: AUDIO_SFX is a small synthesiser in the style of the classic 8-bit sound chips: out of a waveform plus an envelope, a pitch slide and vibrato you build running, jumping, hit or coin noises — with no audio file at all. (The sound generator dhsfx exports exactly such calls.)
Erzeugt einen SOUND. wellenform$ = \"sin: Creates a SOUND. wellenform$ = "sine"/"square"/"saw"/"triangle"/"noise". freq = the starting frequency, slide = the pitch drift, atk/sus/dec = the envelope (attack, sustain, decay in seconds), vib_tiefe/vib_speed = vibrato, vol = the volume. Further optional arguments steer the stereo width, the pulse width and the filter.
Gibt einem frisch erzeugten Sound (TONE/: Gives a freshly created sound (TONE/NOISE/SFX/SAMPLE) a grainy retro character: bit-crush (8 bit by default) plus a soft low-pass filter (3300 Hz by default) — the typical Amiga lo-fi sound.
Samples: einen Klang in Tonhöhen spielen: Samples: playing one sound at many pitches
Ein Sample ist eine kurze Aufnahme (z. B: A sample is a short recording (a single piano note, say) that you play at any pitch you like — the principle of a sampler. SAMPLE_PLAY transposes the recording by a number of semitones. Short one-shots suit drums and hits; with a loop region (SAMPLE_SET_LOOP) sustained notes can be produced.
LOAD lädt eine Audiodatei als SAMPLE. PL: LOAD loads an audio file as a SAMPLE. PLAY plays it transposed by halbtoene (0 = the original pitch, 12 = an octave higher) and returns a channel number. SET_LOOP marks a loop region, LEN gives the length in samples.
Über PLAYMUSIC (Kapitel 46) hinaus kanns: Beyond PLAYMUSIC (chapter 46) you can steer running music finely: pause it, resume it, stop it with a fade, ask after the playback position or bend the pitch. Tracker modules (.mod/.xm) are streamed in real time as well.
Pausiert/setzt die Musik fort, stoppt si: Pauses or resumes the music, stops it (optionally with a fade-out in milliseconds), and with POSITION gives the current playback time in seconds (FLOAT) — to synchronise a light show to the music, for instance.
Lautstärke (0..1) und Tonhöhe/Tempo der: Adjust the music's volume (0..1) and its pitch and tempo live — turning the music down while a voice speaks, say, or slowing it into slow motion.
Der zweistufige Weg statt PLAYMUSIC: ers: The two-stage way instead of PLAYMUSIC: load first, then start — so that you can prepare a piece during the loading screen and strike it up later with no delay. AUDIO_MUSIC_QUEUE appends a piece that follows automatically when the running one ends (intro → main theme).
endlos, 1,5 s weich einblenden: endless, fading in softly over 1.5 s
Die Abfrage-Seite: aktuelle Lautstärke u: The asking side: reading out the current volume and pitch (to show them in the options, say), and checking whether any music is running at all. AUDIO_MUSIC_VOLUME is the shorter name for AUDIO_MUSIC_SET_VOLUME.
Die Tonausgabe startet von selbst, sobal: The sound output starts of its own accord as soon as you play something — you only need AUDIO_INIT when you want to set it up beforehand with values of your own. The default is 16 simultaneous channels; if that is not enough with many effects, you raise it.
AUDIO_BUSY_CHANNELS zählt die gerade kli: AUDIO_BUSY_CHANNELS counts the channels sounding just then — useful for not giving every single hit its own sound during mass explosions. AUDIO_STOP_ALL breaks everything off: the clean cut when the scene changes.
Alle Klänge laufen über drei Busse: \"sf: Every sound runs over three buses: "sfx" (effects, samples, synth), "music" (the music) and "master" (the sum of both). Through the bus you regulate a whole group at once — the classic separate sliders for “effects” and “music” in the options menu.
Setzt/liest die Lautstärke (0..1) eines: Sets or reads a bus's volume (0..1). bus$ = "sfx", "music" or "master".
Auf jeden Bus lässt sich eine Kette von: On each bus a chain of effects can be laid that compute in real time — you can change their values at any moment. With them you lend a cave level reverb, a radio set a band-pass filter or a boss fight a distorted edge. Every effect is neutral until you activate it.
REVERB legt einen Raum-/Hall-Effekt auf: REVERB lays a room-and-reverb effect on the bus (mix = the proportion, 0..1). DELAY is an echo with an adjustable delay time — the time can be changed at run time.
FILTER ist ein Tiefpass (lässt nur Frequ: FILTER is a low-pass (it lets through only frequencies below cutoff_hz — a muffled sound, the classic “acid” sweep). DISTORTION adds overdrive and fuzz.
COMPRESSOR drückt laute Spitzen zusammen: COMPRESSOR squeezes loud peaks together and makes the sound more even (ratio<=1 = off). EQ lifts or lowers a range of frequencies (gain_db: positive = louder, negative = quieter, 0 = neutral).
Bus-Einstellungen sichern: AUDIO_PUSH un: Saving the bus settings: AUDIO_PUSH and AUDIO_POP
Alle Bus-Einstellungen sind global – Lau: Every bus setting is global — volume, balance, filter, reverb, echo, distortion, compressor, EQ. Lay reverb on the master for a cave and forget it on the way out, and the menu echoes too. Rather than undoing every line by hand, you put the whole state on a stack.
AUDIO_PUSH sichert alle Bus-Einstellunge: AUDIO_PUSH saves every bus setting, AUDIO_POP fetches them back, AUDIO_DEPTH gives the depth of the stack. A POP without a PUSH is an error.
Hast du mit AUDIO_MODULATE einen LFO auf: If you have laid an LFO with AUDIO_MODULATE on a bus value that an AUDIO_POP writes back, the modulation ends at that point — both are writing the same control, and the last one wins. That is not a fault but a consequence of how the values converge; if you want to keep the modulation, set it up again after the POP.
Eine laufende Modulation wird dabei abge: A running modulation is displaced in the process
Das Gegenstück für die Grafik heißt GFX_: The counterpart for the graphics is called GFX_PUSH / GFX_POP and saves the light, fog, camera, shadows, font and post effect — see chapter 42.
Eine Uhr, die vom Audio-Thread selbst ge: A clock driven by the audio thread itself — not by your (less exact) game loop. With it you plan sounds precisely onto a musical beat rather than “roughly now”. Handy for rhythm games or effects synchronised to the music.
AUDIO_CLOCK_NEW legt eine Uhr an (starte: AUDIO_CLOCK_NEW creates a clock (it starts paused). AUDIO_CLOCK_START starts it. AUDIO_CLOCK_TICKING tells you whether it is running just then. You convert a BPM figure into the tick rate yourself: bpm / 60.0 * unterteilungen.
PAUSE hält die Uhr an (Ticks bleiben ste: PAUSE halts the clock (the ticks stand still, START resumes). STOP sets it back to 0 and halts. REMOVE releases the clock for good.
SET_SPEED ändert das Tempo einer laufend: SET_SPEED changes a running clock's tempo (at a change of tempo in the piece, say). AUDIO_CLOCK_TICKS gives the number of ticks gone by since the start — your counter for “which beat are we on”.
Plant den Start eines Sounds exakt auf d: Plans a sound's start exactly on the clock tick given — triggered by the audio thread itself, not by your frame timing. That way a hi-hat sample sounds exactly in time instead of wavering slightly with the frame rate.
Für 2D-/3D-Spiele mit Ortsgefühl: Ein Li: For 2D and 3D games with a sense of place: a listener is the scene's “ear” (mostly bound to the camera or the player's character), an emitter a source of sound somewhere in the world. Kira takes on the calculation of panning and of the fall in volume with distance itself — you need calculate nothing yourself.
Legt einen Listener an der Position (x,: Creates a listener at the position (x, y, z) — mostly the camera's position. SET_POSITION moves it (update it every frame). SET_ORIENTATION turns its line of sight about the Y axis (yaw in degrees) — enough for the typical top-down or third-person view, without full 3D rotation.

Geben Emitter bzw. Listener wieder frei: Release an emitter or a listener again — tidying up when a source of sound or a scene is no longer needed.
Modulatoren: Klänge, die sich von selbst: Modulators: sounds that move of their own accord
Ein Tremolo, ein Wobble-Bass oder ein Fi: A tremolo, a wobble bass or a filter sweep means: a value is constantly moving. You could compute it yourself every frame — but then the sound hangs on the frame rate and stutters as soon as the game does. Modulators run on the AUDIO thread instead: sample-exact, regardless of what the game is doing, and without your program computing anything per frame.
Es gibt zwei Sorten. Ein LFO schwingt en: There are two sorts. An LFO oscillates endlessly (for everything recurring), a tweener travels once from one value to another (for transitions). Both give the same handle type, AUDIO_MOD.
Erzeugt einen Schwinger. wellenform$ ist: Creates an oscillator. wellenform$ is "sine", "triangle", "saw" or "pulse", hz the speed (4.0 = four times a second). The amplitude and centre lay down the range of values (by default it swings between -1 and +1). The two setters change a running LFO without creating it anew.
Ein Tweener hält einen Wert und fährt ih: A tweener holds a value and travels it to a new one on command — opening a filter slowly when the player surfaces, say. easing$ is "linear", "in", "out" or "inout".
Connects a modulator to a bus. ziel$ is "volume" (tremolo), "pan" (auto-pan), "filter", "resonance", "reverb" or "distortion". The modulator's range of values is mapped onto min…max in the process — so an LFO between -1 and +1 with min=0.4/max=1.0 lets the volume swing between 40 % and 100 %. AUDIO_MOD_REMOVE breaks the connection again.
Verschiebt einen ganzen Bus im Stereobil: Moves a whole bus in the stereo image (-1 = left, 0 = centre, +1 = right). Until this, only a single channel could be panned; with it you put the whole of the music slightly to the left, say, while the effects stay in the centre.
Weil die Modulatoren auf dem Audio-Threa: Because the modulators run on the audio thread, tremolo, vibrato, wobble bass, auto-pan and filter sweeps stay clean even when the frame rate collapses — precisely the difference from a solution built by hand in the game loop. A complete demonstration is examples/150_audio_modulatoren.dh.
Mit AUDIO_FFT(array) füllst du ein ARRAY: With AUDIO_FFT(array) you fill an ARRAY OF FLOAT with the current frequency strengths of the total output. Out of it you build bar visualisers, or let effects “dance to the music”. Together with the bus effects and Kira's streaming functions, the audio module covers everything a game needs in the way of sound — from a single beep to a dynamic soundtrack.
Das curves-Modul rechnet einzelne Punkte: The curves module computes single points on a curve. Where the tween module (chapter 52) animates a value from A to B over time, curves answers the question “which value lies at progress t on this curve?”. With it you send objects flying along soft arcs, pan cameras gently or let values settle elegantly. Every command is a pure function — no state, no setting up.
Zwei Kurventypen durch dieselbe Gegend:: Two kinds of curve through the same territory: the Bézier curve (yellow) is merely drawn towards its handles, the Catmull-Rom curve (cyan) runs directly through its control points.
Alle Kurven bekommen einen Parameter: Every curve is given a parameter
(meist von 0 bis 1) und liefern den int: (usually from 0 to 1) and gives back the interpolated value. What tells them apart is
die Kontrollpunkte den Verlauf formen –: the control points shape the course — from a straight line to a freely sweeping path.
Die einfachen: LERP, SMOOTHSTEP, SMOOTHE: The simple ones: LERP, SMOOTHSTEP, SMOOTHERSTEP
CURVE_LERP zieht eine gerade Linie zwisc: CURVE_LERP draws a straight line between two values. SMOOTHSTEP and SMOOTHERSTEP are S-curves: they begin and end gently (accelerating slowly, braking slowly) — the typical “ease-in-out” feel. SMOOTHERSTEP is the softer variant again.
Linear interpolation: a + (b - a) * t. At t=0 out comes a, at t=1 out comes b, at t=0.5 the middle.
Normalisiert x auf den Bereich [kante0,: Normalises x to the range [kante0, kante1] (clamped to 0..1) and lays an S-curve over it. Ideal for soft fades in and out.
Eine kubische Bezier-Kurve hat vier Punk: A cubic Bézier curve has four points. P0 is the start, P3 the end — the curve touches both. P1 and P2 are “handles”: they pull the curve their way without its passing through them. That is how you shape jump arcs or elegant camera moves. In the picture above the grey lines are the handles, the yellow path the curve.
Kubische Bezier-Kurve in einer Dimension: A cubic Bézier curve in one dimension. Gives the interpolated scalar at t.
Bezier-Kurve in der Ebene: vier Punkte a: A Bézier curve in the plane: four points as (x, y), the return value a TUPLE (x, y). Perfect for sending an object along a path.
Anders als Bezier läuft eine Catmull-Rom: Unlike a Bézier, a Catmull-Rom curve runs directly THROUGH its middle points (P1 and P2). P0 and P3 are merely the neighbours that see to a smooth transition. This is the first choice when an object is to travel smoothly along a series of given waypoints — a patrol route or the course of a race track, say.
Catmull-Rom-Spline 1D bzw. 2D. Die Kurve: A Catmull-Rom spline in 1D or 2D. The curve runs from P1 to P2 and touches both; P0 and P3 determine the tangents, for a gentle join to the neighbouring segments.
Für einen Pfad aus vielen Wegpunkten fäh: For a path of many waypoints you travel the segments one after another: between point 1 and 2 (with 0 and 3 as neighbours), then between 2 and 3 (with 1 and 4 as neighbours) and so on — every segment uses four consecutive points.
Interpoliert von p0 nach p1 mit ausdrück: Interpolates from p0 to p1 with tangents (velocities) given explicitly: m0 at the start and m1 at the end. Both tangents at 0 gives a gentle S-curve like SmoothStep.
Beide Module ergänzen sich. tween animie: The two modules complete one another. tween animates a value dependably over a duration; curves turns a progress into a position on a path. Let a tween run the parameter t from 0 to 1 over two seconds and put t into CURVE_BEZIER2, and your object flies a soft curve with exact timing.

CURVE_LERP(jetzt, ziel, 0.1) jeden Frame: Calling CURVE_LERP(jetzt, ziel, 0.1) every frame is a tiny trick with a large effect: the value always comes the same fraction closer to the target, and so brakes gently of its own accord. That is how butter-smooth camera moves, trailing health bars and sluggishly following pursuers come about — with a single line per frame.
Mit dem net-Modul reden Programme über d: With the net module, programs talk to one another over the network — for a chat, a high-score query or a multi-player game on the LAN. It offers the two classic means of transport, TCP and UDP. Important for games: every connection is “non-blocking” by default — a read command returns at once, even when nothing is there, so that your game loop never freezes.
Netzwerk ist ein großes Thema; dieses Ka: Networking is a large subject; this chapter shows the building blocks and a working example on one and the same machine (over the address 127.0.0.1, “localhost”). For real play across several devices, questions of firewalls and IP addresses come in as well, which would burst these covers.
– verbindungsorientiert, zuverlässig: A: — connection-oriented, dependable: everything arrives complete and in the right order. Right for chat, turn-based games, signing in to a lobby.
– verbindungslos, schnell: Einzelne Pak: — connectionless, quick: single packets can be lost or swap places, but it is nimble. Right for constant position updates in action games, where the next packet overtakes the loss anyway.
Ein TCP-Server lauscht mit NET_TCP_LISTE: A TCP server listens on a port with NET_TCP_LISTEN. NET_TCP_ACCEPT collects a waiting connection — or gives NIL when nobody is connecting just then (which you check with IS_NIL). A client builds the connection with NET_TCP_CONNECT. Over the finished connection you send text with NET_SEND and read with NET_RECV.
LISTEN öffnet einen Server-Socket (Port: LISTEN opens a server socket (port 0 = the operating system picks a free one, which you can ask for with NET_LISTENER_PORT). ACCEPT returns a new NET_SOCKET connection — or NIL when none is waiting (check with IS_NIL(x) or x <> NIL).
CONNECT verbindet zum Server (5 s Anschl: CONNECT connects to the server (a 5 s connection time limit). NET_SEND sends text and returns the number of bytes sent. NET_RECV reads up to max_bytes and gives an empty string when nothing is there (yet). All UTF-8.
leer, wenn noch nichts kam: empty when nothing has come yet
PEER_ADDR/PEER_PORT verraten die Gegenst: PEER_ADDR and PEER_PORT tell you a connection's far end. NET_CLOSE closes a connection, NET_CLOSE_LISTENER the server socket — tidy both away at the end.
Ein vollständiges Beispiel auf einem Rec: A complete example on one machine
Server und Client können im selben Progr: Server and client can run in the same program — handy for trying things out. Here a client connects, sends a message, and the server reads it. The short SLEEP pauses give the operating system time to deliver the data.
UDP kennt keine feste Verbindung. Ein So: UDP knows no fixed connection. A socket binds itself (NET_UDP_BIND) to a port for receiving, or is opened with NET_UDP_OPEN for sending only. You address every packet separately as you send it, with a destination host and port. After a receive, NET_UDP_LAST_FROM tells you whom the packet came from.
BIND bindet einen UDP-Socket an einen Po: BIND binds a UDP socket to a port (0 = a free port). OPEN creates a socket for sending only. NET_UDP_PORT gives the port bound.
SEND sends a packet to host$:port. RECV reads the next packet (empty when there is none). NET_UDP_LAST_FROM gives the sender's address for the packet received last, as a STRING "host:port".
NET_UDP_LAST_FROM gibt einen STRING der: NET_UDP_LAST_FROM returns a STRING of the form "host:port" ("127.0.0.1:63332", for instance), not two separate values. You get the host part, should you need it, with SPLIT(adr, ":")[0].
Verrät, ob eine TCP-Verbindung noch als: Tells you whether a TCP connection still counts as open. Becomes FALSE as soon as an attempt to read or write has noticed the far end closing — handy as a quick check before you call NET_SEND or NET_RECV.
Alle Lese- und Annahme-Befehle (RECV, AC: Every reading and accepting command (RECV, ACCEPT, UDP_RECV) returns at once: if nothing is there, they give empty text or NIL. So you ask the network once a frame without stopping the loop. If for once you want to wait until data comes, you set a time limit with NET_SET_TIMEOUT (or NET_UDP_SET_TIMEOUT) — careful in the game loop, because that holds the frame up.
NET_TCP_ACCEPT liefert NIL, wenn gerade: NET_TCP_ACCEPT gives NIL when no connection is waiting just then. NIL is a perfectly ordinary value (a literal) that you can write and compare directly — so check with IF NOT IS_NIL(client) THEN … or, equivalently, with IF client <> NIL THEN ….
cloud – Spielstände und Bestenlisten auf: cloud — saved games and high-score tables on a server
Selbst Sockets zu programmieren lohnt si: Programming sockets yourself is worthwhile for a protocol of your own. For the two commonest cases — “the saved game lives on the server” and “a worldwide high-score table” — there is the cloud module: it talks over HTTP to a small server whose reference implementation lies under cloudserver/ in the project (you can run it on a Raspberry Pi on your home network, or with a provider).
Legt Serveradresse und das geteilte Gehe: Sets the server address and the shared secret. Must come BEFORE all the other CLOUD_ and LEADERBOARD_ calls, or a clear error message follows.
CLOUD_SAVE legt einen beliebigen Text un: CLOUD_SAVE stores any text you like under a player identifier (JSON from the json module is usual), overwriting the previous state as it does. CLOUD_LOAD fetches it back.
CLOUD_LOAD wirft bei einem Fehler absich: On an error CLOUD_LOAD deliberately raises no run-time error — “nothing saved yet” and “server unreachable” both look like empty text. You can only tell them apart through CLOUD_LAST_ERROR$: empty means a genuine first visit, filled means an error. Pass over that, and on a network hiccup you will cheerfully overwrite the saved game with a fresh start.
Leerer Spielstand heißt nicht immer „neu: An empty saved game does not always mean “a new player”
SUBMIT reicht ein Ergebnis ein und liefe: SUBMIT hands in a result and returns TRUE when it was a new personal best — only the best value is kept per table and name. With kleiner_ist_besser = TRUE the lowest value counts (speedrun times). FETCH fetches the best n entries as an ARRAY OF TUPLE of (name$, punkte).
Schließt einen UDP-Socket und gibt den A: Closes a UDP socket and releases the port again — the counterpart to NET_UDP_BIND.
TCP ist ein Strom, kein Paket-Versand: Z: TCP is a stream, not a despatch of packets: two NET_SENDs can arrive at the receiver as one NET_RECV — or the other way about. If you need messages with boundaries, send the length ahead (four digits, say) or end every message with a separator such as a line break, and put them back together at the receiver.
Das html-Modul holt Daten aus dem Web: e: The html module fetches data from the web: calling up a web page or an API (HTTP_GET), uploading data (HTTP_POST), downloading a file (HTTP_DOWNLOAD). Then there are helpers for preparing text for URLs and for taking simple HTML apart. With these you build online high-score tables, fetch daily content or load extra assets from the net.
HTTP-Aufrufe brauchen einen Moment und k: HTTP calls take a moment and can fail (no network, the server gone). Do not make them in the middle of the render loop, or the picture will stutter — and guard them with TRY/CATCH. The time limit is 10 seconds.
HTTP_GET ruft eine Adresse auf und liefe: HTTP_GET calls up an address and gives the reply as text. HTTP_STATUS afterwards tells you the HTTP status code (200 = OK, 404 = not found …). On an error status or a connection problem the call stops — catch it with TRY/CATCH.
GET ruft die URL ab und gibt den Antwort: GET calls up the URL and returns the reply text (UTF-8). HTTP_STATUS gives the status code of the last reply — still readable after an error.
POST sendet body$ an die URL (z. B. um e: POST sends body$ to the URL (to enter a high score, say) and returns the reply. HTTP_HEADER reads a reply header from the last request; the case of the name does not matter.
Lädt eine Datei direkt auf die Festplatt: Loads a file straight onto the disc and returns the number of bytes. For binary data (images, sounds) always take DOWNLOAD rather than GET — GET would corrupt the bytes by treating them as text.
Weil ein Netzwerkaufruf jederzeit scheit: Because a network call can fail at any moment, it belongs in a TRY/CATCH block. After an error status HTTP_STATUS is still readable, so that you can react to the particular case.
In einer Web-Adresse dürfen viele Zeiche: Many characters (spaces, &, ?, accented letters) may not appear directly in a web address. URL_ENCODE turns a text into a safe form, URL_DECODE undoes it. You need this as soon as you build search terms or names into a URL.
ENCODE ersetzt Sonderzeichen durch %XX-S: ENCODE replaces special characters with %XX sequences (space → %20, & → %26). DECODE resolves them again.
Antworten von Webseiten sind oft HTML –: The replies of web pages are often HTML — text mixed with formatting tags. Three helpers get the useful parts out: HTML_TEXT removes every tag and gives pure readable text, HTML_FIND_ALL gathers the contents of all the tags of one kind, HTML_GET_ATTR pulls an attribute (a link's destination address, say) out of a tag.
Streift alle Tags weg und wandelt HTML-S:
Strips every tag away and converts HTML's special spellings back (& → &). Block elements such as

produce a line break;
Liefert den Innen-Inhalt aller Vorkommen: Gives the inner content of every occurrence of a tag as an ARRAY OF STRING. Nested tags of the same name are matched up correctly.
Holt den Wert eines Attributs aus dem er: Fetches an attribute's value from the first tag in the snippet passed in — a link's href, for instance. Understands double-quoted, single-quoted and unquoted values.

Abruf und HTML-Zerlegung greifen ineinan: Fetching and taking the HTML apart mesh together: fetch the page, gather the tags you want, pull the text out.
Die meisten modernen Web-Schnittstellen: Most modern web interfaces reply not with HTML but with JSON. You then combine html with the json module (chapter 68): you put the reply from HTTP_GET straight into JSON_PARSE and read the fields with JSON_GET_*. You only need to take HTML apart when you want to “scrape” real web pages.
Ein Entity-Component-System (ECS) ist ei: An entity-component system (ECS) is another way of organising game objects. Rather than building each character as an object with methods (as in chapter 20), you break it down into pure data and write the logic separately from it. That sounds strange at first, but it is the model with which modern engines move thousands of objects smoothly.
Das mentale Modell: Daten statt Objekte: The mental model: data instead of objects
Drei Begriffe tragen das ganze System. E: Three terms carry the whole system. An
ist nur eine Nummer – ein Namensschild,: is only a number — a name tag that stands for “a thing in the game”, with no contents at all. A
ist ein benannter Wert, den du an eine: is a named value that you pin to an entity:
schließlich ist eine Schleife, die alle: is, finally, a loop that works on every entity with certain components — “move everything that has a position AND a velocity”, for instance.
Der Gewinn: Eine Entity kann beliebig zu: The gain: an entity can be put together however you like. A stone has only “position”, an enemy additionally “velocity” and “life”, a bonus also “collectable”. You need plan no hierarchy of classes — you plug components together like building blocks. And because data of the same kind lies close together, it can be processed in bulk at great speed.
Alles lebt in einer Welt (ECS_WORLD). Da: Everything lives in a world (ECS_WORLD). In it you create entities; each returns a unique number ≥ 1. You can destroy entities, ask after their state and count them.
NEW_WORLD erzeugt eine leere Welt, NEW_E: NEW_WORLD creates an empty world, NEW_ENTITY a new entity (returning its id), ECS_COUNT counts the living entities.
DESTROY entfernt eine Entity samt all ih: DESTROY removes an entity along with all its components (TRUE when it existed). ECS_ALIVE checks whether an entity is still alive.
Components anheften und lesen: Pinning on components, and reading them
Für jeden Datentyp gibt es einen Add-Bef: For each data type there is an add command. The component's name is a string — it is created at run time, you need declare nothing in advance. Pin the same name on again and the value is overwritten.
Hängt einen benannten Wert an eine Entit: Hangs a named value on an entity. ADD_OBJ takes any value at all (your own classes, maps, arrays). The type is checked as it is pinned on.
GET_* liest einen Component (Fehler, wen: GET_* reads a component (an error when the entity does not have it). GET_OR_* gives a default instead. ECS_HAS checks existence, ECS_REMOVE removes a single component.
Ein System fragt mit ECS_QUERY alle Enti: A system asks with ECS_QUERY for every entity that possesses a certain combination of components, and works through them. That is the heart of the pattern: the logic acts on “everything that has this data”, whatever kind of game object it otherwise is. The result is an ARRAY OF INTEGER of entity ids.
Liefert die IDs aller Entities, die alle: Gives the ids of every entity that possesses all the components named. QUERY2 and QUERY3 require 2 or 3 components at once (the intersection).
Bulk-Operationen: Massen blitzschnell: Bulk operations: masses at great speed
Der Query-Loop oben ist verständlich, ab: The query loop above is understandable, but slow with thousands of entities — several command calls fall due per entity. For the hot paths there are bulk commands that process a whole layer of components in ONE call. They are many times quicker (realistically forty times).
INTEGRATE addiert delta auf ziel für all: INTEGRATE adds delta onto ziel for every entity with both components (the classic position += velocity). SCALE multiplies (friction, say), CLAMP limits to a range (at the edge of the screen, say).
REMOVE_DEAD zerstört alle Entities, dere: REMOVE_DEAD destroys every entity whose component is ≤ grenze (hp ≤ 0, say). COUNT_WITH counts a component's holders in constant time. FILL sets every value to the same value (a reset).
Neben Zahlen und Text kannst du auch Wah: Beside numbers and text you can hang truth values and arbitrary objects on an entity as well — an instance of a class or a sprite handle, say. ECS_GET reads an object component back.
Lesen mit Ersatzwert, falls die Entity d: Reading with a substitute value should the entity not have this component at all — which saves you the ECS_HAS check beforehand.
Die INTEGER-Varianten der Bulk-Befehle:: The INTEGER variants of the bulk commands: INTEGRATE adds one component onto another (for every entity that has both), FILL sets a whole component to a fixed value. One call instead of a loop over thousands of entities.
Für eine Handvoll unterschiedlicher Obje: For a handful of different objects (the player, one boss, a few menus) classes (chapter 20) are clearer. ECS shows its strength as soon as you have VERY MANY things of the same kind — projectiles, particles, swarms of enemies. Writing a game system as a bulk operation rather than a loop over classes is then the difference between a smooth thousand objects and stuttering. The two styles can be mixed in the same game.
Die letzten vier Module verbinden Drache: The last four modules join Drachenhauch to the physical world: reading data from a microcontroller (serial), addressing a controller you have built yourself (usb), managing the wireless network (wifi) or reading a Bluetooth sensor (bt). They are not meant for every game, but they open up exciting projects for the tinkerer — a game that reacts to a real button or a temperature sensor, say.
Diese vier Module sind im Standard-dhrt: These four modules are NOT in the standard dhrt. Call one of their functions and a clear message with the build instruction follows. You need a hardware build: python rust\build_runtime.py --hardware. Each module also has requirements of its own (drivers, platform), which are named below. The following examples are therefore not “printed off” against the runtime — they show the usage.
Fast alle Abfrage-Funktionen liefern hie: Nearly every query function here gives multi-line or comma-separated STRINGs (lists of devices or networks). You take them apart into an array with SPLIT (chapter 16) and go through the entries.
Serielle Kommunikation ist der Klassiker: Serial communication is the classic way of talking to an Arduino or ESP32: you open the COM port, send commands and read the readings sent, line by line. Every read command is safeguarded by a timeout (1 second by default).
PORTS listet die verfügbaren COM-Ports (: PORTS lists the COM ports available (comma-separated). OPEN opens a port at the baud rate (9600, say) and returns a SERIAL_HANDLE. CLOSE closes it.
WRITE schickt Text (gibt die Byte-Zahl z: WRITE sends text (returning the number of bytes). READLINE reads to the end of the line, READ up to n bytes. SERIAL_AVAILABLE tells you how many bytes are already waiting at the input — so that you read only when something is there.
Über USB-HID sprichst du Eingabegeräte a: Over USB HID you address input devices that announce themselves as a “human interface device”: macro pads, home-made controllers, programmer boards. You find a device by its vendor and product number (VID/PID) and then exchange raw packets of data.
LIST nennt alle HID-Geräte (mehrzeilig,: LIST names every HID device (multi-line, one vid:pid|product|manufacturer per line). OPEN opens one by VID/PID and returns a USB_HANDLE; PRODUCT and MANUFACTURER read the names in plain text.
WRITE sendet ein Datenpaket, READ liest: WRITE sends a packet of data, READ reads up to n bytes (with a time limit in milliseconds). The bytes are treated as characters — with ASC and CHR$ you convert them to numbers. CLOSE releases the device.
Das wifi-Modul steuert die WLAN-Verbindu: The wifi module steers the wireless connection through each operating system's own on-board tool, with no extra library at all: netsh on Windows, nmcli on Linux, networksetup/airport on macOS. You can scan for networks, ask after the current connection and signal strength, or connect with an SSID and password.
Der Windows-Pfad (netsh) ist der am läng: The Windows path (netsh) is the longest proven. The Linux and macOS backends are newer and have not yet been verified on real hardware — should there be trouble, a look at the error message is worthwhile: what netsh/nmcli/networksetup returns is mostly passed straight through.
AVAILABLE prüft, ob ein WLAN-Adapter da: AVAILABLE checks whether a wireless adapter is there. CURRENT gives the current SSID (empty = not connected), SIGNAL the strength 0..100. SCAN lists the networks within reach (multi-line ssid|signal, sorted by strength).
CONNECT legt ein Profil an und verbindet: CONNECT creates a profile and connects, DISCONNECT disconnects. PROFILES lists the networks stored, DELETE_PROFILE removes one.
Mit bt liest du BLE-Geräte aus: Pulsmess: With bt you read BLE devices: heart-rate monitors, thermometers, wearables, maker boards with a BLE chip. You scan for devices, connect by the address and then reach for “characteristics” — the individual data points a device offers through its services.
SCAN sucht für timeout_sek Sekunden und: SCAN searches for timeout_sek seconds and lists the devices found (addr|name|rssi). CONNECT connects by the address and returns a BT_HANDLE; IS_CONNECTED checks the state.
SERVICES listet die UUIDs der Dienste, C: SERVICES lists the services' UUIDs, CHARACTERISTICS the data points of one service. READ reads a characteristic's value (bytes as characters), WRITE writes one.
Mit dem serial-Modul redest du über ein: With the serial module you talk to the microcontroller over a text protocol you have thought up yourself — so you have to program on both sides. Firmata turns that around: you load the ready-made StandardFirmata sketch onto the board ONCE (in the Arduino IDE under File → Examples → Firmata), and after that you steer the pins directly from Drachenhauch. No sketch of your own, no tinkering with a protocol.
FIRMATA_PORTS listet die verfügbaren ser: FIRMATA_PORTS lists the serial ports available (the same as SERIAL_PORTS). StandardFirmata usually runs at 57600 baud.
Legt fest, was ein Pin tun soll. Die Mod: Lays down what a pin is to do. The mode values are the raw Firmata numbers: 0 = input, 1 = output, 2 = analogue input, 3 = PWM, 11 = input with an internal pull-up resistor.
An oder aus: schreiben schaltet den Pin,: On or off: writing switches the pin, reading gives its state as a BOOLEAN. A button with a pull-up gives FALSE when it is PRESSED (it pulls the pin down to ground) — which is confusing the first time.
ANALOG_WRITE gibt einen PWM-Wert (0–255): ANALOG_WRITE puts out a PWM value (0–255) — dimming an LED, regulating a motor; the pin must be in mode 3 for it. ANALOG_READ reads an analogue value (0–1023 on an Uno).
Schreiben und Lesen sprechen NICHT diese: Writing and reading do NOT speak the same number for the same pin: FIRMATA_PIN_MODE, DIGITAL_WRITE/READ and ANALOG_WRITE take the digital pin number (9, 13 …), FIRMATA_ANALOG_READ by contrast the analogue CHANNEL (A0 = 0, A1 = 1 …). That is a quirk of the Firmata protocol itself, not a Drachenhauch peculiarity. The analogue pin and channel are also limited to 0–15.
Muss einmal pro Frame aufgerufen werden: Must be called once a frame — only then are the pin states reported by the board read in. The same pattern as INPUT_UPDATE or TIMER_UPDATE: without UPDATE the read commands stay standing at their old value.
Firmata deckt Pin-Ein-/Ausgabe ab – Digi: Firmata covers pin input and output — digital, analogue and PWM. I2C sensors, servos, stepper motors and OneWire thermometers are not part of it; for those you still write a sketch of your own and talk to it over serial.
mqtt – Nachrichten mit dem IoT-Netz aust: mqtt — exchanging messages with the IoT network
MQTT ist das im Maker- und IoT-Bereich v: MQTT is the most widespread messaging protocol in the maker and IoT world: devices send messages to a “topic” on a broker, and whoever has subscribed to that topic receives them. With it you steer an ESP32 from inside your game — or, the other way about, let a sensor steer your game.
Verbindet sich mit einem Broker (öffentl: Connects to a broker (publicly test.mosquitto.org, say, or a Mosquitto of your own on the home network). The client_id$ must be unique on the broker.
PUBLISH schickt eine Nachricht an ein Th: PUBLISH sends a message to a topic; with behalten = TRUE the broker remembers it for receivers that join later. SUBSCRIBE subscribes to a topic — wildcards are allowed (+ for one level, # for everything below).
MQTT_UPDATE holt einmal pro Frame die ei: MQTT_UPDATE collects the messages that have arrived, once a frame (and keeps the connection alive in passing). You then fetch them one at a time: MQTT_NEXT_MESSAGE moves on to the next and gives FALSE when there are no more — the same cursor pattern as DB_NEXT in the database module.
Umgesetzt ist MQTT 3.1.1 mit QoS 0 – die: What is implemented is MQTT 3.1.1 with QoS 0 — the level practically every ESP32 example uses: messages are sent once, with no acknowledgement. Not included are QoS 1 and 2, last wills, and encrypted connections (TLS).
SERIAL_IS_OPEN prüft die Verbindung (ein: SERIAL_IS_OPEN checks the connection (otherwise you only notice an unplugged USB cable when you read). SERIAL_FLUSH pushes buffered data straight out, SERIAL_TIMEOUT lays down how long a read waits at most.
USB_OPEN_PATH öffnet ein Gerät über sein: USB_OPEN_PATH opens a device by its system path rather than by vendor and product number — needed when two identical devices are plugged in. USB_SERIAL gives the serial number, to tell them apart.
Hardware schickt selten fertigen Text, s: Hardware seldom sends finished text; it sends raw bytes — every position in the STRING received is a byte from 0 to 255. With ASC(s[i]) you get a byte's numeric value, with CHR$(n) you build one to send. Which bytes mean what stands in the device's data sheet (for standard BLE sensors, in the official GATT specification).
