Was eine Demo ist – und was sie zusammen: What a demo is — and what holds it together
In Teil IV hast du ein Spiel gebaut, in: In Part IV you built a game, in Part V you came to know one module after another. To close, something different: a demo. That is a program which does nothing but show off what the machine can do — a continuous piece of picture and music, scene by scene. The form has existed since the eighties; it is called the demoscene, and it has brought forth a good deal of what is taken for granted in games today.
Warum das als Abschlusskapitel taugt: Ei: Why that makes a good closing chapter: a demo forces you to master everything at once — time, sound, 2D, 3D, physics, shaders — and it forgives no sloppiness in the one thing that really matters: that picture and music belong together. That is exactly what this chapter is about.
Die Titelszene der mitgelieferten Demo:: The title scene of the demo supplied: plasma in the post effect, a sine scroller, and spectrum columns dancing to the real music.
Die vollständige Demo liegt als gbdemo/g: The complete demo comes with the book as gbdemo/gbdemo.dh. Do start it first and read on afterwards — what you have already seen is easier to understand. With the digit keys you jump into a scene, with A to K you play sounds, and M switches between eight pieces of public-domain music.
Die zwei Bausteine, die alles tragen: The two building blocks that carry everything
Fast jeder Anfänger baut die Bild-Musik-: Almost every beginner builds the coupling of picture and music the wrong way round: they count the seconds with a clock of their own and hope it fits the music. It never fits for long. As soon as the frame rate wavers — and it always wavers — the two clocks drift apart, and after two minutes the change of scene sits in the middle of the beat instead of on it.
Drachenhauch hat für beide Hälften des P: Drachenhauch has a command of its own for each half of the problem. Together they are the backbone of every demo:
Die Sekunde IM STÜCK, nicht seit Program: The second WITHIN THE PIECE, not since the program started. It comes from the playing itself — hang the running order on it and it cannot slip against the music at all.
Füllt ein dimensioniertes ARRAY OF FLOAT: Fills a dimensioned ARRAY OF FLOAT with the band levels of the sound BEING HEARD AT THAT MOMENT. Not of the notes in a file — of the finished mix, every effect included.
The array must have a size beforehand. AUDIO_FFT fills as many bands as will fit in — a DIM without a size reports an error.
Der Unterschied zwischen „ich rechne mir: The difference between “I compute something that looks roughly like music” and “I read what is sounding right now” is the whole difference between a nice animation and a demo. Everything that pulses in our demo pulses on those 32 numbers.
Das Gerüst: ein Ablaufplan aus Sekunden: The frame: a running order made of seconds
Eine Demo ist eine Liste von Szenen mit: A demo is a list of scenes with time marks. No more than that. The whole running order sits in a few constants and a chain of IFs — and because the time comes from the music, every cut sits where it should:
Szenen-Grenzen in Sekunden des Stücks: scene boundaries, in seconds of the piece
Jede Szene ist eine SUB, die genau ein B: Every scene is a SUB that draws exactly one frame. It remembers nothing across time — it looks at zeit and at the spectrum and paints the current picture out of them. That sounds strict, but it makes each scene understandable on its own and testable by itself.
Beim Entwickeln willst du nicht jedes Ma: While developing you do not want to wait four minutes every time for your scene to come round. Introduce a variable versatz and compute zeit = AUDIO_MUSIC_POSITION() + versatz. The digit keys 1–8 then jump straight into a scene by setting versatz to suit. It is built into the demo supplied — and it saved a great deal of time in the building.
Harte Schnitte wirken billig. Jede Szene: Hard cuts look cheap. Each scene therefore gets a value between 0 and 1 with which it fades up at the beginning and down at the end. The function for it is as small as it is unspectacular:
Die beiden Begrenzungs-Zeilen sind kein: Those two clamping lines are not decoration. Without them the value goes negative when it overruns — and if you multiply a colour by it, nonsense comes out. That very mistake was in the first version of the demo.
Vieles soll nicht dauernd wabern, sonder: A great deal should not billow away constantly but happen on the beat: a flash, a burst of particles, a thrown ball. For that you need beat detection. The principle is simple — bass clearly above its own average — but there is a trap in it that almost everyone builds once:
glatt[] hält Spitzen und fällt langsam: glatt[]  holds peaks and falls away slowly -> calm columns
roh ist das ungeglättete Bild diese: roh      is this instant's unsmoothed picture
Schlag = ROHER Bass über seinem gleitend: beat = RAW bass above its running mean, with a lock-out
Die Schlagerkennung muss auf den ROHEN W: The beat detection must sit on the RAW values. The trailing smoothing that makes the columns look calm irons out precisely the peaks that matter: in the first version of the demo the smoothed bass stood constantly at 0.90 against a mean of 0.75 — the condition “clearly above the mean” could never be true, and no ball ever flew. Keep the two apart: glatt[] for the picture, roh for the beat.
COOLDOWN aus dem timer-Modul ist hier ge: COOLDOWN from the timer module is exactly right here: it gives TRUE only when enough time has passed since the last TRUE. Without that lock-out the detection reports the same beat across several frames.
The last building block is the post effect. POSTFX sends the finished picture through a fragment shader before it lands on the screen — that is where the glow, the vignette, the plasma and the tunnel come about. Rather than loading a shader of its own for each scene, the demo takes a single one and switches it over through a uniform:
POSTFX bekommt das FERTIGE Bild. Einen H: POSTFX is given the FINISHED picture. The shader can therefore fade a background in only where the picture is dark — the demo draws its scenes on black, and the shader fills the dark places with plasma or tunnel. Fail to bear that in mind and you will wonder why your “background” lies over everything.
Wenn dein Shader die Nachbarpixel abtast: If your shader samples the neighbouring pixels — every glow does — then clamp the sampling points HALF a texel away from the edge. Clamping to 0..1 is not enough: exactly on the edge, the bilinear filtering mixes the last row with the first, and the bright content from the bottom edge bleeds back in at the top. In the demo that was to be seen as a row of colour scraps in the topmost row of pixels.
als Uhr nehmen – nie eine eigene mitzähl: as the clock — never count one of your own.
lesen und daraus Bass, Mitten und Höhen: and form the bass, middle and treble from it.
auf den rohen Werten, mit COOLDOWN als S: on the raw values, with COOLDOWN as the lock-out.
als SUBs, die aus zeit und Spektrum gena: as SUBs that paint exactly one frame out of zeit and the spectrum.
mit einem Shader für alles, umgeschaltet: with one shader for everything, switched over through a uniform.
Im nächsten Kapitel gehen wir die acht S: In the next chapter we go through the demo's eight scenes one at a time — each shows a different corner of the runtime.
Die acht Szenen – und was in jeder steck: The eight scenes — and what is in each
Jede Szene der Demo führt eine andere Ec: Every scene of the demo shows off a different corner of the runtime. Here is the heart of each one: the picture, the technique that decides it, and the stumbling block you fall over on the way. You can rebuild each on its own — the frame from the last chapter is enough for it.
Die Titelszene ist reine Zweidimensional: The title scene is purely two-dimensional and yet the best proof that everything hangs together: the columns are the spectrum, the logo grows on the beat, and the plasma background breathes with the bass. The sine scroller — text running through the picture as a wave — is as old as the demoscene itself, and built in six lines:
Die Höhe hängt an px, nicht an k – desha: The height hangs on px, not on k — which is why the wave stands still in space while the text runs through it. Were it to hang on k, the wave would travel along with the text and the effect would be gone.
Jeder Stern wird zweimal projiziert – vo: Every star is projected twice — before and now. The stretch between is the streak.
Sterne fliegen auf dich zu: Jeder hat ei: Stars fly towards you: each has a depth z that grows smaller, and is projected centrally — the nearer, the further out and the brighter. The trick for the warp effect is to project each star TWICE: at its position before this frame and at its present one. The stretch between is the streak, and the faster it goes (that is, the more bass), the longer it is.
LINES, PLOTS, BOXES und CIRCLES zeichnen: Without a count, LINES, PLOTS, BOXES and CIRCLES ALWAYS draw the whole array. Dimension a buffer to a fixed size and fill only part of it each frame, and the old values in the remaining places get drawn too — in the first version of the demo those were the day before yesterday's stars, standing about everywhere. Either you pass the count as the last argument, or you push the unused places out of the picture yourself (coordinate -10).
3 · Würfelfeld: 1600 Würfel, drei Draw-C: 3 · Cube field: 1600 cubes, three draw calls
Ein 40×40-Gitter aus Würfeln. Der Abstan: A 40×40 grid of cubes. The distance from the centre picks the frequency band — so the wave runs from the inside out, with the music.
Hier zeigt sich, wofür GPU-Instancing da: Here it shows what GPU instancing is for: 1600 cubes, each with its own position, height and rotation — and yet only three draw commands. MODEL_INSTANCED takes a whole array of matrices and sends it to the graphics card in one sweep.
pro Würfel: Position + Drehung in EINE M: per cube: position + rotation into ONE matrix
The fourth argument is a colour ARRAY. The runtime groups by it and issues one draw call per DIFFERENT colour — not per cube. So three colours for 1600 cubes are three calls. If you need 1600 different colours you will get 1600 calls too; for that, a gradient in the shader would be the better answer.
Der Abstand jedes Würfels zur Mitte wähl: Each cube's distance from the centre picks its frequency band: ring = INT(SQR(wx*wx + wz*wz) * 0.55) MOD 32. The wave thereby runs outwards from the middle as a ring — far more organic than if every cube took the same band.
Neun Kugeln, Rauheit von 0,03 (Spiegel –: Nine spheres, roughness from 0.03 (a mirror — you can see the landscape in it) to 0.85 (matt). The panorama is light and background at once.
Diese Szene packt die schwerste Artiller: This scene brings out the heaviest artillery: a real HDR panorama supplies the ambient light AND the visible background, each sphere has a material of its own, and the sun casts shadows.
dasselbe Panorama als Hintergrund: the same panorama as the background
Rauheit von spiegelnd bis matt über den: roughness spread around the ring from mirror to matt
Licht, Himmel, Schatten und Dunst sind G: Light, sky, shadows and haze are GLOBAL state. Switch them on in one scene and you must switch them off again when the scene changes — or the HDR sky will rise behind the next scene too. For that the demo has a SUB szene_start(n) that tidies up once at every change.
Der Boden muss zum Spiegelbild passen: The ground must match the reflection
Wer eine spiegelnde Kugel vor einen einf: Put a mirroring sphere in front of a single-coloured ground and you create a contradiction: in the sphere you see terrain, beneath it a field of colour. The demo's ground therefore carries a procedural texture (GENTEX_CELLULAR as a diffuse map) and runs out into the horizon with LIGHT_FOG. Note as you do: MESH_PLANE does NOT tile its texture — it is stretched once over the whole plane. Across 400 units of width it becomes a field of colour again; 130 units plus haze look right.
5 · Physik: ein Logo, das zusammenfällt: 5 · Physics: a logo that falls down
Das Logo steht aus Klötzen da, im Hinter: The logo stands there in blocks, and rubble rains in the background. Only what is actually hit gets hit: the B is still standing.
physics2d ist kein Kollisions-Werkzeugka: physics2d is not a toolkit for collisions but a real rigid-body solver (Rapier). Gravity, stacking, friction and bouncing are computed by the runtime; the demo only builds and watches. The letters stand as patterns in the source — a hash becomes a block:
aus dem Muster Klötze machen -- erst ein: make blocks out of the pattern -- STATIC to begin with
Das FALSE ist der Kern der Szene. Baut m: That FALSE is the heart of the scene. Build the letters movable straight away and the crossbar of the G falls down the moment the scene begins — you never see the logo. It therefore stands there statically and is only switched over when a ball really arrives:
beim Einschlag: nur DIESEN Buchstaben be: on impact: make only THIS letter movable
Zwei Fehler stecken hier dicht beieinand: Two mistakes lie close together here, and both look like physics errors while being errors of logic. First: switch over when the ball is FIRED rather than when it lands, and the logo falls half a second too early — it looks as though it were toppling of its own accord. Second: switch every block over at once and you also bring down the letter nobody touched. Remember for each block which letter it belongs to.
Der eigentliche Wow-Effekt dieser Szene: This scene's real moment of wonder is not the logo but the rain of rubble behind it: the same solver computes a few hundred further bodies in passing, which stack up into heaps on the ground. The drawing is done in two passes — the background first, then the logo — or the little blocks lay themselves over it.
6 · Tunnel: Schweife aus einem Render-Ta: 6 · Tunnel: trails out of a render target
Der Tunnel kommt aus dem Post-Effekt, de: The tunnel comes from the post effect, the ring from the spectrum — and the fading trails from a render target that stays standing.
Der Tunnel selbst ist Shader-Arbeit: ein: The tunnel itself is shader work: a 1/r mapping, the classic demo tunnel. In front of it lies a ring whose radius comes band by band out of the spectrum — the music as a shape. What is interesting is how the trails come about:
TRUE = der Inhalt bleibt über das Bild h: TRUE = the content stays standing beyond the frame
Ein Render-Target wird normalerweise vor: A render target is normally emptied before every frame. With TRUE it stays standing — which is the prerequisite for trails. The fading is done NOT by drawing itself (a target cannot draw itself) but by multiplying with a dark grey.
Ein Spektrum-Ring braucht ein GESPIEGELT: A spectrum ring needs a MIRRORED spectrum. Lay the bands simply the whole way round and band 31 (treble, small) and band 0 (bass, large) butt straight up against one another — a jump of over 150 pixels between two neighbouring points, out of which the Catmull-Rom curve makes a spike shooting far outwards. Let the spectrum run up one half and mirrored back down again.
7 · Klangfarben: die Effektkette bei der: 7 · Timbres: the effect chain at work
Ein Tiefpass fährt herunter – und die re: A low-pass travels downwards — and the columns on the right really do disappear, because they are the real spectrum BEHIND the effect chain.
Die einzige Szene, in der die Demo den K: The only scene in which the demo touches the sound. It goes through the effect chain in six stages: a low-pass sweep, wobble (an LFO on the filter), echo, reverb, distortion and auto-pan.
Wobble: ein LFO fährt den Filter -- auf: wobble: an LFO drives the filter -- on the AUDIO thread
Der Punkt daran: Nach dem Setzen rechnet: The point of it: after the setting, the program computes nothing further. The audio layer drives the modulators and effects itself, sample-exact — so a filter sweep runs on unperturbed even when the frame rate collapses.
Der Beweis steht im Bild: The proof stands in the picture
Weil die Säulen das echte Spektrum hinte: Because the columns show the real spectrum behind the chain, you can see the filter working. Measured on the demo: the sum of the upper twelve bands falls from 0.79 (at a 7200 Hz cutoff) to 0.13 (at 460 Hz), while the bass stays unchanged at 3.8 to 5.6. A factor of six — that is no animation, that is the filter.
Effekte hängen am Bus und bleiben hängen: Effects hang on the bus and stay hanging. Fail to set them back to neutral on leaving the scene and you send the rest of the demo through the distortion.
Ein Drahtgitter-Ring, der Abspann – und: A wireframe ring, the credits — and a dot showing the source of the sound: the ping travels audibly around you.
Zum Ausklang etwas Ruhiges – und ein let: Something calm to close on — and one last trick that can only be understood with loudspeakers. The ping in the credits really does circle the listener: the runtime computes the panning and the fall-off with distance itself, the program only sets the position.
Ohr im Ursprung, Quelle kreist in 6 Mete: ear at the origin, the source circles 6 metres away
jedes Bild: Quelle weiterdrehen, ab und: every frame: turn the source on, strike it now and then
Der leuchtende Punkt auf dem Bild zeigt: The glowing dot in the picture only shows where the sound stands at that moment. Without that label the finest effect goes unnoticed — and that is a general lesson: what one does not see, one takes not to exist.
Quer durch alle Szenen liegt noch etwas:: One more thing lies across every scene: eight sounds on the keys A to K, playable at any moment. Not one of them is a file — each is ONE line:
Wellenform, Frequenz, Slide, Attack, Sus: waveform, frequency, slide, attack, sustain, decay,
Vibrato-Tiefe, Vibrato-Tempo, Lautstärke: vibrato depth, vibrato speed, volume [, SID extensions]
Die letzten Argumente sind die SID-Erwei: The last arguments are the SID extensions: pulse width, pulse-width modulation and a resonant filter sweep. With them the character of the old home-computer sound chips can be rebuilt — the laser above is a sawtooth whose filter rushes down from 5000 Hz in 140 milliseconds.
Eine Demo ist die ehrlichste Prüfung für: A demo is the most honest examination a runtime can face: it cannot be passed with a pretty still. Everything has to run at once, mesh together and listen to the music. Once you have worked through this chapter you know not only the commands — you know how to put them together into something that is more than the sum of its parts.
Der Quelltext der Demo liegt vollständig: The demo's source comes with the book in full (gbdemo/gbdemo.dh) and is commented throughout — especially at the places where something went wrong in the building. Change the scene boundaries, swap the piece of music, append a ninth scene. That is exactly how the demoscene has always worked.
Ins Netz stellen – Drachenhauch im Brows: Putting it on the net — Drachenhauch in the browser
Ein fertiges Spiel liegt auf deiner Fest: A finished game lies on your hard disc. Whoever is to see it must download it, unpack it, contradict a warning from Windows and then hope it starts. Between your work and a viewer, in other words, lie five opportunities to give up.
Es geht auch anders: Dieselbe Laufzeit,: There is another way: the same runtime that runs on the machine exists as WebAssembly. A link is enough — the browser loads it, compiles your source itself and runs it. No plug-in, no Python, no installation. This chapter shows how that is done, and what is different in the browser from on the machine.
Der Playground im Browser: links der Que: The playground in the browser: the source on the left, the running program on the right. The lighting and PBR in the picture come from the same runtime as on the machine — the browser compiles the source itself.
Zwei Befehle. Der erste baut die Laufzei: Two commands. The first builds the runtime for the browser and packs your program in with it, the second puts up a small server:
Danach im Browser http://localhost:8000: Then open http://localhost:8000 in the browser. The build takes some minutes and needs the emscripten toolchain; the result is three files in the web folder: dhrt.js, dhrt.wasm and — should your program need files — dhrt.data.
Ein Doppelklick auf die index.html funkt: Double-clicking index.html does NOT work. WebAssembly may not be loaded over file://; it needs real HTTP. That is exactly what the second command is for — it is not decoration.
Die .dh-Datei, die du beim Bauen angibst: The .dh file you name when building has two tasks: it is the program the demo button starts, and its assets folder is packed in with it. Only those files are available in the browser — a LOADIMAGE of anything else finds nothing.
Die Seite ist mehr als ein Abspielgerät:: The page is more than a player: on the left stands an editor, on the right the canvas and beneath it the output. Type, click Run, watch. Every run starts a fresh runtime — a program that has crashed leaves no heap of shards for the next.
laden je ein fertiges Programm und start: each load a finished program and start it: plasma, starflight, 3D with lighting, physics, spectrum.

Zum Veröffentlichen kopierst du den Ordn: To publish, you copy the web folder somewhere files are served from — GitHub Pages, web space, a network drive. It is purely static; there is nothing that would have to run on a server.
Was im Browser anders ist: What is different in the browser
Der Browser ist kein Betriebssystem, und: The browser is not an operating system, and that shows in a few places. None of them is a fault in your program — but not knowing them means a long search:
Ton bleibt still, bis geklickt wird: The sound stays silent until something is clicked
Browser erlauben Klang erst nach einer N: Browsers allow sound only after an action by the user (otherwise every advertising page would make a din)
Einen Startbildschirm zeigen: „Klicken z: Show a start screen: “Click to start”
Leinwand wird nach Programmende schwarz: The canvas goes black when the program ends
Der Zeichenpuffer wird nach dem Anzeigen: The drawing buffer is discarded after being shown
Nichts – während des Laufs ist alles zu: Nothing — during the run everything is to be seen. SAVESCREENSHOT does give an empty picture in the browser, though
Es gibt kein Dateisystem des Nutzers: There is no file system belonging to the user
Spielstände über das save-Modul statt üb: Saved games through the save module rather than through dialogues
Serial/USB/Bluetooth/WLAN und Datenbank: Serial/USB/Bluetooth/wireless and the database are missing
Diese Module sprechen mit Geräten des Re: These modules talk to the machine's devices
Solche Programme laufen weiter nur auf d: Such programs go on running only on the machine
Eine Schleife OHNE FLIP friert den Tab e: A loop WITHOUT FLIP freezes the tab. On the machine a program simply computes away to itself; in the browser the page only gets air again when you finish a frame. So FLIP there is not only “show the picture” but also “make way for a moment”. If you compute for a long time, sprinkle FLIPs through it.
Auf einem Telefon gibt es keine Tastatur: On a telephone there is no keyboard and there are no mouse buttons. TOUCH_COUNT, TOUCH_X and TOUCH_Y give the fingers, GESTURE$ the gesture recognised. A game that can be steered with one finger reaches many times the audience — and mostly costs only a few lines.
Auf dem Rechner ist es gleich, ob dein O: On the machine it makes no difference whether your assets folder holds five or fifty megabytes. In the browser every visitor downloads everything before the first picture appears — and waits while they do. A few figures for scale: the runtime itself is around 9 MB, a tracker module with four minutes of music about 260 KB, a PNG texture 20 to 500 KB depending on size.
Daraus folgt eine Faustregel, die im Net: From that follows a rule of thumb that weighs more heavily on the net than on the machine: what can be computed should not travel along as a file. An AUDIO_SFX sound is one line instead of a WAV file, GENTEX_PERLIN creates a texture instead of loading one, and a tracker module sounds for four minutes at a fraction of the size of an MP3.
Genau so ist die mitgelieferte Demo geba: That is exactly how the demo supplied is built — six minutes of picture and sound, and apart from the music and one font it loads nothing. Everything else comes about as it runs.

über einen Link, der den Quelltext selbs: through a link that contains the source itself.

Schritt für Schritt zur Ursache: Step by step to the cause
Wenn du eine Meldung nicht sofort verste: If you do not understand a message straight away: (1) go to the line named. (2) Read which command or variable is meant. (3) Check its values — an extra PRINT directly before it often helps, to see what is really in there. (4) For commands, look the expected arguments up in Appendix A. Most errors are clear after those four steps.
